title: Oh, Turns Out I’m the Vicious Concubine Villainess
author: Yun Tuzi
synopsis:
[Beautiful and Doted Concubine + Reborn Ruthless Tyrant + Redemption and Sweet Pampering + Both Pure]

Emperor Jianwu, Xie Pei, in his past life, trapped himself in the dogma of a sage and virtuous ruler, striving to be a noble and enlightened emperor, only to end up abandoned by all, losing his throne, and being poisoned into a cripple.

At his most desperate moment, only the so-called vicious and domineering concubine, whom all the civil and military officials spoke of, remained loyal to him, even taking an arrow for him and dying.

Xie Pei was heartbroken, and after rebirth, he abandoned personal morals and integrity, resorting to any means necessary to achieve his goals.

Only the moonlight in his heart, he cherishes her in every way, hoping she can have a happy and fulfilling life this time.

Ming Xi had transmigrated, her father was the illustrious Marquis of Wuding, her brother was the brilliant and talented Young General, and also a sister-control freak. She had lived to sixteen without experiencing the slightest hardship in life.

In the 22nd year of Jinghe, the emperor suddenly issued a decree, bestowing her as a concubine to the Crown Prince, who had just come of age.

Ming Xi had long known that with her status, she could at least marry into a great clan as a principal wife, but she would still have to deal with the struggles of the inner court.

Since she had to fight anyway, she might as well fight in the most noble place in the world, perhaps even securing the respected position of Empress Dowager, wielding great power and overlooking the land.

Just as Ming Xi prepared eighteen strategies to win over the Crown Prince, she turned to find that the Crown Prince, as radiant as the moon, was acting strangely, very strangely.

Before she could even do anything, the Crown Prince was clinging to her like a possessive ghost, obedient and showering her with endless affection.

Ming Xi silently wondered, could it be that transmigration always comes with true love?

Was she actually the sweet and pampered female lead?

Not long after, Ming Xi discovered that she was merely the vicious concubine side character.

And her Crown Prince, who was not quite normal, was the main villain.

This was absurd!

chapters.title: The Ridiculous Banquet
chapters.content:
"Outrageous! Shameless!"

From the southeast corner pavilion of the Princess's mansion garden, vague and lewd sounds could be heard.

The nobles present listened to this scandalous performance in broad daylight, their expressions a mix of shock and fascination.

The old matriarch of the State of Rites, covering her heart, shouted sternly.

However, since it wasn't her own residence, she couldn't take it upon herself to deal with the adulterers inside.

"Ah, where is Miss Ming?"

A girl's exclamation caused a thousand ripples.

Ming Xi, the legitimate eldest daughter of the Marquis of Wuding?

Wasn't she the one the emperor had recently bestowed as a concubine to the Crown Prince?

Could it be...

The old matriarch frowned and turned her head.

Which family's girl was this who spoke out of turn?

Had she left her brain in her mother's womb?

How dare she say such things!

Lin Huairou seemed to stammer nervously, "It was my little maid who said that Miss Ming had been avoiding people and sneaking towards the garden earlier, but now she's nowhere to be seen..."

The old matriarch coldly interrupted her, "Enough! Do you have the right to speak here? How did your elders raise you?"

The future Crown Prince's concubine having an affair with someone, even if it were true, they had to pretend they didn't know.

Who would dare to publicly place the green hat on the Crown Prince's head in front of everyone?

Did they think the royal family found them too pleasing to the eye, or did they want the Crown Prince to, after ascending the throne, kill them one by one according to the list of those present today?

Lin Huairou, scolded, lowered her head and bit her lip, hiding the malice and schadenfreude in her eyes.

Her ninth brother said that as long as Ming Xi and the Marquis of Wuding's family were removed, the position of the next Grand Preceptor would be securely her grandfather's.

At that time, not only would she be a mere concubine, but even the position of Crown Princess would be hers.

Lin Huairou was so excited she almost laughed out loud, wishing she could rush in and catch them in the act.

"Who can tell me what's going on here?"

Everyone was startled and turned to see Princess Huayang leading a group of servants, approaching in a grand procession.

As for the Miss Ming mentioned by Lin Huairou, who should have been one of the main characters in the pavilion's scandalous affair, was standing gracefully beside the princess.

In the cold autumn frost, the wind blew her skirt and sash, making the girl with raven hair and fair skin appear as if she were a fairy. Her water-like eyes, filled with a faint smile, looked at Lin Huairou without a trace of mockery, yet more mocking than any words.

Lin Huairou's face changed. Impossible!

She had personally locked Ming Xi and the stupid, fat son of Marquis Jian'an in the pavilion.

How could...

Then who was in the pavilion now?

Actually, if everyone listened carefully, they would notice that the intense and lewd sounds did not include any female voices.

"Greetings to Princess Huayang."

Lin Huairou stiffly followed the crowd in bowing, a strong sense of foreboding rising in her heart.

Princess Huayang ignored them and ordered sternly, "Kick open the door for me."

Two guards complied, kicking the door open with one foot.

Two naked bodies were exposed to everyone's eyes.

"Jue Ge'er!"

"You beast, Zheng Yaozu, let go of my ninth brother!"

Lin Huairou screamed in horror and rushed in without regard.

"...Isn't that the heir of Marquis Jian'an and the legitimate grandson of the Lin family? What kind of relationship do they have?"

The habit of homosexuality has existed since ancient times, and it's not uncommon among the powerful, but these two seem to have taken it too far, right?

Moreover, wasn't it said that the two families intended to form a marriage alliance?

So, it turns out that Young Master Zheng was interested not in the Lin family's daughter, but in their son!

Princess Huayang's face was terrifyingly dark. "Hurry up and separate these two shameless fools!"

"Jue Ge'er! Jue Ge'er! Call for a doctor, quick!"

Lin Huairou held her dying younger brother, screaming at the top of her lungs.

She suddenly looked towards the girl standing among the flowers.

Ming Xi had not spoken a single word since her appearance, nor had she confronted Lin Huairou.

But Lin Huairou felt as if she had fallen into an abyss.

Meeting her resentful gaze, Ming Xi smiled softly, a smile more intoxicating than the garden full of flowers.

It was you!

How dare you, you vile woman!

Lin Huairou was furious.

She would definitely tear Ming Xi apart.

Suddenly, Lin Jue spat out a large mouthful of blood, convulsed a few times, and then stopped breathing.

"Jue Ge'er!"

Lin Huairou collapsed to the ground.

She was finished!

...

"Miss Ming, please."

The chrysanthemum appreciation banquet had turned into such a ridiculous affair. Even though Princess Huayang was furious, she had to maintain order and wait for the heads of the Jian'an Marquis and Lin family to arrive and sort things out.

But this had nothing to do with Ming Xi.

She had originally intended to leave, but just as she was about to ask for permission to depart, the princess ordered her maid to invite her to the study.

Ming Xi was surprised and couldn't guess what the princess had in mind.

Princess Huayang was not like Lin Huairou, that foolish girl with bubbles for brains. She wouldn't do anything to her in her own residence.

The light purple skirt swept over the threshold as Ming Xi stepped into the study.

The leading maid did not follow her in and even extended her hand to close the door.

Ming Xi turned to look at the tightly closed door. Her face showed no sign of alarm, but the sleeve arrow hidden in her hand was ready to be launched.

The layout of the study was clear at a glance, except for the sound of boiling water coming from behind the Suzhou embroidery screen on the left.

She spoke up, "Who is inside?"

"It's just me. I only wanted you to have a cup of tea."

A man's gentle and smiling voice responded.

Hmm? "Me"?

Ming Xi was surprised and bowed, "Greetings to Your Highness, the Crown Prince."

"Don't kneel."

A pair of large hands steadily supported her arms.

The white wide sleeves were luxurious, and the man's hands were cold, white, slender, and with distinct knuckles.

Ming Xi secretly admired them for a moment but was puzzled as to why the Crown Prince was here.

Wasn't it said that his relationship with Princess Huayang, his royal aunt, was very bad?

Recently, the emperor had issued a decree, bestowing two concubines and four good wives to the Crown Prince.

But Princess Huayang's chrysanthemum appreciation banquet had only invited Ming Xi.

It wasn't that the princess was deliberately trying to set Ming Xi up for failure, but everyone in the capital knew that she and the Crown Prince were at odds, yet she had a good relationship with the Marquis of Wuding's family.

It was because, years ago, Princess Huayang had married into the Uze country for the stability of the Great Zhou, struggling in that barbaric land for many years.

Until the Marquis of Wuding led the army to a great victory over the Uze iron cavalry at Yuchuan Pass, reclaiming Weizhou, which had been occupied by foreign tribes for hundreds of years.

Later, the Marquis of Wuding's heir, Ming Jing, emerged as a prodigy, and together with his father, they launched several joint attacks on the Uze army, forcing them to negotiate and send Princess Huayang back to the court.

Princess Huayang was very grateful to the Marquis of Wuding and his son for this. After returning to the capital, she often used the emperor's guilt to help them in the court, freeing them from the emperor's suspicions.

She also held a special fondness for Ming Xi and took good care of her.

So, no one would have expected the Crown Prince to appear in Princess Huayang's study to meet his future concubine.

Could it be a pre-marital inspection?

But she was a concubine, not the Crown Princess.

Did the Crown Prince find it necessary?

After she stood firm, Xie Pei let go of her hands.

Seeing that she kept her eyes downcast and avoided his gaze, Xie Pei's Adam's apple slightly rolled, restraining the impulse to touch her.

It seemed he had still scared her.

....................

(Note: The male lead has been pure in both his past and present lives. Ming Xi has been the same person to the male lead in both lives, but she only has memories of the modern world and this life. Given the male lead's crazy devotion, he would never mistake his beloved woman for someone else. There is no such thing as loving the wrong person or mistaking identities, nor any stand-ins. This won't be written. Also, the male lead is very unscrupulous towards everyone except the female lead, extremely unscrupulous.)

chapters.title: All Very Strange
chapters.content:
Behind the folding screen, separated by a desk, Ming Xi and the Crown Prince sat facing each other.

She watched as the Crown Prince, rumored to be noble and dignified, personally brewed tea with fluid, graceful movements, truly a feast for the eyes.

Ming Xi’s mind raced, but she simply couldn’t fathom the Crown Prince’s intentions.

Having grown up in the capital for fifteen years, born into a marquis’s household, with an especially accomplished father and brother, she had always had a seat at imperial banquets. Naturally, she had seen Crown Prince Xie Pei before.

Ming Xi’s beauty and talent might not be unparalleled in the world, but she was certainly among the most outstanding.

Wherever she appeared, she drew countless gazes, including, of course, those of the Crown Prince before her.

But that was all it ever was: a ruler’s detached appreciation of beauty. Nothing more.

So, apart from this sudden imperial decree of marriage, Ming Xi truly couldn’t think of any other connection between herself and the Crown Prince.

Why would he go to such lengths to secretly meet her on Princess Huayang’s territory?

Xie Pei placed a cup of tea in front of her and said gently, “You must have been startled today.”

Ming Xi: “?”

Wasn’t *he* the one who was startled?

She glanced at the Crown Prince, with his jade-like face and temperate demeanor, and felt a headache coming on. She really couldn’t decipher the meaning behind his words!

In the past, at imperial banquets, the Crown Prince had never been terrifying, but he had never been warm or approachable either.

Noble and distant, with the imposing bearing of a ruler, no one dared act presumptuously in his presence.

Now, what political purpose was the Crown Prince trying to achieve through her?

Or was he planning to make a move on the military power held by her father and brother?

Could he already be so impatient to overthrow his own father and seize the throne?

But the Crown Prince didn’t seem like a fool. There was no need for him to destroy his own defenses and leave himself open to eternal infamy, was there?

Ming Xi picked up the teacup and took a sip to steady her nerves before slowly replying:

“Thank you for your concern, Your Highness. It’s just that I never expected Lord Zheng and Young Master Lin to have that kind of relationship. I had even heard that their families were preparing to form a marriage alliance. Who could have imagined such a scandal would occur?”

Marquis Jian’an was a distinguished military general, the Commander of the Five Armies Camp, and deeply trusted by the Emperor.

Chancellor Lin, on the other hand, held great prestige in the Grand Secretariat and was one of the leading figures of the Donglin faction.

If the two families were to form a marriage alliance, the influence of the civil official faction over the Three Capital Camps would only grow stronger.

With the Grand Secretariat’s power reaching the heavens and their arrogance unchecked, they posed a significant constraint on imperial authority. For the Crown Prince, the future emperor, this was far from ideal.

But now, forget about a marriage alliance, after such a disgraceful incident, the two families would likely become sworn enemies.

The Eastern Palace could take this perfect opportunity to suppress the Grand Secretariat and consolidate the military power of the capital camps.

Ming Xi was already destined to marry into the Eastern Palace. The more stable and powerful the Crown Prince’s position, the better it would be for her.

Of course, Ming Xi wasn’t foolish enough to take credit for this.

Men, especially those in power, would never appreciate a woman at their side who was scheming.

Even if today, she had only been defending herself.

But others, upon learning of it, would never understand her. They would only criticize her for being ruthless and venomous.

“They say Young Master Lin has been frail since childhood. He really shouldn’t have been so reckless. Earlier, when I saw him coughing up blood, I wonder how he is now?”

The girl’s gentle brows and eyes showed concern and sighs.

Xie Pei didn’t detect Ming Xi’s probing; he only thought she genuinely cared about Lin Jun.

*He deserved it?*

The Crown Prince’s hand holding the teacup paused, a flicker of rage flashing in his eyes, but he didn’t let the girl across from him notice.

Not wanting her to think he was cruel, Xie Pei said gently, “The Imperial Princess has summoned the imperial physicians. You needn’t worry.”

And then?

Ming Xi sat upright, waiting for the Crown Prince’s next words.

But Xie Pei simply pushed a plate of lotus flower mung bean cakes toward her, diverting her attention.

“This is the specialty pastry of the Imperial Princess’s kitchen. Would you like to try some?”

Ming Xi: “...”

Was this really the time for pastries?

Was he hiding his tail *that* deep?

So, just how grand were this Crown Prince’s ambitions?

To go to such lengths, feigning tenderness to win over his own concubine?

Xie Pei, under her gaze, slightly curled his fingers. “What’s wrong?”

Ming Xi, feeling the weight of the situation, picked up a jade chopstick and took a piece of mung bean cake.

Forget it, forget it. She wouldn’t guess anymore, her brain was about to overheat.

Anyway, in the eyes of the world, she was already the Crown Prince’s woman.

His schemes were likely the usual ones. She would just have to counter them as they came.

The room fell silent, the air filled with a touch of awkwardness.

Xie Pei didn’t dare to keep his gaze on her for too long, afraid she might notice something. He coughed lightly, covering his mouth with his fist, and suddenly asked, “What do you think about the imperial marriage decree?”

Huh?

Ming Xi blinked. The Emperor had bestowed the marriage, what was there for her to think?

She pondered for a moment before flattering this future master of hers, “This humble woman is overwhelmed with joy?”

Xie Pei: “...”

Originally, he had wanted to apologize to her. The position of a concubine was indeed beneath her.

But with the current unclear situation in the palace and court, with undercurrents surging, the position of Crown Princess would only make her a target for everyone...

In the end, it was his own weakness and his inability to control his private desire to keep her by his side as soon as possible.

Xie Pei always felt deep guilt and tread carefully around her.

But he never expected that she would be so happy about their marriage.

The Crown Prince’s ears, hidden beneath his hair, turned red.

So she had already developed feelings for him this early?

Xie Pei couldn’t help but take her soft, warm hand in his, then quickly let go, not wanting to take liberties. His cold and aloof brows softened like a spring breeze.

“Don’t be afraid, and don’t worry about anything. I will protect you.”

...

Men’s words were just words.

Ming Xi didn’t stay long in the study. She had someone inform Princess Huayang before leaving the princess’s residence directly.

It wasn’t that she was being rude; Princess Huayang was genuinely busy at the moment.

In the end, Lin Jun couldn’t be saved and died in the midst of that scandalous affair.

Chancellor Lin was so grief-stricken that he coughed up blood, and the Lin family, in a frenzy, stormed the Marquis Jian’an’s residence, demanding justice.

But Marquis Jian’an was no pushover. Wasn’t his son, Yaozu, the only heir of the marquis’s household?

Though he hadn’t died, the imperial physician’s diagnosis was that he would never be able to... perform his marital duties again. He might as well go and join the eunuchs in the palace.

The marquis’s household was in chaos.

The two families were locked in a life-and-death struggle at the princess’s residence.

The most unfortunate Princess Huayang was so furious she laughed.

She had been hosting a fine chrysanthemum-viewing banquet, and now it was ruined. And they still dared to bring their misfortune to her doorstep?

In a fit of rage, Princess Huayang overturned a table and went straight to the palace to lodge a complaint with her older brother, the Emperor.

Ming Xi felt a slight pang of guilt.

Just a few days ago, her elder brother had sent another batch of antiques and famous paintings for her to enjoy, all of which had been looted from the Uze Kingdom during their invasion of the Central Plains.

When she returned home, she would carefully select a few valuable items to send to Princess Huayang as a gift to apologize.

The princess loved spoils of war from the Uze Kingdom the most, it would surely delight her.

In the carriage, Tingyu hesitated before finally lowering her voice to ask, “Miss, Lady Lin tried to harm you, so why did you strike back at Young Master Lin instead?”

At the banquet, a maid had “accidentally” spilled wine on Ming Xi’s skirt, and she had known something was amiss.

Whether or not she had a persecution complex, she never hesitated to assume the worst in people.

And sure enough, it was the same old trick, drugging and framing her for adultery.

Even though the scheme was old, it was always effective in ruining a woman.

Ming Xi looked up, her red lips curling slightly. “Because Lin Huairou was just a pawn. The one truly targeting me was Lin Jun.”

“I refuse to stoop to the same level to take revenge on a woman.”

But then again, there was no problem with doing the same to a man.

Besides, shouldn’t the mastermind be the one to suffer the consequences?

Tingyu’s eyes widened in confusion. “Has Young Master Lin gone mad?”

Tingyu and her sister, Tingruo, were not ordinary maids. They were elite assassins personally trained by the Marquis’s heir, Ming Jing, to be Ming Xi’s shadow guards.

Tingyu was meticulous, brave, and resourceful, while Tingruo was fiercely loyal and would protect Miss Ming Xi to the death, no matter the circumstances.

The two sisters were Ming Xi’s confidantes, so they were well aware of the deep-seated feud between the Wu Ding Marquis’s household and the Lin family.

Years ago, when Chancellor Lin failed to win over the Marquis, he had schemed during the battle at Weizhou City, replacing the military provisions with sand. He had also instigated the Emperor to send a supervising censor to stir trouble, nearly leading to the downfall of the Marquis, the heir, and tens of thousands of the Tian Ding Army.

Over the years, Ming Xi had been pulling strings behind the scenes, causing the Lin family to suffer many setbacks.

Secretly, the two families had reached a point of mutual destruction.

But even if Lin Jun hated Ming Xi and the Wu Ding Marquis’s household, why would he resort to such a foolish and crude scheme?

The imperial family wasn’t stupid. If the future concubine of the Eastern Palace was publicly caught in an adulterous act, the Emperor and the Crown Prince would surely investigate the truth.

This was a case of losing a thousand troops to kill eight hundred of their own, wasn’t that self-destructive?

In truth, Ming Xi was even more puzzled than Tingyu.

Lin Jun might have been physically weak, but his ambition was anything but.

His grandfather’s rise in the Grand Secretariat was largely due to Lin Jun’s secret counsel.

Even the scheme years ago to sabotage her father, brother, and the Tian Ding Army had been his idea.

For someone so young to be this malicious, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to call him the Zhao Kingdom’s Jia Xu.

Such a deeply scheming person, even if he wanted to eliminate the Wu Ding Marquis’s household, would surely wait until he had secured military power.

Why would he pull off such a low-level, idiotic scheme today, only for her to easily counter and make him suffer the consequences?

After all these years, Ming Xi had tried every means to kill Lin Jun but had never succeeded.

Yet today, he had so conveniently fallen into her hands.

There was joy, yes, but Ming Xi was more wary and disbelief.

And yet, Lin Jun had indeed been played to death by Zheng Yaozu.

Ming Xi thought of something and ordered Tingyu to continue closely monitoring the Lin family’s movements.

Though it was highly unlikely that Lin Jun had pulled off some kind of golden cicada shell escape.

Moreover, Ming Xi thought of the Crown Prince who had appeared at the princess’s residence.

If His Highness had a hand in this, then it wouldn’t be surprising that Lin Jun had been backfired.

But based on what Ming Xi knew of the Crown Prince before, he would never stoop to such underhanded methods to eliminate an enemy.

At the thought of the Crown Prince’s strange behavior toward her earlier, Ming Xi even suspected that he might have been possessed by someone else.

“And I don’t know where the Lin family obtained such a bizarre drug, to make someone behave like a beast...”

In the end, one was dead, and the other was ruined.

Tingyu didn’t even dare imagine what would have happened if Miss Ming Xi had truly fallen for the trap.

Hearing this, Tingruo lifted her head and said hatefully, “Miss, you should have let this servant snap Lin Huairou’s neck.”

Was it enough to only have Lin Jun dead?

Ming Xi held her hand warmer, a light laugh escaping her lips. She looked as pure and elegant as the precious Yaotai Jade Phoenix in the princess’s residence, untouched by vulgarity.

“Killing someone is messy to handle afterward. Besides, from the looks of it, Lin Huairou’s fate will be far worse than death.”

chapters.title: Reborn and Transmigrated Again
chapters.content:
In the Estate of the Duke of En, the maternal home of Empress Xiao.

"Useless! Useless! All of you are useless!"

The most favored eighteenth young lady of the Xiao family furiously overturned her dressing table and, still not satisfied, kicked the maid beside her several times.

The maid did not dare to dodge, only kowtowing and begging for mercy.

"Vile servant, what are you shouting about? Do you want to tarnish my reputation?"

Xiao Mingzhu kicked even harder. "Someone, this vile servant is guilty of insubordination. Sell her to a brothel!"

After the maid was gagged and taken away, Xiao Mingzhu was still not satisfied.

Though young, she was a beauty, but her twisted, malicious expression ruined her delicate features.

And, whether it was an illusion or not, her smooth, jade-like skin seemed to be turning dull and sallow.

Xiao Mingzhu collapsed in despair. "System, in the original book, Lin Jun was clearly a major supporting male character. Why did he suddenly die?"

And he died from playing with men!

Xiao Mingzhu still didn’t know when things had started to spiral out of control.

At first, it was the originally smooth-sailing Prince Qi who was caned and imprisoned by the Emperor, and the female lead Su Qing'er’s family was seized and sent to the Teaching and Entertainment Office.

That was fine. Xiao Mingzhu was happy to watch the female lead suffer.

If the male lead was a bit miserable, that was also fine, it would make it easier for her to pursue him.

But before she could enjoy it for long, the plot continued to spiral like a runaway horse.

The Crown Prince Xie Pei had not married any wives or concubines before ascending the throne, but now he had side consorts and good concubines.

Today was even more absurd. The most powerful strategist by the male lead’s side, the future Chief Councilor, the extremely popular sickly supporting male character in the original book, had died before even making his debut.

Was this reasonable?

Xiao Mingzhu felt that either the world had gone mad, or the system was toying with her.

Could it be the butterfly effect caused by her transmigration?

[Detecting that the host’s task ‘Seize the fortune of the vicious and bewitching concubine Ming Xi’ has failed. Due to the host’s current debt, the reward ‘skin like congealed fat’ is being repossessed to offset the interest. Please try harder to complete the task. Three failures will result in an electric shock punishment, and ten failures will lead to annihilation!]

The system’s cold, mechanical voice shattered her sense of superiority.

Xiao Mingzhu couldn’t believe it and covered her face, shouting, "Is this because I didn’t try hard enough?"

She had spent two months pursuing Lin Jun, even emptying her points to buy a "Lovesick Gu" to turn Lin Jun into an obedient lapdog.

Xiao Mingzhu had thought she finally had a sharp blade in hand, and defeating a vicious female supporting character would be easy.

And to successfully complete the task, she had even reluctantly borrowed high-interest loans from the system to buy the most potent aphrodisiac to give to Lin Jun to destroy that vicious bewitching concubine.

But what was the result?

Xiao Mingzhu didn’t think there was anything wrong with her plan. It must be...

"In the original book, Lin Jun was described as so formidable, but it turns out he’s useless. I asked him to scheme against the vicious female supporting character, and he went and played with men instead?"

All her time and points were wasted.

[…]

Could it be that Lin Jun was schemed against in return?

The system was truly speechless. From the beginning, it had advised her to just let Lin Jun deal with Ming Xi himself.

But she had insisted on being clever, demanding that Lin Jun follow her plan exactly.

Now look, she had lost the chicken and the corn.

And she still had the nerve to blame others?

[Ding, Main Task: Pursue the male lead, Prince Qi Xie Yi. Current goodwill: 50 (The male lead pays special attention to the host but has not reached the level of liking). Must be completed before the male lead ascends the throne.]

[Ding, Due to the host’s failure in the previous task, the second main task is forcibly activated: Pursue the great villain, Crown Prince Xie Pei, make him fall in love with you, then betray him to help the male lead ascend the throne. Current goodwill: -50 (The great villain intensely despises the host and harbors strong murderous intent). Must be completed within one year.]

Before Xiao Mingzhu could be shocked by the system forcing another main task on her, she was stunned by Xie Pei’s negative goodwill.

Wait, goodwill could be negative?

And -50 at that!

Was the system malfunctioning?

[System detection normal. Please reflect on yourself, host.]

Xiao Mingzhu: "..."

F*ck!

---

Lin Jun’s death didn’t just shatter Xiao Mingzhu’s resolve.

In the estate of the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief in the capital, Shi Yue, the second legitimate daughter of the Shi family, was one of the four good concubines selected by the Emperor for the Crown Prince.

"You said what? Lin Jun is dead?"

Shi Yue was so shocked she stood up.

That was the future "Qilin Son" of the Lin family, the future Chief Councilor who would stir up the court!

In her past life, Prince Qi had imprisoned Emperor Jianwu, controlled the capital, and nearly succeeded in usurping the throne, with Lin Jun playing a pivotal role.

How could such a deep and ambitious man die like this?

And in such a disgraceful manner.

Why was everything different from her past life?

Shi Yue’s face turned pale, and she broke out in a cold sweat.

First, the Emperor had decreed her as a good concubine for the Crown Prince.

But she clearly remembered that in her past life, she had been selected in the imperial examination after the Crown Prince ascended the throne!

Perhaps all women in the world wanted to marry the young and promising Crown Prince, but that certainly did not include Shi Yue after her rebirth.

In her past life, the Emperor was cold and ruthless, Noble Consort Ming was domineering, Consort Xiao was vicious, Su Qing’er was a sanctimonious Mary Sue, and the harem was in constant strife. She had been tormented to the point of unbearable suffering.

After Prince Qi forced his way into the palace, she was thrown into the cold palace and tormented to death.

These days, Shi Yue had been filled with resentment, feeling that the Crown Prince was a lingering ghost who refused to let her go.

Now, another thunderbolt, the future Lin Chief Councilor, who could overturn the world, was dead!!!

Shi Yue couldn’t help but doubt whether her rebirth was just a nightmare.

Or was it because of her rebirth that things in this life had changed?

If so, did she still have the advantage?

Shi Yue bit her lip, feeling extremely unwilling.

Was her rebirth just to repeat the tragedy of her past life and continue to be at the mercy of others?

No, she refused to accept her fate. Even if she entered the palace, she would not be as passive and non-competitive as in her past life, only wanting the Emperor’s love.

Noble Consort Ming, Consort Xiao, and Su Qing’er, she would not let any of them off.

As for the future Emperor, the current Crown Prince?

Shi Yue sneered. If he was as ruthless as in her past life, then he couldn’t blame her for throwing herself into Prince Qi’s arms and collaborating with him to pull him off the throne earlier.

---

Late at night, the Zhonghua Hall in the Eastern Palace was pitch black and silent.

The tightly closed window was suddenly blown open by a gust of wind.

The icy wind blew the curtains by the bed like waves.

The wind howled, bone-chillingly cold, yet Crown Prince Xie Pei, on the bed, was drenched in sweat, trapped in a nightmare he couldn’t wake from.

"Ming Xi! Just because you are the most favored in the harem, do you think the Emperor truly loves you?"

"Do you know why you miscarried years ago and became infertile for life? It was your beloved Emperor, who stood by you through life and death, who conspired with the Empress Dowagers of the East and West Palaces to poison you!"

"And do you know why the Emperor favors you? Isn’t it because your father and brother control the most elite Tian Ding Army of the Great Zhou? Once the Emperor is done using them, he will kill the donkey after it has served its purpose, destroy the Wu Ding Marquis’s estate, and grant you a white silk to hang yourself!"

"Don’t believe me? Look at this secret letter. It’s the Emperor’s order to the Brocade Guards. When the Uze Kingdom was destroyed and the army returned, your father was assassinated, wasn’t that the work of your beloved Emperor?"

"How can you still foolishly love your father’s murderer, clinging to a useless man for three years? Hahaha, it’s laughable."

"Ming Xi, Ming Xi, what’s the use of your lifetime of pride? In the end, you’re just a joke."

"You should actually thank His Highness, the Prince Regent. If it weren’t for him forcing his way into the palace, your brother would have been killed by the Emperor long ago. How could he have raised an army to rebel and besiege the capital?"

"Be sensible and go persuade your brother to surrender and support the Prince Regent’s ascension to the throne. Otherwise..."

In the dead of winter, the once most luxurious Nine Curved Pond in the palace was now desolate. The once most beautiful and wanton Noble Consort Ming, now in coarse clothes, weakly collapsed to the ground, almost shattered.

And the once ruler of the Great Zhou Dynasty was now a helpless cripple, his tendons severed, his throat poisoned mute.

He clumsily fell off the bed, desperately trying to crawl toward that despairing woman, his eyes bloodshot, his mouth open to explain, but no sound came out.

He didn’t! He didn’t!

Xi’er...

But no matter how much he begged in his heart, Ming Xi never turned back to look at him again.

Until a cold arrow came from nowhere.

The originally arrogant Xiao Mingzhu screamed in panic, ordering someone to catch the assassin.

The world fell silent. Xie Pei stared blankly at the woman who had shielded him. The cold arrow pierced her heart, and blood stained her clothes.

He wanted to reach out to help her cover the wound, wanted to shout for a physician to save her, but he couldn’t do anything. Helpless, he could only watch as she died.

chapters.title: The Crown Prince’s Madness
chapters.content:
"Xi’er!"

Xie Pei jolted awake, his face as pale as a ghost, his heart aching with each beat, nearly suffocating.

The cold wind howled outside, but he couldn’t distinguish between dream and reality.

"Your Highness, Your Highness!"

Eunuch Yu, the Crown Prince’s personal attendant, bent over and carefully pushed open the door. As expected, he saw His Highness in nothing but his sleeping robes, his eyes bloodshot, holding a sword that hummed with terrifying murderous intent.

Eunuch Yu immediately knelt down, and before the sword could strike, he hastily said:

"Your Highness, you saw Miss Ming today. Miss Ming is fine, nothing happened to her... In twenty days, you will welcome Miss Ming into the Eastern Palace!"

The rampant murderous aura around Xie Pei solidified. The world-destroying pain and despair in his eyes faded, and his mind gradually cleared.

He stared at Eunuch Yu with a cold, terrifying gaze for a long time, but his voice was gentle. "Do you know?"

Know what?

Eunuch Yu’s head was covered in cold sweat. He didn’t dare to speak, afraid that one wrong word would get him split in half by His Highness on the spot.

Xie Pei smiled, overjoyed. "Xi’er said she would marry me. She was very happy."

Eunuch Yu: "..."

No matter how speechless he was, he still had to flatter. "Your Highness and the future Empress are deeply in love. After marriage, you will live in harmony and happiness, a perfect match for a hundred years, growing old together."

These words greatly pleased Xie Pei.

He held the sword and sat on the bed with a commanding presence, letting the cold wind blow on his thin sleeping robes.

"Has Lin Jun’s body been moved?"

"In response to Your Highness, there was a fire at the Lin residence tonight. The remains of the Ninth Young Master Lin were destroyed in the fire. The Five City Military Police and the Jingzhao Prefect can both testify. No one will discover that the body was switched."

Xie Pei nodded. "Tell Miao Yunpan to dig thoroughly. I want the results by tomorrow."

Eunuch Yu agreed and added, "Your Highness, the informant from the Duke of En’s estate reported that the eighteenth young lady of the Xiao family had a violent outburst today and even sold her maid to a brothel."

At the mention of Xiao Mingzhu, murderous intent surged in Xie Pei’s eyes again.

He coldly laughed. "Bring her secretly to the Dark Hall. You know what to do."

Let Xiao Mingzhu’s dog bite her. Whether he would use this piece in the future or not, it was better to have it ready.

Eunuch Yu: "Your Highness, rest assured."

Xie Pei waved his hand, dismissing him.

Eunuch Yu saw that His Highness continued to sit in the cold wind, seemingly indifferent to his own life or death. He could only anxiously advise:

"Your Highness, your marriage to Miss Ming is imminent. Please take care of your health."

Xie Pei looked at him indifferently. After a moment, he said, "Go close the window."

Eunuch Yu hurriedly smiled and went to close the window.

Indeed, Miss Ming was now the cure for His Highness.

But he didn’t understand why His Highness had suddenly come to cherish her so much.

Not just Miss Ming.

Two months ago, the Crown Prince was assassinated on his way back from famine relief in Jiangnan. After waking from his coma, his temperament...

In front of the Emperor, the Empress, and the civil and military officials, he was still the filial, respectful, dignified, and capable Crown Prince. But only those who served him closely knew that His Highness had changed.

The original Crown Prince was both literary and martial, skilled in governance, diligent in politics, loved by the people, and kind-hearted, almost the perfect heir.

He was just a bit too sentimental, whether it was toward his stepmother Empress Xiao, his birth mother Consort Su Lan, or his younger brother Prince Qi.

No matter what trouble they caused, even if he didn’t approve, he would selflessly clean up their messes.

Eunuch Yu and the Eastern Palace officials had subtly reminded His Highness that there was no familial love in the royal family. His Highness’s constant indulgence would only nurture their ambitions and lead to endless future troubles.

But His Highness didn’t like to hear such words, and no matter how worried they were, they could do nothing.

All of this had suddenly changed two months ago.

His Highness inexplicably took an interest in the eldest legitimate daughter of the Wu Ding Marquis’s estate. He even secretly sent his own death soldiers to protect her, inquiring about her every move several times a day, as if he wanted to keep her in his pocket.

A few months ago, during the floods in Jiangnan, the relief silver was embezzled, with half going into Prince Qi’s pockets. His Highness had nearly emptied his own private funds to make up for it, working tirelessly to stabilize the situation and settle the people.

According to His Highness’s original character, as long as Prince Qi begged him a little, His Highness would never bear to turn him in. He would only privately punish him and then go to great lengths to protect him.

However, this time, after returning to the capital, His Highness had remained silent, letting Prince Qi think his actions had gone unnoticed.

At the same time, His Highness not only sent people to secretly protect the son of the Zhenzhou Prefect, who had been forced to travel to the capital to petition the Emperor, but also fanned the flames so that the whole world knew Prince Qi had embezzled the relief funds, causing hundreds of thousands of people to become homeless and destitute, a heinous crime.

In the end, even though the Su family had taken the blame for Prince Qi, he was still caned and imprisoned by the Emperor, his reputation ruined.

Eunuch Yu had long disliked Prince Qi. On the surface, he was respectful to His Highness, but in reality... Hmph!

He deserved it. The Eastern Palace’s confidants were happy to see it.

But His Highness’s sudden change was truly...

Confucius said, "The gentleman does not speak of strange forces or violence." Eunuch Yu didn’t dare to think too much about why His Highness’s character had changed so drastically.

The bedchamber returned to silence. Xie Pei lay on the bed, still wide awake, unable to sleep.

He hadn’t ascended the throne yet. There was still an Emperor above him, watching. He couldn’t act recklessly to kill those enemies.

Xi’er... Very soon, very soon, she would become his wife again.

Don’t rush, don’t rush.

The blood in his palm reminded Xie Pei to stay awake, to not go mad and run to kidnap her and hide her away.

He couldn’t let her be dragged down and suffer as she had in her past life, withering away so early.

In this life, no one could harm her. No one.

chapters.title: A Warning
chapters.content:
The scandal involving the Lin family and the Ji'an Marquis's estate had stirred up a storm in the capital, with one stone causing a thousand ripples.

Undercurrents surged in the imperial court, and the power struggle among various factions was like a smokeless battlefield, with invisible hands manipulating the reshuffling of power.

Of course, none of this was something Ming Xi could involve herself in for the time being.

She was merely a young lady in the boudoir preparing for her marriage.

However, the Wu Ding Marquis's estate didn’t seem very peaceful either.

"Eldest Young Lady, this concubine truly doesn’t dare! Please, let Young Master return!"

In the elegant boudoir, Ming Xi, dressed in a light apricot ruqun, sat on a luohan bed, her fair fingers flipping through a book, the tips of her fingers glowing with a soft pink luster.

"What is wrong with Concubine Sun? Brother Hao is only going to Weizhou with the steward delivering winter supplies. Why are you acting as if I’ve driven him out of the marquis’s estate? It truly saddens and confuses me."

The young lady’s helpless sigh made Concubine Sun, who was wailing as if the sky had fallen, seem even more unreasonable.

Concubine Sun, who had been covering her face and weeping, froze, her heart filled with hatred.

This damned girl loved to pretend!

Just a trip to Weizhou?

There was a war going on there!

The Uze Kingdom had been peaceful for less than two years when the old Khan passed away. The new Khan, eager to prove himself, had set his sights on the Central Plains, repeatedly sending troops to probe their defenses.

As a result, the border was once again engulfed in flames of war.

Of course, Concubine Sun couldn’t do anything about these national affairs. As long as the Marquis and the heir didn’t lose the war, all she cared about was...

"But Brother Hao is only thirteen! He’s the precious young master of the estate!"

Did it fall to him to deliver winter supplies to the Marquis and the heir at the front lines?

This damned girl was clearly using Brother Hao to threaten and warn her!

Previously, when the imperial envoy came to the marquis’s estate to deliver the decree, it was announced that Ming Xi, the legitimate eldest daughter of the Wu Ding Marquis, was to be bestowed as a consort to the Crown Prince.

Concubine Sun was, of course, extremely jealous, but even more so, she was so overjoyed she could have jumped for joy.

Finally, this strange little demoness was going to be married off!

From then on, the entire marquis’s estate would be hers!

But before she could even lift her tail in triumph, her son had been tricked by Ming Xi into going to the border, falling into the hands of the heir, Ming Jing, that black-hearted tiger with a smiling face.

With her dim-witted son, Ming Jing could manipulate him as easily as playing with a cuju ball.

And what if those heartless siblings quietly arranged for her precious Hao to die in Weizhou?

The thought made Concubine Sun feel as if the sky had collapsed. She cried even more pitifully, and her knees buckled as she tried to kneel before Ming Xi.

But before her knees could touch the ground, she felt her arms being gripped firmly by Ling Ruo, who held her steady.

Concubine Sun: ...

How could this skinny little servant have the strength of an ox?

Ming Xi closed her book and looked at her with a faint smile, "Although Concubine Sun is only a concubine of my father, she is still my elder. If you kneel before me, do you want me to lose years off my life?"

Concubine Sun trembled, "How would this concubine dare? Eldest Young Lady, Weizhou is a dangerous and freezing place. Brother Hao is still just a child..."

Ming Xi said indifferently, "The dangerous and freezing place you speak of is where my father, my brother, and countless soldiers of Great Zhou are currently fighting, shedding blood to defend our nation. Brother Hao comes from a military family and should take his father and brother as role models, striving to strengthen himself and serve the country, rather than becoming a decadent and useless young master who indulges in luxury."

Concubine Sun gritted her teeth. She sure could make it sound noble, but how much of it was sincere?

Ming Xi seemed to see through her thoughts and found it amusing.

"Brother Hao is also Father’s son, my and my brother’s younger brother. Concubine Sun need not be so suspicious. For this trip to Weizhou, a hundred estate guards will accompany him for protection, and my brother will also send his personal guards to meet him."

"Concubine Sun, do you know that spoiling a child is as good as killing him? Next month, I will enter the Eastern Palace. When I am not here, who in the estate can control that little tyrant, Brother Hao?"

"He is thirteen, not three. Do you really want him to become an uneducated, bullying good-for-nothing?"

"Do you not know the fate of the Ji'an Marquis’s heir?"

Zheng Yaozu’s current predicament was entirely of his own making.

If he hadn’t been lustful and set his sights on Lin Huairou, crying and begging to marry her, Lin Huairou wouldn’t have used him to scheme against Ming Xi and escape the marriage.

Ming Xi had seen Zheng Yaozu snatch women off the streets and kill innocent commoners multiple times.

Such a tumor of a person, merely crippling his means of harm was already letting him off easy.

If her own younger brother ever became like Zheng Yaozu, Ming Xi would not hesitate to break all three of his legs.

Ming Xi looked into Concubine Sun’s eyes. "In the future, when I am in the royal family, the more outstanding my brothers are, the safer I will be. If Brother Hao turns out to be useless, he will only bring disaster and provoke the Emperor’s wrath... Concubine Sun, would you like to calculate first how many heads the nine clans of our Wu Ding Marquis’s estate have?"

Concubine Sun left Qinghua Courtyard in a daze.

It was deep autumn, yet her back was almost soaked with cold sweat.

Concubine Sun was truly unwilling to accept this!

The Madame was a useless waste. Why couldn’t she replace her and make Hao the legitimate son?

But she also knew that unless Ming Xi and her brother were completely ruined, she would have to continue living as the Madame’s servant without the Madame’s authority.

The bitterness in Concubine Sun’s mouth was unbearable.

For so many years, she had never once gained even the slightest advantage over Ming Xi.

That damned girl had been uncanny since she was a child. Whether it was the late Old Madame or the Marquis, they all seemed to have their eyes clouded.

They always treated her as if she were a fragile and delicate young lady, firmly believing she was the kindest and most innocent girl in the world.

Kind and innocent, my foot!

What kind and innocent young lady would, at the age of eight or nine, shamelessly push a maid into a well right in front of her, then softly order the servants to seal that well?

Even though that maid was a spy sent by the Wu Ding Marquis’s enemies, only there to poison and seduce, to ruin the heir’s future...

In any case, Concubine Sun would never forget that day.

The cute little girl, as pure as jade, tilted her head at her, the feathered flower in her hair swaying with the cold wind, like a heavenly maiden beside Guanyin.

Who could have imagined that a life had just been extinguished by her hands.

She hadn’t felt any cuteness, only sheer terror.

That girl was a natural-born demon!

And then there was the chrysanthemum banquet hosted by Princess Huayang a few days ago. No one suspected that the incident involving the ninth young master of the Lin family and the Ji'an Marquis’s heir had anything to do with Ming Xi.

But Concubine Sun swore that if this wasn’t Ming Xi’s doing, she would kneel and call her ancestor.

Just look at all these years, who among those who had offended her had ever come to a good end?

That little demoness was like a plague, bringing ruin wherever she went.

It was truly terrifying!

Suddenly, Concubine Sun thought of the other consorts and noble ladies who would enter the Eastern Palace with Ming Xi.

Heh, if those women dared to think that Ming Xi was a weak and easily bullied beauty, they would probably be devoured by her without even a bone left to bury.

Concubine Sun schadenfreude sighed. After all, it wasn’t fair that only she had to suffer at Ming Xi’s hands!

Meanwhile, Xiao Mingzhu, who had gone to the palace to ask Empress Dowager to make things difficult for Xie Pei, and Shi Yuan, who was at home pondering her past life memories, both inexplicably sneezed.

chapters.title: Favorability Drops Again
chapters.content:
Inside the room, watching Sun Concubine flee in disarray, Tingyu couldn’t help but laugh.

"Miss, Sun Concubine probably won’t dare have any more schemes."

Ming Xi took a sip of tea, moistening her throat, not really concerned about this trivial matter.

Sun Concubine had been "shaped" by her for so many years, controlling her was too easy.

"Is my mother still chanting sutras in the Buddhist hall?"

"...Yes. Madam said she hopes her sincerity will move Buddha to bless you with a turn of fortune from misfortune."

Tingyu didn’t dare repeat the original words. Just thinking about them made her neck feel chilly.

Madam actually believed that her daughter becoming the Crown Prince’s concubine was a disaster sent from heaven, ruining her life forever.

In Madam’s eyes, the true essence of a woman’s happiness was seeking priceless treasures with ease and finding a loving partner, being with one person for a lifetime.

Even if the Crown Prince’s concubine had a rank and was recorded in the imperial genealogy, in Madam’s view, she would still be nothing more than a lowly concubine.

Having to share a man with so many other women, wasn’t that a pit of fire?

If it were her, she’d rather die.

Tingyu just... found it absolutely absurd!

But then again, Madam being absurd wasn’t news.

Back then, she had been so consumed by her love for the Marquis that the entire Marquis’s mansion was in chaos, and she even lost her composure at a palace banquet, nearly ruining the Marquis’s career.

The Dowager Marchioness, unable to tolerate it any longer, forced the Marquis to take the clever Sun Concubine as a concubine.

Since the Marquis didn’t object and even consummated the marriage with Sun Concubine, Madam had tried to kill herself, even attempting to flee with her five-year-old son and not-yet-one-year-old daughter.

Fortunately, the young World Prince was precocious. Knowing his mother was recklessly endangering his and his sister’s lives, he quickly sent someone to notify the Dowager Marchioness and the Marquis, preventing irreversible consequences.

Unable to escape, Madam had since resented the World Prince, refusing to see him and constantly declaring she had no such ungrateful, selfish son...

With such an infuriating mother dragging them down, if it weren’t for the World Prince and the young lady’s intelligence in firmly securing the Dowager Marchioness’s favor and suppressing Sun Concubine, neither of the two young masters would have survived to adulthood.

Seeing Tingyu’s expression of helplessness, Ming Xi found it amusing. She wanted to say that her mother’s little quirks were nothing.

Tingyu was just overreacting, she hadn’t seen Ming Xi’s birth mother from her past life.

Now *that* was a true piece of work.

Strictly speaking, Ming Xi could also be considered a native of this world.

In her past life, Ming Xi was born into a wealthy family, but her father didn’t dote on her, her mother didn’t love her, and she was frail and sickly.

That terrible pair of parents had wished every day for her early death to make room for their illegitimate children.

But Ming Xi wasn’t one to suffer losses. She could give up things herself, but she wouldn’t let others take them from her.

It had taken Ming Xi over twenty years, dragging her half-useless body, to eliminate all her "siblings," outmaneuver her cheap parents, donate all their family assets to charity, and then die with a flourish.

When she groggily regained consciousness, she had become the fetus in the belly of the Marchioness of Wuding in the Great Zhou Dynasty.

Compared to her terrible past life, Ming Xi’s start in this life was as good as it could get, noble birth, good health.

The Marquis of Wuding was a century-old aristocratic family. Her father, the Marquis, was a war hero highly favored by the Emperor.

Though he was a bit chauvinistic, blindly loyal, filial, and rough around the edges, he was still responsible toward his children.

The Dowager in the inner mansion was stern but not cruel. Even though she despised her daughter-in-law, she never took it out on her grandchildren, treating Ming Xi and her elder brother with considerable affection.

As for her somewhat abnormal, love-obsessed mother, Lady Wen... it wasn’t a big problem.

These years, Lady Wen had been led by Ming Xi to focus on vegetarian meals and chanting sutras, mourning her lost love, and had basically stopped causing trouble.

Ming Xi wasn’t without trying to "drain the water" from Lady Wen’s brain to make her more sensible.

Not just her, even the Dowager had tried to educate her daughter-in-law.

But love-brain disease was simply incurable, worse than the terminal illness from her past life. No amount of effort would help.

"Have the servants in the small Buddhist hall keep a close watch on my mother. Don’t let any rumors spread."

The room fell silent. Ming Xi leaned against the soft cushion, and once again, she couldn’t help but think of the Crown Prince.

She still couldn’t figure out his strange attitude toward her at the Princess’s mansion.

Based on her years of observation, research, and understanding of Crown Prince Xie Pei, Ming Xi had always thought he would wait until he ascended the throne before selecting consorts at the request of his officials.

She didn’t expect to enter the palace so soon.

The Emperor’s bestowal of marriage had indeed disrupted her plans a bit.

But it was no big deal.

Ming Xi had always been clear: given her background, the worst she could do was marry into a noble family as the principal wife.

In her view, powerful men were all the same. Seeking true love and a lifelong partner was just asking for trouble, self-inflicted suffering.

A counterexample? Her mother, Lady Wen.

Ancient or modern, power and money in one’s own hands were a woman’s true security.

So why not fight wherever she was?

Instead of fighting in the inner courts of the nobility, why not challenge the pinnacle of imperial power?

Ming Xi would never mistreat herself. No matter where she was, no matter her status or circumstances, she would ensure she lived well, even the best.

So what if she was a concubine of the Crown Prince?

So what if she had to share a man with five other women?

Ming Xi wasn’t entering the palace for love. The Crown Prince was less her husband and more her leading superior.

What she wanted was to establish herself in the harem, to step by step gain the power and influence she desired through him.

The position of Empress was just a small goal. The respected position of Empress Dowager, wielding great power and influence, wasn’t impossible to strive for.

Ming Xi’s fair fingers played with the jade pendant hanging from her waist, a faint, serene smile on her red lips.

Actually, no matter what the Crown Prince was planning, as long as he was willing to focus his energy on her, it was her opportunity.

Once she married into the Eastern Palace, after spending more time with him, she would surely find a way to grasp the Crown Prince’s true intentions.

...

Xie Pei had just finished court when he was stopped by an inner attendant from Jingren Palace.

"Your Highness, Her Majesty the Empress requests your presence."

Xie Pei turned the jade thumb ring on his hand. "Let’s go."

The news that Xiao Mingzhu had entered the palace early in the morning to stir up trouble in the Empress’s quarters, sowing discord between mother and son, had already been delivered to him by Jingren Palace’s spies.

Xiao Mingzhu was never not cunning or venomous.

Unfortunately, she was the Empress’s own niece, so she couldn’t be killed just yet.

But there were always ways to make life more painful than death.

"Your subject greets Mother Empress."

In Jingren Palace, the Empress, seated high on the phoenix throne, looked at the Crown Prince, who respectfully paid his respects, and put on a sour face.

They said that as children grew, they no longer obeyed their parents. And the Crown Prince wasn’t even her biological son, there was that extra layer of separation.

Mingzhu had said the Crown Prince only had eyes for his birth mother and felt no affection for her or the Enguo Duke’s family.

For example, this time, the Crown Prince knew full well that she intended for her niece to become his Crown Princess, yet he deliberately accepted the Emperor’s decree to marry a concubine, ruining her plans.

Sure enough, the Crown Prince was displeased that she, as his mother, had delayed his marriage and his chance for heirs.

But didn’t he realize? She had done it all for him. Apart from the Xiao family’s daughters, which noble lady in the capital would truly care for him?

He was ungrateful. After all these years of her doting and raising him, this was how he repaid her.

"Crown Prince, you’ve really grown. I thought you had forgotten the way to Jingren Palace."

"Your subject is filled with fear. To have caused Mother Empress such heartache with my filial impiety is my great shame."

Seeing the Crown Prince sincerely apologizing, the Empress’s expression softened slightly.

Xie Pei suddenly covered his mouth and coughed.

"Is the Crown Prince’s injury still not healed?"

The moment the words left her mouth, the Empress felt embarrassed.

Hadn’t she just scolded him for not coming to pay his respects, knowing full well he was injured?

The heir’s health was a matter of national importance, how could it be compared to mere formalities?

If word got out, the censors would surely criticize her for being an unkind mother.

"Mother Empress need not worry. Your subject is fine. The day before yesterday, Sister Hongxiu came to deliver tonic soup and mentioned that Mother Empress has been coughing in the mornings. I asked the imperial physician, who said it was due to autumn dryness, so I had some autumn pear paste prepared to soothe your lungs."

Xie Pei perfectly played the role of the filially pious elder son, considerately giving the Empress a way out.

Eunuch Yu, head bowed, presented the autumn pear paste that the Crown Prince had "personally" prepared.

The Empress wasn’t truly trying to break ties with the Crown Prince. The Crown Prince was outstanding, and the Eastern Palace’s position was secure. She had neither the time nor the ability to raise another prince in his place.

Now that she had a way out, the Empress immediately took it. "The Crown Prince is thoughtful."

Enough, enough. The Great Zhou governed the world with filial piety. No matter what schemes the Crown Prince had in his heart, she was his adoptive and official mother.

He had to be filial and obedient to her for life, never defying her, unless he wanted to be spat on by the world and leave a stain on the history books.

The Empress could only sigh inwardly. If only she had given birth to her own son.

"Late autumn brings frost. You’ve just recovered from your injury, so take good care of your health. Many things can be left to subordinates. Don’t insist on doing everything yourself."

"Your subject understands."

The Crown Prince and the Empress began exchanging polite concerns, the mother-son affection on full display.

The tension in Jingren Palace dissipated, replaced by a warm and harmonious atmosphere.

Xiao Mingzhu, however, almost couldn’t maintain her expression.

She had come today intending to use the Empress to teach Xie Pei a lesson. Once mother and son started arguing, she would step in to mediate with gentle kindness, surely making Xie Pei develop favorable feelings for her.

But she had predicted the beginning, not the process or the outcome.

Her aunt, the Empress, was useless, soothed by Xie Pei with just a few words.

Xiao Mingzhu grumbled in frustration.

[The Great Villainess’s favorability has dropped by another 10 points. Current: -60. If favorability drops below -100, the host’s mission fails and punishment will be administered!]

Xiao Mingzhu: "..."

Xiao Mingzhu almost jumped up.

What had she done?

Why had Xie Pei’s favorability toward her dropped again?

Was this damn Crown Prince’s brain really broken?

Fine. Very well, Xie Pei, is it?

You’ve successfully caught my attention.

The colder and more indifferent he was toward her, the more Xiao Mingzhu was determined to make him fall in love with her, only to cruelly abandon and trample on him.

Suddenly, like a butterfly, Xiao Mingzhu fluttered in front of Xie Pei, her still baby-fat face beautiful and innocent.

"Mingzhu greets Crown Prince cousin."

Xie Pei glanced at the affected Xiao Mingzhu, as if only just noticing her existence. "Cousin, no need for such formalities."

Xiao Mingzhu’s smile was lively as she sat down beside him, convinced that a feudal old man like Xie Pei couldn’t resist a pure and charming girl like her.

But soon, Xiao Mingzhu couldn’t smile anymore.

Because Xie Pei’s favorability kept dropping: -1, -1, -1...

Xiao Mingzhu’s defenses crumbled. She really broke.

She wanted to point at the Crown Prince’s nose and curse him as an ingrate, to have the Empress petition the Emperor to depose him! Depose him!

But unfortunately, Xiao Mingzhu didn’t have the courage yet.

But she was *so* angry!

Xie Pei indeed had to exert great effort to restrain his murderous intent to avoid snapping Xiao Mingzhu’s neck on the spot.

In the previous life, if not for her, Xian wouldn’t have died with resentment.

Xie Pei knew that the true culprit behind Xian’s death was his own incompetence, but that didn’t mean Xiao Mingzhu didn’t deserve to die.

chapters.title: Madam, Please Stop Making a Scene
chapters.content:
Half a month before the grand wedding, the palace sent cultivation matrons to instruct the consorts, including Xiangyuan, on palace etiquette. At the same time, they used secret palace methods to condition their bodies.

The goal was to nurture them as tender as tofu to please His Royal Highness, the Crown Prince, while also ensuring their bodies were in the optimal state for conception, to secure the royal bloodline.

"Miss, your skin is truly finer than snow and more lustrous than jade."

In the steamy bedchamber, Ming Xi, wearing only a white undershirt, bit her lip and smiled coyly. "Auntie, you're teasing me again."

Auntie Qin was combing her hair with a fine-toothed comb. The girl's black hair cascaded like a waterfall, glossy and soft, exuding a subtle fragrance that was simply irresistible.

"I have served so many nobles, but I have never seen a flawless beauty like you, Miss."

With her stunning looks, fair and delicate skin, and an otherworldly elegance like a valley orchid, every part of her was perfect without a single flaw.

No wonder His Royal Highness the Crown Prince was so infatuated with her. He had repeatedly instructed them to take good care of her and not to restrict or trouble her with any rules or formalities.

"Miss, Madam is making a scene and wants to see you."

Tingyu quickly entered and whispered in Ming Xi's ear.

The smile on Ming Xi's lips faded slightly. She didn't ask Tingyu what had happened but signaled Tingru to help her dress.

"Auntie, there's something going on with my mother. I need to go see her."

"Today's conditioning is over. Miss, you may go attend to your business."

Ming Xi nodded to the two cultivation matrons and, accompanied by Tingru and Tingyu, hurried to the small Buddhist hall.

"How dare you! When did you servants gain the right to pull and tug at me, a Marquess's wife?"

"What? Can't I even move freely in my own home? The Marquess hasn't divorced me yet!"

The night was deep, but the small Buddhist hall was as lively as a marketplace.

Sun Yiniang and the servants couldn't stop Madam Wen at all.

"Madam, can you please stop making a scene?"

Sun Yiniang was on the verge of a breakdown.

The palace people were currently staying at the residence. Madam Wen didn't care about making a fool of the Wuding Marquess's household in front of the entire capital, but Sun Yiniang did!

Whether it was the blame from the palace nobles or Ming Xi, that little vixen, thinking she managed the Marquess's household poorly and punishing her, Sun Yiniang couldn't bear either.

Damn it, she shouldn't have been tempted by the glory and wealth of the Wuding Marquess's household all those years ago and entered as a concubine.

Over the years, she hadn't enjoyed any blessings. She had only been a workhorse for the Marquess's household, toiling without reward.

"Sun Yingqiu, you, a mere concubine, dare to lecture me, the legitimate madam? That's right, Ming Chonglun has heartlessly betrayed me. Now he finally wants to favor the concubine and abandon the wife, doesn't he? Isn't he afraid of being impeached by the censor?"

Madam Wen pointed at Sun Yiniang's nose, cursing both her and the Marquess of Wuding.

Sun Yiniang: "...Forget it, just let it all collapse!"

"Mother."

Accompanied by Tingru and Tingyu holding a lamp, Ming Xi, dressed in a moon-white wide-sleeved gown, hurried over.

Sun Yiniang looked at the girl, who seemed like a celestial being under the moonlight, but her face turned pale. She hastily waved her hands. "It's not my fault. I didn't start this."

Ming Xi glanced at her. "Auntie, you go back and rest first."

Sun Yiniang saw that she indeed didn't intend to blame her, so she heaved a sigh of relief and immediately left with her maids.

"Sun Yingqiu! You stand still for this madam!"

Madam Wen hatefully wanted to chase after Sun Yiniang to continue their quarrel, but Ming Xi blocked her.

"Child! Your father is heartless. He has already allowed the concubine to climb over my head. He wants to force me out to make way for Sun Yingqiu. There's no place for your mother and me in this Marquess's household anymore."

Ming Xi: "..."

Mother, Father is still on the front lines fighting. How does he have the time to engage in these household struggles?

Although this was her own mother, even someone with as little conscience as Ming Xi sometimes couldn't help but feel exhausted on behalf of her father and Sun Yiniang.

Knowing that she couldn't reason with Madam Wen, Ming Xi gently soothed her while pulling her into the room.

"Mother, you still have me. I will always be on your side."

Madam Wen, hearing this, cried even more piteously.

"My poor child! How can Ming Chonglun, a Marquess and great general, allow his daughter to be pushed into a pit of fire!"

"The imperial palace is a place that devours people without spitting out their bones..."

Ming Xi's eyelids twitched, and she reached out to cover Madam Wen's mouth.

"Mother, there are palace cultivation matrons staying in the residence now. I understand you, but these words really cannot be spoken aloud. It doesn't matter if I am punished, but I fear it will implicate you."

Madam Wen was deeply moved by her daughter's consideration, but she felt even more heartbroken.

Her daughter was obedient and filial, just like she had been in her youth.

All she had ever wanted was to find a devoted husband for her, regardless of wealth or status, as long as he could make her happy for the rest of her life.

Unlike her, who had been betrayed by her husband and wasted her life in this cutthroat Marquess's household.

It had to be said, Madam Wen's luck was truly good!

Only someone with a head full of air could live so comfortably.

Anyone who had been battered by society would never have the idea that "wealth and status don't matter."

Madam Wen suddenly let go of Ming Xi and pulled out a package from somewhere, stuffing it into her arms.

"Child, you must leave the Marquess's household as soon as possible. The farther you run, the better. Don't worry, if the palace blames anyone, your mother will take full responsibility. I truly cannot bear to watch you jump into a pit of fire!"

Ming Xi: "..."

She felt a slight headache. If a Crown Prince's consort ran away, the Emperor's wrath would be unleashed. How could Madam Wen possibly bear that responsibility?

At that time, the entire Wuding Marquess's household would be destroyed. Her father and elder brother would lose their lives, and even Madam Wen's maiden family wouldn't escape.

How many lives would be lost in the process?

Had she ever considered that?

Madam Wen clearly hadn't. She had lived in her own world her entire life.

Ming Xi helped Madam Wen sit down and wiped her tears. "Mother, I cannot leave. I will not leave the capital, and I will not leave you."

"Moreover, both thunder and rain are the Emperor's grace. His Majesty has bestowed upon me the title of Crown Prince's consort. Isn't that immense imperial favor?"

Madam Wen was a woman educated under this imperial system, and she still had a natural reverence and obedience to the Emperor.

She nervously bit her finger. "But, but how can a mother bear to watch you..."

Ming Xi reached out and hugged her. "Mother, I understand your maternal love, but I cannot be a disloyal, unfilial, and unrighteous person, spending my life with a stained reputation, unable to show my face to anyone."

Madam Wen's face turned pale, as if she finally realized that her daughter couldn't escape. She sobbed and cursed her husband and son.

It was all their fault for being useless and failing to protect her daughter.

Ming Xi coaxed Madam Wen to sleep before leaving.

In the courtyard, all the servants who attended to Madam Wen were kneeling on the ground, trembling.

Tingyu stepped forward and quietly reported to Ming Xi all of Madam Wen's actions that day.

Actually, Madam Wen's behavior today was no different from usual, except that after dinner, while she was out for a walk to aid digestion, she had encountered a little palace maid serving Auntie Qin.

Ming Xi gave a faint smile. "I haven't even entered the palace yet, and the palace intrigues have already begun."

But she had to admit, the person behind this had set their sights on Madam Wen to use her as a tool against her, which was quite clever.

Everyone in the capital knew that the Madam of Wuding Marquess was a ridiculous woman. If used well, she could indeed be a sharp blade against her and the entire Marquess's household.

Tingru immediately said, "This servant will go and capture the person for interrogation!"

Ming Xi sighed helplessly. Tingru was loyal, but a bit too fierce.

"Even if it's just a little palace maid, we can't take the law into our own hands. Tingyu, you go and inform Auntie Qin about this."

Tingyu was a bit worried. "What if Auntie Qin is the mastermind?"

Wouldn't Miss be alerting the enemy?

Ming Xi confidently said, "She isn't."

Over these days, she had already determined that Auntie Qin was the Crown Prince's person.

Unless His Highness had lost his mind and wanted to ruin his own reputation, he wouldn't have someone instigate his own consort to run away.

Thinking of the overly kind attitudes of the two cultivation matrons towards her these days, Ming Xi's eyelids couldn't help but twitch.

Was the Crown Prince trying his best to shower her with affection?

If Ming Xi were truly an innocent and naive young girl, it would be hard not to be swayed into developing a romantic mindset.

Self-indulgently thinking that the Crown Prince was deeply in love with her.

But Ming Xi knew best that in this world, there was no such thing as unconditional kindness or unconditional love.

When a man suddenly treats you with a thousand kinds of goodness, the first thing you should ask is not to be moved, but to question why?

What does he want to gain from you?

Love means little in the face of power.

chapters.title: The Traitor
chapters.content:
Late at night, Xie Pei couldn't sleep again, so he got up to kill someone.

In the dark dungeon, the sound of whips cracking and screams echoed, sending chills down the spine.

A burly man with exotic features was tied to a torture rack. Each lash from the barbed whip dragged out long strips of flesh and blood.

Xie Pei sat upright in a rosewood armchair, carving a jade hairpin. A magnificent peony gradually came to life under his hands.

His gentle and meticulous movements formed a bizarre contrast with the bloody torture.

"Your Highness, Zhan Desheng has passed out."

Xie Pei held up the jade hairpin, carefully examining any imperfections. He casually said, "What? Do I need to teach you how to wake him up again?"

The one wielding the whip was Lu Ming, the Chief Inspector of the Brocade Guard. Hearing this, the corner of his mouth twitched.

What he really wanted to ask was whether to beat him to death directly or interrogate him first.

After all, the methods for these two were different.

But only a fool would dare to argue with the Crown Prince.

Lu Ming scooped up the salt water next to him and splashed it on the bloody figure on the rack.

"Ahhhhh!"

The burly man, Zhan Desheng, who was also the Deputy Commander of the Crown Prince's personal guards, let out a piercing scream.

Xie Pei carefully placed the jade hairpin in an exquisite box, then took out a piece of warm jade to continue carving.

Xi'er loved these beautiful accessories, so he needed to prepare more.

"Your screams are still so full of energy. Lu Ming, when did you, the Chief Inspector of the Brocade Guard, become a living Bodhisattva? Or are you not eating enough?"

Lu Ming: "..."

Zhan Desheng's face twitched, and he wailed, "Your Highness, I have been wronged!"

"Who exactly is sowing discord? I have always been loyal to Your Highness, with no other intentions!"

"Loyal? No other intentions?"

Xie Pei seemed to have heard a hilarious joke. He finally bestowed a glance upon Zhan Desheng.

"Ah!"

A small, exquisite carving knife pierced through Zhan Desheng's wrist, severing his tendons.

Xie Pei pleasantly admired Zhan Desheng's face contorted in pain.

It was just one hand. Was it that painful?

In his previous life, Zhan Desheng had personally pierced his limbs and severed his tendons to flatter and please Xie Yi.

Zhan Desheng gritted his teeth, still resisting stubbornly, "Your Highness, why?"

Ever since he had followed the Crown Prince, he had done everything properly, loyally protecting his master, never showing the slightest flaw.

The Crown Prince had suddenly turned on him, and Zhan Desheng was still confused.

Xie Pei had no obligation to explain to him. He raised his hand, and a teenager in his early teens was brought in.

"Father! Father! Save me! Save me!"

"Rong'er!"

Zhan Rong was Zhan Desheng's only son. Zhan Desheng had always doted on him, giving him whatever he wanted.

Seeing him captured, Zhan Desheng could no longer remain calm.

"Crown Prince! Crown Prince! I am truly wronged. I have never betrayed you!"

Xie Pei said indifferently, "Apply the paper torture."

Zhan Rong was pressed onto a bench, and Eunuch Yu personally administered the punishment.

As the paper soaked in liquor was pasted on his face, Zhan Rong found it increasingly difficult to breathe, his limbs struggling constantly.

Zhan Desheng's eyes were about to split open, "Rong'er! Rong'er! No! Crown Prince, please, spare my son. He knows nothing. He is innocent!"

Xie Pei's smile remained unchanged, as if painted on, cold and sinister, "Hmph, I can watch your painful and desperate look a thousand times and never get tired of it."

In the previous life, after they had crushed him and thrown him into hell, why did they have to harm Xi'er?

She was so innocent, so pure and kind.

How dare Zhan Desheng slander her as a bewitching concubine, plastering the entire Great Zhou with proclamations, making her suffer the scorn and spit of the world!

Every time he thought of her going hungry by the Nine Curves Pool, saving money for his medicine by doing embroidery until her eyes were ruined, humbling herself to beg those palace servants and guards... Xie Pei's eyes turned blood red with hatred.

"Add another layer of paper torture!"

Eunuch Yu didn't dare to look directly at the violent Crown Prince. He quickly pasted another layer of soaked paper on Zhan Rong's face.

"No! No! I confess! I confess everything! Please spare my son!"

Zhan Desheng couldn't hold on anymore. He wasn't afraid of the torture on himself, but he couldn't bear to watch his son die.

Xie Pei raised his hand, and the paper torture on Zhan Rong's face was removed.

Watching his son roll his eyes back, gasping for air like a dying dog, Zhan Desheng's face withered, his dry and cracked lips moved, not knowing if it was fear or regret.

"Your Highness, whether you believe it or not, I was truly loyal to you at first. But why did you have to pretend to be a saint?"

"I only asked you for a scholar's position at the Imperial College for my son, but you insisted he take the exam himself. Hmph, if he could pass, would I need to ask you, the Crown Prince?"

"What's all this talk about fairness? We, your subordinates, are loyal to you. Don't we just want the merit of following the dragon to the throne, to shelter our descendants, enjoy wealth and privilege?"

"If you make us the same as those commoners, why should we risk our lives for you?"

"Do you know how the Prince of Qi promised me? High-ranking titles, hereditary privileges. Tell me, should I be loyal to you or to the Prince of Qi?"

Xie Pei looked at him coldly.
