In his previous life, after he ascended the throne, he had appointed Zhan Desheng as the Commander of the Imperial Guards, a trusted confidant.

Hadn't he given him high ranks and generous salaries?

Hadn't he promoted every capable child of his officials and meritorious subjects?

He had only been unwilling to excessively indulge the children of the meritorious officials, allowing them to wantonly destroy the country's systems and harm the common people.

Was that wrong?

In the past, Xie Pei had disapproved of Emperor Taizu's massacre of the meritorious officials, thinking it too cruel and bloody. But now...

Emperor Taizu was wise. He killed well!

"Ungrateful wretch!"

Lu Ming punched Zhan Desheng hard in the stomach.

"If it weren't for His Highness saving you, your entire family would have been trampled to death by the Xirong army at the border!"

"Truly a barbaric mongrel, with no humanity!"

Zhan Desheng's mother was a commoner abducted by Xirong cavalry.

He was of mixed heritage, and at the border, he had lived worse than a dog.

It was the Crown Prince who had taken a fancy to his bravery, bringing him back to the capital and promoting him step by step to Deputy Commander of the personal guards.

In the end, he had betrayed the Crown Prince so easily.

He truly deserved to be cut into a thousand pieces.

Zhan Desheng coughed up several mouthfuls of blood and laughed coldly, "Mongrel? Heh heh, I knew it. Whether it's the Crown Prince or you, no one has ever respected me!"

"You..."

Lu Ming wanted to give him a few more punches.

Xie Pei stopped him with a calm voice, his face full of cold indifference, not the slightest bit angry at Zhan Desheng's betrayal.

Those useless emotions, he had discarded completely in his previous life.

"Yu En, chop off one of Zhan Rong's arms."

What was the use of anger?

Wasn't making the enemy wish for death enough?

"No! Crown Prince, I have already confessed. Whatever you have, take it out on me. Spare my son!"

Eunuch Yu, expressionless, raised his hand and cut off Zhan Rong's right arm with a single stroke.

Father and son screamed miserably at the same time.

One was in real pain, the other was heartbroken that his son had become a cripple.

"Crown Prince! Xie Pei! May you die a terrible death! You will surely face retribution ahhhh..."

Lu Ming couldn't stand him insulting the Crown Prince. He picked up the pliers and pulled out all of Zhan Desheng's teeth.

Xie Pei didn't mind Zhan Desheng's curses. In his previous life, under his and Xie Yi's "efforts," who in the Great Zhou hadn't cursed him as the reincarnation of King Zhou, cruel and heartless, sure to face heavenly punishment?

As long as they weren't cursing Xi'er, it didn't matter to Xie Pei.

"Drag Zhan Rong away. Keep him barely alive. Cut off a piece of him every day and send it over. I believe that soon, father and son will be reunited again."

Xie Pei caressed the warm jade in his hand, feeling that he was truly kind.

Close to red, Xi'er was kind, and he had learned a little from her.

Killing the heart, Zhan Desheng was truly broken now.

Eunuch Yu lowered his head, and Lu Ming was silent.

Even as a member of the Brocade Guard, hardened by a hundred battles, he couldn't help but feel a chill down his spine.

It wasn't because of the minor torture, but because of the current Crown Prince...

Lu Ming was the Crown Prince's milk brother, having grown up with the Crown Prince since childhood. He was a natural supporter of the Eastern Palace, with unparalleled loyalty.

His understanding of the Crown Prince was something even Eunuch Yu couldn't compare to.

Eunuch Yu was shocked by the Crown Prince's change, so how could Lu Ming remain unmoved?

But he knew that the Crown Prince was still the Crown Prince; it was just that his entire person, all his beliefs, seemed to have been shattered and twisted.

If the Crown Prince of the past was an extremely kind saint, then now he was, an extremely evil devil.

Those in power must discard unnecessary kindness. It was good that the Crown Prince could change.

But perhaps he had changed too much.

Lu Ming always felt that the Crown Prince, in this state, could destroy himself at any time.

Seeing the Crown Prince leave the dungeon, Lu Ming wanted to say something but stopped himself, ultimately asking nothing.

The ruler was the ruler.

As a subject, there were some lines that could never be crossed.

As soon as Xie Pei stepped out of the dungeon, a dark guard came to report news from the Marquis of Wuding's residence.

Xie Pei's expression instantly turned ugly. He hurriedly asked, "Is she alright?"

"Your Highness, rest assured. The Marquis's wife was persuaded by Her Highness the Crown Princess. No rumors will spread."

The dark guard saw that his master's expression had not improved, so he quickly added, "Madame Qin said that Her Highness the Crown Princess had retired early and seemed to be in good spirits, unaffected."

Only then did Xie Pei's expression ease. The dark guard then mentioned the matters from the other consorts' and concubines' residences.

Xie Pei said indifferently, "Handle it well. Don't let anyone notice the Marquis of Wuding's residence."

"Cheng Ying."

A figure silently knelt before Xie Pei.

"Use Zhan Desheng's name to lure the Prince of Qi to the Dongjiao Buddhist Temple. I remember that Minister Lin has been reciting scriptures and offering prayers for Lin Jue there recently. There are rumors that his preference is related to his ancestors. Maybe Lin Jue is following Minister Lin's example."

Since his good second brother was jealous of his upcoming marriage, as the elder brother, how could he not help him find someone to warm his bed, so he wouldn't feel so empty and lonely, always causing trouble for his wedding?

It was a good thing he, as the elder brother, didn't hold a grudge and was going through so much trouble to find him a companion.

As for the mysterious aphrodisiac that had caused Lin Jue and Zheng Yaozu's deaths, Miaoyun Pan had made some progress recently. Let his good second brother test its effects first.

"Remember to make a big scene. It would be best if the entire capital knows."

Cheng Ying accepted the order and left.

The dark guard kept his head lowered.

Even though their emotions were subdued and their loyalty was absolute, they were still stunned by the Crown Prince's... oh no, his brilliant tactics.

Xie Pei glanced at the dark guard, "Anything else?"

"...Your Highness, what to do with Lü He?"

"Died of illness."

"Yes."

After the dark guard left, Xie Pei looked up at the bright moon in the sky. The weather was nice tonight. He hoped Xi'er had sweet dreams.

He knew she liked gossip and watching the excitement.

The Prince of Qi and Minister Lin's special "intergenerational friendship", he wondered if Xi'er would like it.

chapters.title: The Drama Never Ends
chapters.content:
"Girl, Lühé is unwell. This servant feared she might pass her illness to you, so I had her sent back to the Inner Court Office this morning."

Early in the morning, Qin Aunt came to pay her respects to Ming Xi, saying this in a casual tone.

In the bronze mirror, the girl's beautiful face was reflected, her delicate brows slightly furrowed, revealing a touch of sorrowful melancholy. "How is she? Did you have someone call a physician to see her?"

"A physician from Huichun Hall was called to see her."

Of course, a physician had to be called. Otherwise, how could they prove that Lühé had suddenly fallen ill with a serious disease and died on her own, having nothing to do with Young Lady Ming and her?

Ming Xi nodded slightly. "I trust your judgment, Aunt. Tingyu."

Tingyu stepped forward and handed a bag of silver to Qin Aunt. "Please accept this on behalf of our young lady, Aunt Qin. Give it to Lühé and tell her to take good care of herself."

"This... Young Lady is so kind."

Qin Aunt hesitated for a moment but did not refuse. She understood that part of this silver was a reward for her, and part was for her to clean up the mess.

But she did not dare to say that His Highness the Crown Prince had already arranged everything perfectly. She could not help but admire in her heart.

This future concubine was always terrifyingly thorough in her actions.

Qin Aunt had heard about the situation in the Wuding Marquis's mansion before.

The marchioness was a muddle-headed woman. After the old madam passed away, who in the capital wasn't waiting to see the joke of the Wuding Marquis's inner quarters?

Yet, over the years, whether it was social interactions or household management, the marquis's mansion had never made any mistakes.

It was only now that Qin Aunt realized that all of this was not due to the clever and formidable Concubine Sun, as the rumors suggested, but rather the calm and dignified Young Lady Ming before her.

Just look at last night: knowing that Lühé was problematic, she neither lost her temper nor interrogated anyone. She simply casually sent someone to inform her.

What a clever move, letting someone from the palace handle a palace matter.

So, how could His Highness the Crown Prince think that Young Lady Ming was kind-hearted, timid, and weak?

Qin Aunt did not understand, but she respected it.

When she was assigned to Young Lady Ming's side, it was destined that she would serve this future concubine.

The more favored her master was, the brighter her future would be. Naturally, she would not be so foolish as to run and tell His Highness the Crown Prince that Young Lady Ming was not as simple and kind as he thought.

Wouldn't that be water in the brain?

...

In the Shi mansion, the morning lesson was being taught by the matron, but Shi Yuan could not focus at all. Her mind was filled with the red bean sweet soup laced with excessive saffron from last night.

If she had consumed it, she would have been crippled at best, or dead at worst.

The imperial family would not care about her as a victim. They would only think that the Shi family was unlucky, had offended the Eastern Palace, and was guilty beyond redemption.

Her fate, and that of her entire family, would be worse than in her previous life.

Shi Yuan thought of the cook found dead in the lotus pond this morning. They said she had drunk too much last night, lost her balance, and drowned.

Hah, an accident?

Then how come the bowl of red bean sweet soup had also disappeared without a trace?

Now all clues were cut off, and with the dead unable to testify, she did not even know who wanted to harm her.

Shi Yuan felt her heart clench with anger and fear.

Was it Consort Ming? Or Consort Xiao? Or perhaps the Empress or Consort Su in the palace?

Whoever it was, she had taken note of this incident.

In this life, Shi Yuan had already sworn never to let anyone bully her again.

This scene was also playing out in the mansions of the other concubines and good ladies.

The mistresses of each mansion had reacted in time, so no rumors had spread.

Ming Xi had already instructed her people to keep an eye on the other concubine and the four good ladies' mansions last night.

Even though all the mansions seemed calm, she had still noticed some clues.

Indeed, the mastermind behind the scenes was not targeting the Wuding Marquis's mansion, but rather the Eastern Palace.

The Crown Prince had not married or taken concubines for a long time and had no heirs. Finally, the Emperor had bestowed concubines and good ladies upon him. If another scandal broke out, how would the court and the people view the Eastern Palace?

Even if it did not harm the Eastern Palace's foundation, it would be enough to disgust the Crown Prince to death.

The person behind this probably thought that with six people, even if they were unlucky, at least one would be hit.

Unfortunately!

It was still a futile effort.

Ming Xi did not need to guess to know that the Crown Prince had sent people to watch over all the mansions, which was why the matter was handled so promptly and cleanly.

Indeed, if the Eastern Palace did not think ten steps ahead, its position would have been lost long ago.

The more formidable the Crown Prince was, the more potential her investment in him had, and the more she would gain in the future.

Ming Xi was temporarily very satisfied.

Qin Aunt: ...

She always felt that the young lady's attitude towards His Highness the Crown Prince was strange?

It was not that she disliked him or harbored ill intentions, but...

It was hard to describe.

In any case, it did not look like a lovestruck girl treating her beloved.

Forget it, she was just a servant and should not worry about such things.

...

Prince Qi had originally wanted the entire capital to watch the Eastern Palace's spectacle.

Who would have thought that in the end, he himself would become the joke.

Prince Qi was almost driven mad, especially after he sobered up and saw the old orange-peel face of Minister Lin beneath him, along with the strong old man's scent... Ugh!!!

What made it even more unbearable was that this shameful incident had been witnessed by many people.

Prince Qi immediately wanted to draw his sword and kill everyone to silence them, consequences be damned.

He could not let the news spread, or he would be finished.

The world would not accept, let alone support, a ridiculous prince who engaged in such scandalous acts with an old man to ascend the throne.

Kill them, kill them all!

However, Prince Qi might have gone out without checking the almanac.

Today was a day of rest, and the Emperor did not have court. On a whim, he decided to go out in disguise for a private visit and happened to go to the Buddhist temple in the eastern suburbs.

And then... there was no then.

Actually, if Prince Qi had not gone mad and tried to kill people to silence them, forcing the Emperor to intervene, the Emperor would have preferred to ignore his son, cover his face, return to the palace, and secretly order the Brocade Guards to kill him.

His lifelong reputation was about to be ruined by this unfilial beast.

His Majesty also went mad, picking up a whip and turning Prince Qi into a spinning top.

In the end, it was the commander of the Brocade Guards who saw that the situation was not right and feared that His Majesty might kill his son in public. He quickly sent someone to fetch the Crown Prince.

Only then did Prince Qi barely manage to save his life.

But the matter was not over.

During his confinement, Prince Qi had disobeyed the imperial decree by leaving the mansion privately and, disregarding shame, had engaged in such a scandalous act in public with an old man...

As soon as His Majesty returned to the palace, he issued a decree to strip Prince Qi of his title and throw him into the imperial prison.

If it were not for the Empress Dowager's timely plea, His Majesty would not have minded being a tiger that devours its own cub.

When the news spread back to the capital, Ming Xi was the first to know.

Even with her stable emotions, she was still stunned by this earth-shattering scandal.

Tingyu: ...

Must you be that shocked, Young Lady?

Half a month ago, didn't you "arrange" the match between Young Master Lin and the Zheng world's son?

When Tingyu first heard about this, her jaw had dropped in shock, and she had to confirm it repeatedly before she could believe that it was true and not a rumor.

Ming Xi seemed to have read Tingyu's mind. She slowly said, "You don't understand. Lin Jue and Zheng Yaozu might have a difference in build, but Prince Qi and Minister Lin... there's an insurmountable age gap between them!"

And this gap could be described as an abyss.

Tingruo smacked her lips. "Maybe Prince Qi just has a unique taste?"

She had heard that the royal family had peculiar preferences.

There was even an emperor who liked to use women's menstrual blood to refine elixirs.

Ming Xi: ...

She could not refute that.

Ming Xi turned to Qin Aunt. "What do you think, Aunt?"

Qin Aunt looked down at her shoes. "This servant does not dare to comment on the affairs of the imperial princes."

Ming Xi: Alright, she understood. This matter was inseparable from the Eastern Palace.

Sigh, how deep had her misunderstandings of that Crown Prince been in the past?

Was this something a human could do?

Ming Xi would never admit that she had opened a new world for His Highness the Crown Prince.

chapters.title: A Second Bloom
chapters.content:
Ming Xi could not care less about Prince Qi, but as for that old enemy, Minister Lin...

Tingyu was a considerate maid and had collected all the gossip.

"When they were taken out of the temple, he was already at his last breath."

The Lin family would probably have another feast to attend soon.

Ming Xi sighed gently. "Why must Minister Lin and his grandson be so reckless? To be so madly in love that they disregard their own bodies..."

Tingyu: ...

Qin Aunt: ...

Madly in love, my foot!

If the Lin family grandfather and grandson heard this, they might be so angry that they would come back to life.

Ming Xi asked again, "Were the ladies from the various mansions at the temple alright?"

Tingyu: "Yes, His Majesty intervened in time, so no one was injured. However, as soon as they returned to the capital, everyone called for a physician."

Clearly, they were shocked!

Oh Buddha, who could understand the pain in their eyes when they saw Prince Qi and Minister Lin rolling around together?

Many of them had already experienced a "second bloom," having previously "enjoyed" the "mad love story" of Lin Jue and Zheng Yaozu at the Princess's mansion.

Truly, the ladies all wanted to fight the Lin family to the death.

What sin had they committed to be so poisoned by the Lin family grandfather and grandson?

Ming Xi also expressed her sympathy.

Unfortunately, the laws of the Great Zhou Dynasty did not include provisions for emotional damages.

Otherwise, the Lin family would have to compensate the ladies so much that they would go bankrupt.

After this incident, the Lin family was completely finished.

Lin Jue's matter had already been a fatal blow to the Lin family.

Minister Lin could still claim that he had not raised his grandson well, and there was some room to redeem himself.

But this time?

Moreover, no matter how ridiculous Prince Qi was, he was still a member of the imperial family. To maintain the imperial family's dignity as much as possible, His Majesty would certainly pin all the blame on the old Minister Lin.

The Lin family was doomed.

Ming Xi had been in a stalemate with the Lin family grandfather and grandson for so many years.

She had never expected that in just half a month, the Lin family would collapse so easily.

Even now, it still felt somewhat surreal to her.

Of course, she could not sympathize with her enemy.

If it were not for the fact that she and her brother had left a way out back then, and not placed all their hopes on the court, her father and the 300,000 Tian Ding Army would have already perished in Weizhou.

Millions of innocent people on the border would have become the ghosts under the Wuze cavalry's blades.

And in the capital, what kind of fate would have awaited her, the family member of a defeated general?

Therefore, disgrace, death without a complete body, and eternal infamy were what those two hypocritical and disgusting vipers deserved.

...

Clearly, Ming Xi was not the only one stunned by the scandal involving Prince Qi and Minister Lin.

In the En Guo Duke's mansion, Xiao Mingzhu could not close her mouth for a long time.

This was fake, right?

How could the male lead... ue!

Xiao Mingzhu could not help but vomit.

"System, come out and explain!"

[...]

The system had been in chaos for a long time.

[Ding, no anomalies detected. Please adjust the strategy plan yourself, host, and strive to complete the mission.]

Xiao Mingzhu: ...

You useless system! Do you know how useless you are?

The male lead was acting like he had eaten some magic mushrooms from Yunnan. How could you say there were no anomalies?

And you still want me to pursue him?

Pursue your sister's leg!

This dog system was treating her like a Japanese person.

[The main mission must be completed, or you will be erased!]

Xiao Mingzhu clutched her head in pain. "Shut up! Shut up!"

Like Xiao Mingzhu, Shi Yuan was also on the verge of collapse.

Had Prince Qi been cursed in this life?

This was beyond madness.

Could he still replace the Crown Prince and usurp the throne in this life?

Would the world accept such a perverted emperor who was infatuated with old men?

No, Shi Yuan suddenly broke out in a cold sweat.

She remembered now. In her previous life, until her death, Prince Qi had only been the Prince Regent and had never ascended the throne.

She had always thought...

Could it be that in the end, the one who won was still Emperor Xie Pei?

But by that time, Xie Pei had already become a useless man!

Shi Yuan's head throbbed as if it were about to split open. She felt as if she were standing at the edge of an abyss.

No matter which path she took, she would fall to her doom.

What should she do? What on earth should she do?

It was all the Crown Prince's fault. Why did he not love her?

...

The Lin family quickly faced impeachment from many censors.

The Emperor ordered the Brocade Guards to investigate thoroughly.

In just two days, the Brocade Guards obtained irrefutable evidence and went to the Lin mansion to confiscate property and arrest people.

Ming Xi sat by the window of a private room in a teahouse, watching as the Lin family members, one by one, were taken away in shackles by the Brocade Guards.

Among the crowd, she spotted Lin Huairou.

It had not been long since Lin Huairou had been so arrogant at the Princess's mansion. Now, she was thin as a skeleton, her face covered in injuries, and she looked completely mad.

After Lin Jue's death, the Lin family had taken out all their anger on Lin Huairou.

Even if she shouted that it was Ming Xi and the Wuding Marquis's mansion's conspiracy, what could she do?

Lin Huairou had no evidence, and neither did the Lin family.

How could they deal with the rising and powerful Wuding Marquis's mansion and the future concubine of the Eastern Palace?

Minister Lin had been thinking of revenge, believing that a gentleman's revenge is a decade long.

Unfortunately, now... he was dead, and the Lin family had fallen.

They had not even managed to harm the Wuding Marquis's mansion in the slightest.

Ming Xi rested her chin on her hand, looking at the Lin mansion, which still had white banners hanging. Minister Lin would surely die with his eyes wide open.

Knock knock.

The door to the private room was knocked.

Tingruo went to open the door.

"Do not make a sound."

A familiar deep male voice came from outside. Ming Xi turned her gaze and saw the Crown Prince, dressed in plain clothes, stopping Tingruo from kneeling and paying respects.

She stood up. "Y-Young Master, how did you come here?"

Xie Pei smiled gently at her. "I came to ask the young lady for a cup of tea. I hope I am not disturbing you?"

Ming Xi smiled in return. "Of course not. Please, come in, Young Master."

Xie Pei lifted his robe and sat down. This time, it was Ming Xi who made tea for him.

Balun, disguised as a servant boy, signaled Tingyu and Tingruo to leave so as not to disturb the two masters.

Tingruo ignored him. Only after Ming Xi nodded at her did she follow her sister and Balun out.

Tingyu apologetically said to Balun, "Please forgive us. My sister's mind is a bit..."

Balun found the two sisters amusing. He smiled. "Young Lady Tingruo is loyal to her mistress. That is a good thing."

In the private room, Ming Xi placed the tea in front of Xie Pei.

At this moment, the Brocade Guards carried out box after box of precious fabrics, gold and silver jewelry, antiques, and calligraphy from the Lin mansion, along with a thick stack of account books from the officials below.

The onlookers were in an uproar. After all, this was the so-called upright and incorruptible Minister Lin!

Who would have thought that his home was filled with countless gold, silver, and treasures?

So this was the so-called integrity and self-discipline?

Truly, three years as a clean magistrate, ten thousand taels of silver.

The common people had gained new insights once again.

Ming Xi and Xie Pei showed no surprise on their faces.

Xie Pei sipped his tea, feeling that the tea Ming Xi made was much more fragrant than his own.

Ming Xi chatted casually. "Young Master, you have a million things to attend to daily. How do you have time to come out for tea today?"

Prince Qi, oh no, the Second Prince, was in trouble. The Lin family was destroyed. The power structure of the court had changed instantly. As the Crown Prince, he should be the busiest person right now.

"Because of my second brother's absurdity, my father has been in a bad mood these past few days and does not want to see me. I had to come out to take a break."

Prince Sorrow had run away from the prince's mansion on his own. Minister Lin had also gone to the temple on his own. His Majesty's incognito visit was also a last-minute decision.

Everything was so "coincidental."

But even though there was not the slightest trace of calculation, the emperor was still suspicious.

As a sensitive figure, the Crown Prince had, for the sake of appearances, pleaded for his good second brother, stabilized his persona, and then gracefully disappeared to avoid drawing the Emperor's ire.

Thinking of her past life's foolish filial piety towards the Emperor, always concerned about his health and racking her brains to help him share his burdens, only to end up... all her efforts were in vain.

Even if Xie Pei was well-composed, Ming Xi noticed the flicker of sarcasm in his eyes.

She paused for a moment. "Every family has its own difficulties."

In the imperial family, it was even more so. For the sake of that supreme power, it was common for blood relatives to suspect and kill each other.

Xie Pei turned the teacup in his hand. "Yes, it's a pity I understood this a little too late."

Ming Xi: "Shouldn't it not be too late?"

Xie Pei met her clear and limpid eyes and suddenly smiled lightly. "Yes, not too late."

After that, the two of them continued to watch the Brocade Guards confiscate the Lin family's property, neither of them speaking again.

Until a young scholar suddenly threw rotten eggs and vegetable leaves at the Lin family, cursing them for being hypocritical, sanctimonious, and shameless to the extreme!

Xie Pei, however, seemed to see something amusing and let out a "heh."

Ming Xi turned to look at him. "What is Young Master laughing at?"

Wasn't this scene supposed to be the exposure of a hypocrite's true face, a moment of great satisfaction?

Why did he look at those scholars as if they were a group of pig brains?

chapters.title: Promise
chapters.content:
When her gaze turned toward him, Xie Pei retracted the sarcasm on his face and put his gentle mask back on.

His thin lips slightly pursed, not wanting to say anything sharp that might make her misunderstand him as a bitter and sarcastic person.

She didn’t know how those fools in her past life had slandered her.

Each one of them preached morality and justice, yet turned around to confuse right and wrong, and spared no effort to viciously attack an innocent woman.

As if the harsher they cursed, the more noble and upright they appeared.

Why didn’t they ever consider that the rise and fall of a dynasty had never been caused by the so-called "disastrous beauties" they spoke of?

Xie Pei’s chest burned with resentment. In his past life, the more he had respected and honored these scholars, the more he despised them now.

"What does the young lady think of the Lin family, grandfather and grandson?"

Ming Xi paused, hesitated, and instead of answering directly, said, "Young Master, how about I tell you a story?"

"Hmm?"

"I once read a storybook that described the daily life of a highly praised honest official. It went like this: 'The official was very incorruptible. After finishing his official duties each day, he would steal half a day of leisure in his modest residence, sitting in a rosewood armchair, holding pre-rain Longjing tea in his hands, admiring the authentic *Lanting Xu* by Wang Xizhi. The sunlight fell on his clothes, shimmering, and the white jade pendant at his waist, as pure as his character.'"

Rosewood, imperial tribute tea, jade pendants, antique paintings, each either priceless or worth a fortune.

This wasn’t a storybook.

It was the true portrayal of the so-called "humble abode, clean hands, and noble integrity" of the Donglin Party in reality.

Xie Pei raised his eyes, and the two locked gazes.

After a moment, the man relaxed his brows and let out a soft laugh, praising, "The young lady’s story is very interesting. It truly opened my eyes."

Ming Xi tilted her head slightly. "But it seems to me, Young Master, that you already knew this story."

Previously, she had always been puzzled as to why the Crown Prince had suddenly turned his blade toward the Lin family.

After all, though the Lin family grandfather and grandson were treacherous and ruthless in private, their public stance of supporting orthodoxy and loyalty to the country was flawless.

The Crown Prince had always treated Old Master Lin with courtesy and even favored him greatly.

At these words, Xie Pei’s gaze turned extremely dark and obscure.

In his past life, the Lin family grandfather and grandson had pretended to be loyal and upright while secretly colluding with Xie Yi to stage a coup. They controlled the entire cabinet, joined forces with Zhan Desheng, and overthrew him from the throne.

All while Xi’er was leading the palace maids and eunuchs in a desperate attempt to protect him.

Those Donglin Party members, who constantly shouted about loyalty to the emperor, were either accomplices or quick to kneel.

Indeed, as long as there was wealth and honor to be had, who cared who sat on the throne?

"Young Master?" Ming Xi, unaware of how badly the Donglin Party had betrayed Xie Pei in his past life, saw his expression was off and softly called out to him.

Xie Pei suppressed the surging killing intent, not wanting to scare her, but his words still couldn’t help but reveal sharp sarcasm.

"I only know that some people are nothing but despicable, hypocritical moralists, the true traitors who bring disaster to the nation and its people."

Ming Xi: "..."

This evaluation was too accurate!

Ming Xi almost couldn’t resist clapping for His Highness the Crown Prince.

Wasn’t that exactly the case?

All they cared about was factional strife and their own wealth and honor. They didn’t care about the floods outside or the suffering of the people.

Calling them beasts would be an insult to beasts.

Unfortunately, the Donglin Party’s slogans were so loud that even the emperor believed they were upright and loyal officials who served the country and its people.

Who would have thought they were all hypocrites who only knew how to morally bind others, engage in infighting, and lacked any backbone?

Ming Xi had originally thought she would have to continue struggling against the Lin family grandfather and grandson, as well as the entire Donglin Party.

The emperor and the Crown Prince still liked to employ these loudmouthed kings.

Now...

She didn’t know how the Crown Prince had seen through the Donglin Party’s true face, but for now, it was only beneficial to her.

Ah, she was becoming more and more satisfied with this future husband and superior of hers.

Of course, Ming Xi had never once actively spoken out against the Donglin Party, nor would she ever impulsively demand that the Crown Prince exterminate them all after ascending the throne.

The rear palace must not interfere in politics. She knew best what was harmless and what kind of handle must never be left.

Xie Pei looked at her and smiled gently. Though his voice was soft, it carried immense sincerity. "Rest assured, they won’t amount to anything."

He promised her that in the future, he would ensure the Great Zhou would have no Donglin Party left, he would uproot them completely.

Ming Xi lowered her gaze and sipped her tea, pretending not to understand the deeper meaning in the Crown Prince’s words.

Seeing her holding the teacup, obediently lowering her head in silence, Xie Pei’s eyes filled with a smile, soft and indulgent.

He didn’t force her, simply raising his hand to toast her with his teacup.

Ming Xi paused, then smiled slightly, lifting her own cup to clink against his.

The two of them drank the tea in their cups in one go.

A thousand words were left unspoken.

"Young Master, it’s getting late. I should go back."

With the wedding approaching, she wasn’t supposed to be out.

But the complete downfall of her archenemy, how could she not come witness it herself?

Ming Xi picked up her veil and took her leave of Xie Pei.

The white gauze accidentally caught on the step-shaking ornament in her hair. Xie Pei, worried she might pull her hair, stepped forward to help her adjust it, his movements gentle.

It was the first time they had been this close. Through the white veil, Ming Xi caught the pleasant scent of agarwood on him.

After helping her secure the veil, Xie Pei withdrew his hand and took a step back, polite and composed.

"My apologies for the presumption."

Ming Xi shook her head. "Thank you, Young Master. Then I’ll take my leave."

"Alright."

Just as Ming Xi was about to open the door to leave, Xie Pei suddenly called out to her, "Xi’er."

Ming Xi turned her head. Through the thin veil, their eyes met.

Xie Pei softly said, "Be careful on the way."

Ming Xi curved her eyebrows slightly. "Mmm, you too, Young Master."

---

"Eldest Young Lady, why don’t you find some non-harmful sedatives? Whenever the madam... starts making a scene, have the servants sedate her?"

Sun Concubine, who had been reporting the accounts to Ming Xi, suddenly spoke up.

Ming Xi raised her eyes to look at her, and Sun Concubine, frightened, clutched the account book tightly.

"I; I’m not trying to harm the madam! It’s just... there’s no other way. You’re now the Crown Prince’s concubine. How many people in the capital are watching our Hou residence? In the future, incidents like that night will surely happen again."

Sun Concubine swallowed. "The imperial family’s prestige is formidable. If someone with ill intentions uses this to make trouble, the madam will bring disaster upon the entire Hou residence and hundreds of lives!"

The last time Madame Wen had an episode, it had truly terrified Sun Concubine.

Madame Wen was indeed thoughtless, she could easily become a blade in someone else’s hands to use against Ming Xi and the Hou residence.

But she was also the nominal mistress of the Hou residence. If she really caused a commotion, Sun Concubine would have no way to stop her.

To be honest, if it weren’t for her deep fear of Ming Xi and her brother, Sun Concubine would have long since wanted to poison Madame Wen to prevent her from constantly bringing disaster upon the family.

But now, even at the risk of offending Ming Xi, Sun Concubine had to speak up.

Her life, Little Geng’s life, and her maiden family’s lives were at stake!

Ming Xi didn’t get angry. She simply said indifferently, "Where would I find such a drug?"

Medicine was three parts poison. Did she not consider this option?

But using sedatives frequently, how was that different from slowly poisoning Madame Wen?

If it were an enemy, or like her birth mother from her past life, who not only ignored her but also conspired with her half-brothers to harm her, then she wouldn’t hesitate to use any means necessary.

But Madame Wen, despite her troublesome behavior, couldn’t be said to not love her daughter. Even if her actions always ended up harming others without benefiting herself.

Ming Xi had feelings for this mother. No matter what, she could never truly bring herself to harm her.

Sun Concubine spoke in a very soft voice, "I’ve heard that the palace has many strange and rare secret medicines. After you enter the palace, Eldest Young Lady, why not look into it?"

Ming Xi was speechless. Palace secret medicines were things one could just casually look for?

"Enough. I have my own arrangements for my mother. I won’t let her implicate the Hou residence."

Sun Concubine thought to herself, *It’s not that I’m afraid of ten thousand things, but that one in ten thousand.*

However, she didn’t dare to argue with Ming Xi.

Ming Xi glanced at her. "If such a thing happens again in the future, and you truly can’t stop my mother, then, without harming her, gag her and tie her up, then send word to me in the palace. I’ll tell you the method of contact before I marry."

Sun Concubine was overjoyed. "Eldest Young Lady is so clever!"

Ming Xi: "..."

This praise was really unnecessary.

---

chapters.title: The Wedding
chapters.content:
The imperial family’s marriage to a concubine was not like the common folk’s taking of a concubine, it was still a formal wedding with strict procedures.

The Qin Tian Jian (Imperial Astronomical Bureau) selected the auspicious date, and the Ministry of Rites was in charge of the wedding arrangements, including the betrothal gifts, dowry, and welcoming the bride.

Since this was the Crown Prince’s first marriage, both inside and outside the palace attached great importance to it. Within the bounds of regulations, everything was done as grandly as possible.

The chosen auspicious day was the eighth day of the tenth month, a perfect day for marriage.

Early in the morning, Ming Xi was bustled about for her hair and makeup, dressed in a full set of phoenix crown and embroidered cape.

After all, a Crown Prince’s concubine also had an imperial decree and court attire, though the specifications were lower than that of the Crown Princess.

Aunt Qin brought her a bowl of sweet congee to pad her stomach but didn’t let her eat too much, fearing she might lose her composure.

Following the instructions of the ceremonial official, Ming Xi was like a beautifully crafted doll, arranged this way and that by Grandma Quanfu and the others.

Due to the intense fighting at the front, neither the Marquis of Wu Ding nor his sons could return to the capital to see their daughter/sister off.

Ming Jing had long since sent a letter expressing his guilt to his sister, along with a box of land deeds and banknotes sent by his personal guards.

He wished he could give the entire Marquis of Wu Ding’s residence as her dowry.

But since she was a concubine and not the Crown Princess, the dowry couldn’t be too extravagant.

The Young Master had no choice but to stuff as much money and land as possible into his sister’s dowry.

Ming Xi replied with a thick letter to comfort her overprotective brother. She didn’t feel any regret.

In her eyes, marrying the Crown Prince as a concubine was no different from joining a large corporation in the modern world, except for the more cumbersome procedures and rules.

Once she "got promoted and received a raise" in the future and became the "boss’s wife" of the palace, her father and brother could return to celebrate with her.

The concubines of the Eastern Palace were all of noble birth, their marriages political alliances. Normally, the Crown Prince would personally come to welcome his bride.

However, today, with two concubines and four good ladies marrying at the same time, the Crown Prince couldn’t welcome them all personally.

The Ministry of Rites didn’t want to offend anyone, so they decided to have imperial princes and clansmen stand in for the Crown Prince to escort the brides.

The streets were decorated with lanterns and banners, filled with the sounds of gongs and drums, fireworks, and firecrackers. Ming Xi, seated in a flowery sedan chair, swayed all the way into the Eastern Palace.

Since there was no Crown Princess in the Eastern Palace yet, the concubines and good ladies didn’t need to serve tea. After the wedding ceremony, they were each sent to their respective bridal chambers.

After being tossed about by the various ceremonial procedures all day, Ming Xi finally got to sit down and couldn’t help but let out a sigh of relief.

Ming Xi had always cherished her healthy body in this life. In addition to taking good care of herself, she practiced Tai Chi and yoga daily.

A balance of work and rest was the secret to longevity.

So, even though she looked as delicate as a willow, she was actually... not as strong as an ox, but she was indeed much healthier than most frail young ladies in the capital.

After a day of bustling about, Ming Xi actually felt fine, she wasn’t so exhausted that she was about to collapse, just a little hungry.

But until it was determined which new bride the Crown Prince would visit tonight, they all had to sit properly on the bridal bed with their veils down, waiting.

"Noble Consort."

"What is it?"

Ming Xi turned her head, and the tassels of her veil swayed. The exquisite embroidery of dragons and phoenixes on it shimmered in the candlelight.

Even Aunt Qin couldn’t help but be dazzled.

They were all new brides, but for some reason, every move, every frown, every smile of this Concubine Noble Consort, even just her voice, was more beautiful and radiant than anyone else’s.

During the wedding ceremony just now, even though the Crown Prince had maintained his composure, Aunt Qin had noticed that His Highness’s entire attention had been on Concubine Ming.

"His Highness ordered this servant to bring you a bowl of shredded pork noodles to pad your stomach."

Ming Xi’s eyelashes fluttered slightly. "Can I lift the veil?"

"Let Ting Yu lift it slightly, and this servant will help you eat."

"Mmm."

After finishing the noodles, she felt much more comfortable. Ming Xi rinsed her mouth, and the veil was lowered again.

Aunt Qin brought her a soft cushion to support her waist. "You can lean against the edge of the bed. It will be more comfortable. His Highness is still outside entertaining guests. It will be a while before he comes."

Ming Xi: "..."

Oh, so she was lucky enough to be the first one the Crown Prince would visit tonight.

There was an advantage to wearing the veil, she didn’t have to pretend to be shy or excited.

But Ming Xi wasn’t particularly surprised.

After all, among the six of them, she had the most noble birth, and the political value she brought to the Crown Prince was the highest.

As long as he wasn’t out of his mind, he would definitely give her and the Marquis of Wu Ding face tonight.

As for sleeping with a man she wasn’t very familiar with, Ming Xi felt it was fine, she wasn’t nervous or repulsed.

Now that she had "joined the company," there was no reason not to "go to work."

Just as Ming Xi was waiting so long that she was about to fall asleep, the sound of palace servants kneeling and kowtowing came from outside the door.

She, who had been leaning so far she was almost rolling onto the bed, suddenly sat up straight.

Steady footsteps approached her one by one. Under the veil, Ming Xi suddenly caught sight of a red robe embroidered with dragon patterns and auspicious clouds.

Her eyes brightened, and she subconsciously raised her head.

The palace lanterns were bright, and the man who came into view was wearing a red wedding robe, his hair tied with a golden crown, from which two red ribbons hung down. His sharp, oppressive brows and eyes were softened by a faint smile, making him appear warm and gentle.

He was very tall, with a straight and towering figure, bearing the demeanor of a dragon and a phoenix. But when he looked down at her, there wasn’t the slightest air of superiority.

It hadn’t been long since they last met at the teahouse, but as their eyes met on this wedding night, it felt as if a lifetime had passed.

Ming Xi lowered her head. "Your Highness."

The girl in her red wedding dress was as beautiful as a fairy, her skin even more lustrous and white than the pearls on the phoenix crown. When she lowered her eyes, she was the picture of a shy new bride.

Xie Pei’s Adam’s apple rolled, suppressing his wild joy. He gently sat down on the bridal bed.

Grandma Quanfu brought the wine for the "he jing jiu" (wedding toast) ceremony.

Amidst the joyful blessings, the two of them each picked up a cup, drank half, then exchanged and finished the other half.

The fragrance of the wine lingered. As their eyes occasionally met, Ming Xi somewhat understood the meaning of "heavenly thunder stirring earthly fire."

Even without feelings, in such an atmosphere, it was enough to make a man and a woman feel a sense of ambiguous intimacy.

After drinking the wedding toast, Grandma Quanfu respectfully presented a red tray holding two exquisite pairs of scissors.

Ming Xi was taken aback. Having lived in the Great Zhou for fifteen years, she was naturally familiar with the entire wedding process of the capital’s nobility.

But the "he jing jiu" was one thing, this hair-tying ritual was usually reserved for the official wife.

She was just a concubine, not the Crown Princess!

"Xi’er."

The Crown Prince’s low, magnetic voice was slightly hoarse.

Ming Xi looked at him but didn’t ruin the mood by saying it was against the rules. She picked up the scissors and cut off a lock of her hair to give to him.

Xie Pei’s smile deepened. His Xi’er was always so pure and lovely, never letting his expectations down.

Xie Pei carefully took a red string and, with his long, dexterous fingers, tied their hair into a lover’s knot.

Ming Xi blinked in surprise.

His Highness was truly... multi-talented.

After securing the lover’s knot, Xie Pei raised his hand to gently caress her face. The soft, delicate touch of her skin fascinated him to no end.

After his disability in his past life, even touching her had become an unattainable luxury.

The two times they had met before, he had to restrain himself fiercely, afraid of acting improperly and scaring her.

Now, he could finally, rightfully, be intimate with her.

Ming Xi felt a little ticklish from his touch. "Your Highness?"

Xie Pei’s deep gaze fell on her full, glossy red lips, and his breathing became a little disordered, but he didn’t go any further.

He couldn’t rush. She was timid. In the past, even if he spoke a little loudly, it would startle her.

He remembered that in his past life, he had once reprimanded her, and the girl had immediately teared up. He had regretted it instantly.

Now, every time he thought back, Xie Pei wanted to slap his past self for being such a damn fool.

Xi’er had only beaten the nephew of Empress Xiao into a cripple. Even if she had killed him, what was the big deal? How could he have scolded her for that?

Xie Pei despised his past self, who had been a hypocritical, stupid fool.

But in the end, it was all their fault!

Ming Xi felt that tonight’s Crown Prince was a little strange.

The red candles flickered, making her face flush.

She tilted her head slightly, the tassels swaying. "Your Highness?"

Xie Pei reached out to support her small head. "Let me help you remove the phoenix crown."

Ming Xi said, "Oh," then added, "Thank you, Your Highness."

Xie Pei let out a low laugh. "You are my wife. There’s no need to thank me."

Ming Xi: "..."

She didn’t know how to respond to that.

After all, she was just a concubine, right?

Ming Xi was starting to suspect she had received a fake imperial decree.

Her black hair fell loose. The atmosphere in the bridal chamber grew even more ambiguous, and Xie Pei’s gaze became even more scorching.

But Ming Xi glanced at the peanuts and red dates on the bridal quilt and looked up at Xie Pei, as if asking: *Are we starting now? Won’t it be uncomfortable?*

Xie Pei met her clear, bright eyes and: "..."

He burst into laughter, unable to help but recall the first time she had served him in his past life.

She had been shy when she first saw him, but once things actually started, she had become composed, almost driving him to the brink of collapse, and leaving him craving more.

chapters.title: The Wedding Night
chapters.content:
Xie Pei smoothed her hair for her, "The hot water is ready. Go bathe first."

Ming Xi obediently nodded, not pretending to be considerate by asking if he wanted her to serve him first or anything like that.

Excessive eagerness might not be to the Crown Prince's liking.

Moreover, Ming Xi had been pampered and precious for fifteen years. It had always been others serving her, so when would it be her turn to serve someone else?

Even if the Crown Prince was now her immediate superior, it was still not happening.

Ying Yu lowered her head, supporting her young lady to the bathing room, thinking that her young lady was indeed remarkable, able to remain so composed and natural before the crown prince of a nation.

By the time Ming Xi came out of the bathing room, Xie Pei had already finished his toiletries.

He had changed into a night robe and was casually leaning against the edge of the bed, a book in his hand.

In the candlelight, the man's features were extremely handsome, and his figure was excellent. Clothed, he appeared slender, but unclothed, he was muscular. His chest was slightly open, revealing solid muscle lines. His skin was fair yet did not appear weak.

Ming Xi's little claws suddenly felt a bit itchy.

Sleeping with such a handsome man, Ming Xi thought she wasn't losing out at all.

There was just one thing: this man was not hers alone.

But when had a boss ever belonged exclusively to an employee?

"Why are you standing there?"

Xie Pei smiled and stretched out his hand to her.

The girl, dressed only in a red silk nightgown, was as beautiful as a painting. She walked over to him obediently. Which man could resist that?

Xie Pei's eyes deepened, and he couldn't help but pull her soft waist, making her sit on his lap.

"Are you tired?"

Ming Xi seemed oblivious to the presumptuous posture and only shook her head, "Marrying Your Highness makes me very happy. I don't feel tired."

Xie Pei's expression softened even more, unable to hide his joy.

Ming Xi blinked, see? Doing more was not as good as flattering more.

Xie Pei was unaware of his little wife's thoughts and gently said, "I've wronged you."

Ming Xi couldn't respond to that, but recalling the times she had been with him, she felt that sometimes she should still ask, "What wrongs does Your Highness speak of?"

Xie Pei held her tightly with pity, "In every aspect."

Not being able to marry her with the grandest wedding ceremony, and having her enter the palace with other women...

It was his own fault for being so stupid before, only wanting to be a filial son and a sage, not disappointing the emperor, the court officials, or the people.

As a result, he now seemed to have a stable position, but in reality, he was surrounded by crises, with mountains pressing down on him.

He couldn't even let her do as she pleased.

Xie Pei looked into her eyes, "Xian'er, do you blame me?"

After all, he could have, like in his previous life, waited until he ascended the throne, cleared all obstacles, and then presented the imperial seal to her.

But the fear and despair of losing her tormented him constantly, afraid that if something went wrong, he wouldn't be able to protect her.

Only with her by his side could Xie Pei maintain his sanity, barely keeping his human form, not twisting into a monstrous figure.

Ming Xi always felt that her mindset was completely out of sync with this Crown Prince.

Fortunately, she never made things difficult for herself and directly asked, "Blame Your Highness for what?"

Xie Pei sighed, "Everything."

Ming Xi: "..."

Forget it, maybe we should just sleep.

Physical communication was much simpler than mental communication.

Seeing that she seemed sleepy, Xie Pei didn't say anything else. He held her and lay down on the bed, lifting his hand to cover them both with the quilt. He gently patted her back as if coaxing a child, "Sleep."

Ming Xi: "?"

And then?

Seeing that this lord really wasn't going to do anything, Ming Xi had to remind him, "Your Highness, tonight is our wedding night."

It wasn't that she insisted on sleeping with the Crown Prince, but today the entire capital was watching the Crown Prince take his concubines.

If she didn't serve him tonight, the higher-ups in the palace would hold her accountable.

She would also become a laughingstock in the entire palace.

Ming Xi completely refused that.

Xie Pei's breathing grew heavier, and he curled his fingers, lightly tapping her forehead in helplessness, "Don't make trouble. You're still young."

After his rebirth, he had read many medical books and learned that early intercourse and childbirth could greatly harm a woman's health.

In this life, he would never allow anything that could harm her health to happen.

She had to be well, always by his side.

Xie Pei could no longer bear her departure.

Ming Xi lightly bit her red lips, "But..."

Xie Pei soothingly rubbed her back, "Don't worry. I've arranged everything. No one will know, and no one will be able to blame you."

Ming Xi leaned against his chest, feeling a bit conflicted.

She could feel the changes in his body, proving that he did have desires for her.

But Ming Xi hadn't expected him to endure and restrain himself for the reason of fearing it would harm her body.

How rare!

Not to mention the feudal imperial era's rulers, even modern men rarely controlled their desires for the sake of their girlfriend's health.

What was the Crown Prince after?

Ming Xi felt that this "pig butchering" scheme was huge and terrifying!

But since he had said so, she couldn't exactly take the initiative to straddle him and force herself on him, could she?

Ming Xi thought about her small body. Forget it, let's just sleep. The ship would reach the bridge naturally, and even if it sank, it could be salvaged.

Yeah, no big problem.

The person in his arms gradually calmed her breathing. Xie Pei couldn't sleep. His dark eyes were fixed tightly on her. The fake gentle facade tore apart, revealing the ferocious possessiveness and obsession.

"Xian'er..."

Xie Pei greedily leaned closer to her, feeling her breath. Satisfaction made his body tremble uncontrollably, as if burned by fire, yet he savored it.

Only this way could he feel that he had truly been reborn.

He hadn't lost her.

Taking advantage of her deep sleep, Xie Pei shamelessly revealed his true self. He carefully kissed her forehead, nose, and cheeks, then restrainedly held her soft red lips, tracing them carefully. His Adam's apple moved up and down.

It wasn't until the girl uncomfortably turned her head slightly that Xie Pei let out a low breath, reluctantly letting go of her lips. He reached out to hold her even tighter in his arms, as if he wanted to merge her into his own flesh and blood.

"Xian'er, good night."

No one would ever be able to separate them again.

---

chapters.title: Taking the Initiative to Kiss Him
chapters.content:
They had slept very well last night. Early in the morning, when Xie Pei got up to attend court, Ming Xi woke up.

She struggled to sit up from the bed, her voice soft, "Your Highness."

Xie Pei reached out to hold her waist, letting her lean against him, "Did I wake you?"

Ming Xi shook her head, "I will serve Your Highness in dressing."

Xie Pei smiled, "There's no need for you to serve me. If you're sleepy, continue sleeping."

"Isn't that not good?"

Although she said it wasn't good, Ming Xi didn't take any action, only looking at him innocently.

"There's nothing bad about it."

Xie Pei gently helped her lie down. He didn't call any palace servants to attend to him, dressing himself in his court attire.

The Crown Prince's attire in the Great Zhou Dynasty was magnificent and noble. A white broad-sleeved outer garment embroidered with golden dragon patterns, a vermilion inner lining, and a waistband inlaid with gold and jade.

Even though Ming Xi didn't have a romantic brain, it didn't mean she didn't appreciate beauty, especially the top-tier beauty like the Crown Prince.

It was just that His Highness the Crown Prince had a very down-to-earth daily life.

She didn't know that after Xie Pei's rebirth, he didn't allow anyone except her to approach his body.

Even Yu Gonggong, who had served him since childhood, had almost had his neck twisted several times initially.

Xie Pei, of course, noticed her gaze. The corners of his thin lips lifted, and he sat back on the edge of the bed, touching her hair, "Rest well. With me here, you don't have to worry about anything."

Ming Xi softly placed her hand on his arm, giving him a full response, "Your Highness is really good to me."

"Silly girl."

Xie Pei restrained his impulse to be intimate with her, got up, and left the bedroom.

A hardworking boss was indeed a good boss.

Ming Xi looked at his retreating figure, then rolled over to sleep a little more. Her gaze accidentally swept over the red lacquered box on the bedside table.

She reached out to take it, opened it, and saw a handkerchief with a red plum blossom inside.

Ming Xi: "..."

She finally understood why Xie Pei said he had arranged everything.

Wasn't this Crown Prince a bit too considerate?

Ming Xi put the wooden box back in its place. She didn't want to think about it anymore and decided to continue sleeping.

...

The Eastern Palace had no official consort, so after the wedding night, there was no need to pay respects to the Crown Princess.

Also, because Ming Xi was a concubine, she didn't have the qualifications to enter the palace to pay respects to the Emperor and Empress the next day.

They were all elders with extremely high status. Ming Xi didn't want to go into the palace to play the role of a grandchild at all.

So, thinking about it, being a concubine seemed not bad, enjoying life with fewer responsibilities.

As for the other five "sisters" who had married into the Eastern Palace the day before.

They were all new brides and hadn't served the Crown Prince yet. It wouldn't be appropriate for them to run around, so everyone was temporarily staying in their own rooms.

Ming Xi rarely had such leisure time. She didn't have to get up early to manage the affairs of the Hou residence, check the account books, or oversee her numerous properties.

She slept until the sun was high in the sky before getting up.

Ying Yu led the palace maids in to attend to her washing and dressing.

The wooden box by the bed was already gone. Ming Xi didn't ask about it, only concerned about her new boss, "Has His Highness returned?"

"He came back after court. Seeing that you were still resting, he ordered us not to disturb you. Then he went to the Wenhe Hall to handle government affairs, saying he would come back later to accompany you for lunch."

Only heaven knew that when Ying Yu saw the Crown Prince come back from court while her young lady was still fast asleep, her scalp had almost exploded from fear.

She had wanted to wake her young lady up, but Ting Ruo had held her back... what a good sister.

The Crown Prince had also quietly reprimanded her, telling her to always prioritize the young lady in the future. How could she dare to wake her mistress from sleep?

Ying Yu: "..."

She wasn't exactly wronged. The Crown Prince valued her young lady, which only made Ying Yu happy.

The problem was, while a man was still infatuated, he would tolerate everything the young lady did. But once he grew tired of her, all her past offenses would become sins.

Ming Xi noticed Ying Yu's worry and let out a light laugh.

If one day she fell out of favor, having one more offense or one less wouldn't make a difference.

When those in power wanted to deal with you, even if you were a saint, they could still pick at an egg to find a bone and frame you.

Wasn't Consort Wei from history virtuous and perfect?

In the end, wasn't she still suspected and abandoned by the emperor?

Being cautious didn't mean she had to be constantly on edge, or bow and scrape to the Crown Prince to the extreme.

Otherwise, he might even suspect that she and the Wu Ding Marquis's residence had some kind of conspiracy.

So, while she could enjoy herself, she should do so to the fullest. She shouldn't wrong herself for anyone.

A new bride should wear red. Ming Xi chose a crimson gold-embroidered cross-collar robe, a smoke-pink embroidered gown with a trailing skirt adorned with a hundred flowers and butterflies. It was dignified and magnificent, yet still retained the youthful charm of a young girl.

After finishing her makeup, with her eyebrows drawn and floral stickers applied, the Crown Prince arrived.

Ming Xi smiled like a flower and stepped forward to bow.

Xie Pei held her up, his gaze fixed on her, once again realizing that she had married him and was his new bride.

Ming Xi was very satisfied with the Crown Prince's dazzled and somewhat infatuated gaze, "Your Highness has returned."

Xie Pei's heart softened, "Mmm."

"Should Your Highness change clothes before the meal?"

"Alright."

Ming Xi handed him a purple robe and served him as he changed.

Actually, she just held the clothes; Xie Pei did everything himself.

After Xie Pei fastened his belt, Ming Xi saw that his hair was covered by his clothes. She stepped forward to help him arrange it properly.

They were very close, and she was almost nestled in his arms. The girl's fragrance lingered around Xie Pei's nose.

He couldn't help but hold her slender waist, lowering his head to press a kiss on her red lips.

Ming Xi looked up at him. The kissed person didn't blush, but the Crown Prince who had done the kissing had a somewhat evasive look in his eyes, as if he was shy?

Ming Xi blinked, then suddenly stood on her tiptoes and took the initiative to kiss the corner of his lips.

Xie Pei: "..."

Before he could recover, the beloved in his arms had already slipped away like a cloud.

Yu Gonggong and Ying Yu, who had come in to set the table, kept their heads down tightly.

They didn't see, didn't see, didn't see Her Ladyship teasing His Highness.

One thought that it was no wonder she was the one the Crown Prince had been thinking of, she was indeed bold.

The other thought that just because the young lady had appeared quiet and dignified in public these past years, it didn't mean she had forgotten that the young lady had once dressed as a man to follow the heir of the Marquis on a bandit suppression mission. She had even declared with a wave of her hand that she wanted to keep a bunch of male favorites in the future, heroic ones, refined ones, gentle ones, cold ones...

The most composed person in the room was Ting Ruo.

In her eyes, whatever the young lady did was right.

The two of them: "..."

Sometimes, they really envied those who were single-minded. Worries were indeed troublesome.

chapters.title: The Only One He Cares About
chapters.content:
Ming Xi’s courtyard in the Eastern Palace was still called Qionghua Courtyard.

Not just hers, all the side consorts’ and good wives’ courtyards had been renamed to match their family residences.

It was said to be the Crown Prince’s order, to show how much he valued this grand wedding.

Whether true or not, the side consorts and their families behind them all wept with gratitude, praising the imperial grace.

At first, Ming Xi had thought the Crown Prince was quite skilled at balancing favors.

But after the bridal veil was lifted, the more she looked at the bedroom’s decor, the more familiar it seemed.

Apart from the red silk and auspicious characters, wasn’t this exactly the same as her boudoir in the Wuding Marquis’s mansion?

If it were just a name change, it wouldn’t mean much. But to replicate her room’s layout down to the last detail, that was true care.

The antiques on the antique shelf were even more precious, the clothes in the wardrobe more exquisite and numerous, all made of tribute brocade with the latest styles and patterns.

The jewelry on the vanity was exquisitely beautiful, just look at that phoenix-and-flower gold hairpin inlaid with gemstones. Its craftsmanship was so superb that only the imperial family could possess it.

Ming Xi toyed with a snuff bottle in her hand, its painted magpie-on-a-branch design vivid and charming.

Qin Mama smiled and said to her, “Your Highness, this was painted by His Highness himself.”

“Hmm?”

Ming Xi looked at her in surprise.

“Not just this snuff bottle, the jade hairpins, jade pendants, and small seals in your dowry were all carved by His Highness’s own hand.”

Ming Xi: “...”

“Every arrangement in your bedroom was done personally by His Highness. Only for you, Your Highness.”

Qin Mama emphasized the last part.

All the side consorts’ courtyards had been renamed, it was just a distraction, to keep her from becoming the target of public criticism.

The Crown Prince had truly put his heart into this for her.

Ming Xi fell silent.

Even if he wanted to use her to reclaim the Wuding Marquis’s military power, did he really need to go this far?

Though they got along well, tying it to love seemed a bit unrealistic.

Could it be because she was beautiful?

Ming Xi looked at herself in the bronze mirror, her face like a hibiscus, her eyebrows like willow leaves, her lips red, her teeth white, her skin like snow. She was indeed a beauty that few men could resist.

But as a crown prince, what beautiful women couldn’t he have?

Beauty fades with time. If she really thought of herself as just a dish, she wouldn’t last long in the palace.

“Your Highness, look at the magnolia tree outside the window and the date tree in the back courtyard, both were planted by His Highness himself.”

“Front court with jade blossoms in spring, back court with deep-rooted date trees,” Ming Xi chuckled lightly. “Does His Highness also study feng shui?”

Qin Mama laughed, “His Highness normally doesn’t care about such things, but when it comes to you, he does.”

Because he had her in his heart, he wanted everything to be perfect for her. No detail was too small for him to overlook.

So, men weren’t naturally careless, it just depended on how much they cared.

Ming Xi: “...”

She raised an eyebrow and suddenly asked Qin Mama, “Is His Highness going to Consort Feng’s place tonight?”

The Emperor had bestowed two side consorts upon the Crown Prince. One was the daughter of a military noble with power, the Wuding Marquis’s daughter, Ming Xi herself.

The other was the granddaughter of the current Grand Tutor, a scholar from a distinguished literary family; Consort Feng, Feng Yuerong.

Don’t let Grand Tutor Feng’s retirement from court affairs fool you. He was the great Confucian scholar whom the late Empress Dowager had personally invited three times to tutor the Emperor.

Even the Crown Prince had been his student.

How many officials in the Inner Cabinet, the Six Ministries, and local governments were his disciples?

Grand Tutor Feng was undeniably the leader of the pure literary officials.

His granddaughter was naturally qualified to stand on equal footing with a noble lady like Ming Xi from the Marquis’s mansion.

In fact, with their status, either of them could have been the Crown Princess.

However, the position of Crown Princess was coveted by all factions, each refusing to yield.

The Emperor didn’t want to see the court descend into chaos, so he simply didn’t appoint one, leaving the problem to the Crown Prince himself.

Thus, Ming Xi and Feng Yuerong were both made side consorts, one representing the martial, the other the literary, to balance each other.

The other four good wives came from the Shi family of the Censorate, the Qu family of the Ministry of Personnel’s assistant minister, the Zhao family of the Huguang provincial governor, and the Dong family of the Five Armies’ commander.

Because the Ji’an Marquis had been demoted due to his son’s scandal, Dong Liangyuan’s father, originally just a deputy general, had been promoted to full general.

Scholars, generals, and high-ranking officials, the Emperor had provided the Crown Prince with a complete set.

Ming Xi didn’t know whether to marvel at the Emperor’s imperial strategy or to admire his “fatherly love.”

But by tying them and their families to the Crown Prince, the Eastern Palace’s position would undoubtedly become more stable.

After the wedding, the Crown Prince had already spent three consecutive nights in her quarters.

Though Ming Xi didn’t intend to play the role of a virtuous and wise consort, advising the Crown Prince to share his favors equally.

But she also didn’t want to become the seductive consort who monopolized the Crown Prince’s affection.

Speaking of monopolizing affection, Ming Xi wanted to roll her eyes.

Who would believe it? These three nights she and the Crown Prince had spent together were just covering themselves with a blanket and chatting, nothing else had happened.

But if the Crown Prince spent another night here, she feared she would be summoned to the palace for a scolding tomorrow.

If the Crown Prince’s inner quarters caught fire, it would implicate the court, and she and the Wuding Marquis’s family would surely become the target of everyone’s resentment.

With the current unrest at the borders, the Emperor certainly wouldn’t take action against the Wuding Marquis’s family at this time.

But what about later?

A reputation as a “proud and unruly general” would be enough to destroy the Wuding Marquis’s family.

Ming Xi had been racking her brains over how to persuade the Crown Prince to visit another consort’s courtyard tonight.

She hadn’t expected him to be so understanding.

However, Qin Mama seemed to have misunderstood something and kept emphasizing how much the Crown Prince cared for her, as if she wanted to say that Ming Xi was the Crown Prince’s one true love.

Ming Xi found it a bit amusing.

But she couldn’t say that she didn’t mind the Crown Prince favoring other consorts, nor could she appear indifferent.

Where would the Crown Prince’s pride be then?

Qin Mama didn’t know her mistress’s thoughts. When Ming Xi suddenly asked her so bluntly, cold sweat almost slid down her forehead.

If the Crown Prince found out she had upset her mistress with her loose tongue, she would be dead.

Qin Mama’s legs weakened, and she knelt down. “Your Highness, His Highness, he…”

Ming Xi reached out to help her up, lowered her gaze, and her beautiful face couldn’t hide her disappointment as she said softly, “Mama, don’t be afraid. I’m not blaming you. From the moment I received the imperial decree, I understood that His Highness is my husband, but he is not my husband alone.”

“If he has me in his heart, I am already very happy. Some things are not to be desired, nor should they be hoped for.”

Qin Mama looked at the beautiful woman before her, who seemed so disheartened, and opened her mouth, only to lower her voice and say, “Your Highness, love is not important. Favor is what matters most. Only by firmly capturing the prince’s heart can one stand unshaken in the palace.”

Emperors and crown princes focus on the court and the nation. They have little time and attention left for the harem.

The person they want by their side must be understanding, obedient, and vibrant.

Consorts can have small tempers, that’s part of the charm, but they must never make a scene or be unreasonable, or they will only annoy the ruler and eventually be abandoned.

“You can show a little sadness or jealousy in front of His Highness, but you must know your limits. A man’s guilt will bring you more benefits than sweet words ever could.”

---

chapters.title: If She Hit, Then She Hit
chapters.content:
Even though Qin Mama was also moved by the Crown Prince’s care for Consort Ming Xi.

But how long could a ruler’s love last?

New faces replace old ones. Once the Crown Prince ascends the throne, surrounded by countless beauties, will he still treat her mistress the same?

“From the vast waters, taking only a ladle” was nothing but a fantasy in storybooks.

Since ancient times, which emperor didn’t have three palaces and six courtyards?

Ming Xi was slightly stunned. She hadn’t expected Qin Mama to speak so frankly to her.

These were all Qin Mama’s precious experiences and insights from years in the palace, so candid that they bordered on heresy.

Yet she had still shared them with Ming Xi.

She truly liked her mistress and wanted to be loyal to her.

She hoped her mistress could go further and higher.

A genuine smile appeared in Ming Xi’s eyes. “Thank you for your guidance, Mama. I will keep it in mind.”

Qin Mama saw that her mistress had taken her words to heart, and her anxious heart settled.

She believed Consort Ming Xi was a clever person.

“You, come in here!”

Tingyu stormed in, dragging Tingruo into the room and pressing her down to kneel before Ming Xi.

Ming Xi raised an eyebrow. “What happened?”

Tingyu glared fiercely at her stubborn sister. “Your Highness, you have no idea how bold Tingruo is. She almost killed Consort Feng’s head maid in the kitchen!”

Ming Xi: “Hmm?”

Tingyu recounted the whole story.

It turned out that Ming Xi usually had her evening meal earlier, finishing before the Hour of the Rooster.

So, after her afternoon nap, Tingyu and Tingruo had gone to the kitchen to prepare her dinner.

But...

That morning, someone from the Crown Prince’s side had gone to Consort Feng’s place to deliver a message: His Highness would be dining and staying there tonight, so she should prepare well.

Questionzhu Courtyard was as joyful as if it were New Year’s.

Consort Feng had sent her head maid, Qiumei, to the kitchen to order a few more dishes.

Whether Qiumei was truly foolish or simply resentful that Consort Ming Xi had stolen her mistress’s limelight, she had not only spoken sarcastically to Tingyu and Tingruo but had also tried to order the head chef, who was preparing Ming Xi’s dinner, to go help her.

“After all, Consort Ming Xi isn’t attending the bedchamber tonight. What does it matter if her dinner is late?” she had said.

“Don’t delay His Highness’s dinner at Questionzhu Courtyard, that’s the important thing.”

Tingyu and Tingruo had initially ignored Qiumei, not even sparing her a glance.

But Qiumei, thinking they were afraid of her, had gone so far as to knock over Ming Xi’s medicinal meal.

How could Tingruo tolerate that?

If Tingyu hadn’t stopped her in time, Qiumei would have been thrown into a pot of boiling oil by Tingruo.

Tingyu wasn’t as single-minded as her sister. She knew that her mistress was already the thorn in everyone’s eye in the Eastern Palace, with whispers of her being a seductive enchantress.

If the Crown Prince was about to favor Consort Feng, and Consort Ming Xi’s maid beat up Consort Feng’s maid...

What would the Crown Prince think?

What would the entire Eastern Palace think?

What would the nobles and officials in the palace think?

Tingruo pouted, not feeling she had done anything wrong.

Qiumei had deserved it for ruining her mistress’s medicinal meal.

Qin Mama’s expression blanked for a moment, as if she wanted to slap her own forehead.

Ming Xi felt both helpless and amused but didn’t blame Tingruo.

Tingruo was her head maid and represented her dignity.

If she allowed Qiumei to walk all over her and endured it in silence, then anyone in the Eastern Palace could step on her.

Ming Xi checked the time. “Mama Qin, take some medicinal ointment and two bolts of cloud brocade to Questionzhu Courtyard to apologize to Consort Feng. Say that Tingruo acted rashly and injured Qiumei, and I feel terrible about it. I will personally go apologize to Consort Feng tomorrow.”

Qin Mama’s face immediately showed understanding.

At this time, when she returned from Questionzhu Courtyard, she would likely encounter His Highness the Crown Prince.

Upon seeing her, he would surely inquire about the matter and learn that Consort Feng’s people had been rude first.

If any rumors spread in the Eastern Palace, the Crown Prince would only think that his beloved consort had been wronged. He would dislike Consort Feng, thinking her malicious, jealous, and scheming against Consort Ming Xi.

“My mistress is wise. I will go at once.”

Ming Xi: “...”

The first part could have been omitted.

After Qin Mama left to handle the matter, Ming Xi lowered her gaze at Tingruo, her voice soft and gentle. “Anything you want to say?”

Tingruo kowtowed. “This servant accepts whatever punishment my lady deems fit.”

No matter how foolish she was, she knew she had caused trouble for her mistress.

But as long as she was alive, she would never allow anyone to humiliate her mistress.

Ming Xi ordered, “Lift your head.”

Tingruo obediently raised her head. Ming Xi amusedly poked her forehead. “You... If the Empress Dowager or the Queen in the palace speak ill of me in the future, will you hit them too?”

Tingruo pouted. “Lady, I’m not an idiot.”

She knew who she could hit and who she couldn’t.

At most, she’d find an opportunity to secretly poison them.

Ming Xi shook her head with a smile. “Regardless, you did hit someone. I still have to make a show of punishing you. Go kneel in the courtyard for an hour.”

“Tingyu, give her two knee pads.”

Tingruo refused. “Lady, it’s only an hour. There’s no need.”

Ming Xi glanced at her. “Are you the mistress, or am I?”

Tingruo didn’t dare talk back. She tied on the knee pads and obediently went to kneel.

Even though Tingruo was her sister, Tingyu still had to say, “Lady, you spoil her too much.”

They were not just servants but also sworn guards. Everything they did should always prioritize their mistress’s interests and safety.

If Tingruo had acted so impulsively in the past at the Deathsworn Camp, she would have been flayed alive.

This punishment was no punishment at all, how would Tingruo learn her lesson?

Ming Xi chuckled lightly. “I trust Tingruo knows her limits.”

Tingyu: “...”

If she knew her limits, would she have tried to strangle Qiumei and shove her into a pot of boiling oil?

Ming Xi said indifferently, “If Qiumei hadn’t been asking for it, Tingruo wouldn’t have laid a hand on her. If anyone who gets to attend the bedchamber can disregard me, then what’s the point of me being a side consort?”

Tingyu apologized. “It was this servant’s lack of consideration.”

Ming Xi had her rise. “You being cautious isn’t wrong. It’s good that you stopped Tingruo today. We can’t let others bully us, but we also can’t turn the entire Eastern Palace upside down, right?”

Tingyu let out a breath and smiled. “This servant and my sister only listen to your orders, Lady.”

Ming Xi smiled and had her set the table. “Remember to save some food for Tingruo. She won’t be able to sleep tonight if she doesn’t eat.”

Tingyu: “...”

She still thought her lady spoiled Tingruo too much.

Right now, her lady was just a side consort, and Tingruo dared to hit another side consort’s maid. If her lady became a noble consort in the future, or even...

There would be nothing Tingruo wouldn’t dare to do.

This was going to be a headache!

Fortunately, Tingruo was single-minded and took her lady’s words as her creed. She wouldn’t do anything that would truly harm her lady.

chapters.title: Self-Destruction
chapters.content:
In Wen Zhu Yuan, Autumn Mei, with a bruised and swollen face, knelt before Consort Feng, wailing and accusing the people of Qiong Hua Yuan of being unreasonable.

"Your Highness, Consort Ming, relying on the fact that she served the Crown Prince before you, is arrogant and violent. She beats me and doesn't respect you at all. She is jealous and vicious. The Crown Prince is coming to your place tonight, and she immediately gave you a warning!"
