"Your Highness, you must stand up for me! Consort Ming is clearly slapping your face!"

Autumn Xing, who was also a senior maidservant of Consort Feng, hesitated to speak. She knew Autumn Mei's character all too well. There was an 80% chance that Autumn Mei had provoked the incident herself.

But thinking of her own mistress's character... to put it nicely, she was well-read, but to put it bluntly, she was a bookworm who didn't understand worldly affairs and was easily deceived.

Autumn Mei had a sweet mouth, and Consort Feng trusted and liked her more when she was at home.

Sure enough, Consort Feng did not doubt Autumn Mei's words. Her face darkened, and the handkerchief in her hand was almost twisted into a mess.

"How can Consort Ming be such a person? When we were in the boudoir, I clearly heard that she was a noble and dignified lady!"

Moreover, the Crown Prince was not hers alone. How many people could she be jealous of?

Autumn Mei pouted, "The Wu Ding Hou father and son have achieved great merits, and Consort Ming probably doesn't respect anyone. I heard that the seventh young lady of the Lin family (Lin Huai Rou) had previously called her a witch in the Princess's residence. Maybe the Lin family's affairs..."

"Autumn Mei!" Autumn Xing, seeing that Autumn Mei was going too far and involving the previous dynasty's affairs, quickly spoke to stop her.

A servant girl, discussing court politics in the Eastern Palace? Did she really not fear death?

Autumn Mei didn't think she had said anything wrong. She glared at Autumn Xing and wanted to continue inciting Consort Feng against Ming Xi.

"Your Highness, the Qin Gu Gu from Consort Ming's courtyard has arrived."

A palace maid came in to report.

Autumn Mei's face changed, and Consort Feng bit her lip. Although she was very displeased with Ming Xi, if she rejected the person at the door, and the Crown Prince found out, he would definitely think she was an uneducated person.

Moreover, Qin Gu Gu was formerly a palace nurturing matron, and she had to give her some face.

"Let her in."

"Yes."

Qin Gu Gu entered and respectfully saluted Consort Feng.

"Consort Feng, Your Highness, I was ordered to come and apologize to you. It was wrong of Ting Ruo to hit someone just because Autumn Mei criticized my mistress and broke my Consort's medicinal meal. My mistress felt very guilty after knowing this, severely punished Ting Ruo, and sent me with gifts to apologize to you. Tomorrow, she will personally come to apologize to you."

Qin Gu Gu's words made the original cause of the incident clear. Although it seemed like an apology, it was no different from a confrontation.

Consort Feng's face turned red and green with anger. She glared at Autumn Mei, "Is the situation as Gu Gu said?"

Autumn Mei immediately cried out in injustice, but Qin Gu Gu didn't give her a chance to sophisticate. She continued, "If Consort Feng is still angry, my mistress said she would hand Ting Ruo over to the Crown Prince for punishment."

This time, Autumn Mei was truly scared. If the Crown Prince found out, he would definitely uncover everything. Where would she have a life then?

Autumn Mei immediately crawled to Consort Feng's feet, "Your Highness, I... I was also standing up for you. Clearly, you are the Crown Prince's junior fellow apprentice, childhood sweethearts, but..."

"Shut up!" Consort Feng, no matter how foolish, knew she had been used as a pawn by Autumn Mei. The one who lost face was her.

Consort Feng covered her chest, angrily pointing at Autumn Mei, "How dare you!"

Autumn Mei kowtowed repeatedly, "Your Highness, I was wrong, I really know I was wrong."

Consort Feng didn't want to deal with her servants in front of outsiders, feeling it was a loss of face. She could only look at Qin Gu Gu.

"Trouble Gu Gu to go back and tell Sister Ming that it was I who failed to control my servants. Tomorrow, it should be I who goes to apologize to Sister Ming."

"Consort Feng is too kind."

Qin Gu Gu exchanged a few more words with Consort Feng, left the gifts, and departed.

In her heart, she clicked her tongue. This Consort Feng didn't seem very smart!

And what was the Feng family thinking? How could they let someone like Autumn Mei be a part of the dowry into the Eastern Palace?

Did they want Consort Feng to die faster, or was the Feng family getting too arrogant?

On the way back to Qiong Hua Yuan, Qin Gu Gu indeed encountered the Crown Prince's palanquin.

She stood by the roadside and silently bowed respectfully.

"Gu Gu Qin."

The procession suddenly stopped, and Crown Prince Xie Pei lifted the palanquin curtain, looking at Qin Gu Gu by the roadside, feigning ignorance, "Why are you here?"

Qin Gu Gu did not add oil to the fire, but truthfully reported the matter to the Crown Prince.

Xie Pei indifferently said, "Yu En, go and investigate what happened."

Yu Gong quickly accepted the order.

He understood that this so-called "investigation" was to spread the news throughout the Eastern Palace that Consort Feng, who had not yet served the Crown Prince, had become arrogant and allowed her senior maid to bully Consort Ming.

And also to let the news spread to the palace and the court.

To pull Feng Taifu and the Feng family out to be shields for the Wu Ding Hou residence and Consort Ming.

Yu En didn't dare to ask why the Crown Prince, who had once greatly respected Feng Taifu, now seemed to want to eliminate the Feng family as soon as possible.

The master had given the order, and he would carry it out.

Xie Pei then seemingly casually said, "After all, who is the master in Wen Zhu Yuan? I remember there is no Crown Princess in the Eastern Palace yet, right? How can someone bully a Consort?"

"There are still memorials in Wen He Hall that I haven't finished reading. Let's go back first."

The Crown Prince's procession, which had almost arrived at Wen Zhu Yuan, suddenly turned around and left.

Upon learning this, Consort Feng's face turned pale, and she almost couldn't stand steady.

The Feng family had strict etiquette and advocated the teachings of the saints. Consort Feng had been brought up with distorted interpretations of the Three Obediences and Five Constants since she was a child, believing that her husband was her heaven.

Not to mention that Consort Feng had long harbored feelings for the Crown Prince.

If she was abandoned by the Crown Prince, how was that different from the sky falling?

"Autumn Xing, what should I do? What should I do? The Crown Prince must think that I instructed Autumn Mei to bully Consort Ming!"

But she really didn't!

"Your Highness, don't panic. The Crown Prince is not someone who can't distinguish right from wrong. You and Consort Ming have a senior-junior relationship, and for the sake of the Taifu, the Crown Prince won't abandon you."

"Really? Then why did the Crown Prince leave?"

Consort Feng grabbed Autumn Xing as if she was holding onto the last straw.

Autumn Xing comforted her mistress, "The Crown Prince has heavy state affairs. It's normal for him to suddenly return to handle them."

Consort Feng's tears fell, "Is the Crown Prince really not tired of me?"

"Your Highness, rest assured, he won't. But today's incident has given others a handle on you. You must severely punish Autumn Mei to show the Crown Prince that all this has nothing to do with you."

"You cheap slave, what nonsense are you talking about?"

Autumn Mei, who had been cowering, suddenly exploded.

She knew that Autumn Xing, this cheap slave, had always wanted to replace her position. How dare she instigate Consort Feng to punish her!

"Shut up!"

Consort Feng, who had always been easy to deceive and good-tempered in Autumn Mei's eyes, now looked at her with almost hatred.

Autumn Mei was so scared that she fell and sat on the ground, a cold chill rising in her heart.

---

chapters.title: The Crown Prince's Sneaky Visit
chapters.content:
The news of Consort Feng causing trouble before even serving the Crown Prince quickly spread throughout the Eastern Palace.

The four good ladies had different reactions, but they all shared the same thought: Was Consort Feng perhaps a fool?

Consort Ming, who was the first to receive favor, had been so low-key that she didn't cause any trouble for anyone.

Consort Feng hadn't even served the Crown Prince yet, and her tail was already sticking up in the air?

Shi Yuan's expression was somewhat thought-provoking.

This Feng Yuerong was the same as in her previous life, not very smart.

In her past life, Feng Yuerong had married Prince Qi.

After Prince Qi usurped the throne, the entire capital knew about his affair with Concubine Su Qing Er, but Feng Yuerong was the only one who didn't.

However, because Prince Qi needed the Feng family to stabilize the court and win over the scholars of the world, Feng Yuerong's position had always been secure.

So, some people, even if they didn't have brains, as long as they had a good family background, their fate would be good.

But Feng Yuerong should never have provoked Ming Xi.

That woman was a beautiful poisonous snake, pretending to be pure, kind, and gentle in front of the Crown Prince. But whoever dared to provoke her would be bitten to death.

In her previous life, she had dominated the harem, and even someone as vicious as Xiao Ming Zhu had been made to cry for her father and mother by her, forced to avoid her. Even the two empress dowagers didn't want to clash with her directly.

A fool like Feng Yuerong would be easily manipulated by Ming Xi.

"Good Lady, since Consort Feng has been abandoned by the Crown Prince, why don't you..."

Shi Yuan coldly looked at her own maid, "Do you think your mistress doesn't die fast enough?"

If the two consorts were fighting, anyone who joined in now would suffer.

Moreover, without absolute certainty, Shi Yuan temporarily didn't want to expose herself to Ming Xi.

Thinking of that woman's methods, even though Shi Yuan hated her, she couldn't help but feel a hint of fear.

"In the Eastern Palace, remember to be cautious in your words and actions, so you don't end up like Autumn Mei, not even knowing how you died."

"S-Slave... Slave will heed the Good Lady's teachings."

Shi Yuan no longer paid attention to her trembling maid, turning her head to look at the gradually darkening sky.

The Crown Prince would surely have some complaints about Consort Feng for today's incident, but he was a man who valued rules and etiquette the most.

He would definitely still visit Consort Feng tonight to maintain the balance in the Eastern Palace's inner court.

...

The Crown Prince reviewed memorials until nightfall, with no intention of going to the rear court.

It was only when Consort Feng, along with Autumn Mei, came personally to apologize that the Crown Prince's expression softened, and he took her back to Wen Zhu Yuan for dinner.

As for Autumn Mei, the Crown Prince gave Consort Feng face and let her handle the matter herself.

Consort Feng immediately ordered Autumn Mei to be dragged away and given thirty heavy bamboo strokes, which killed her on the spot.

In Qiong Hua Yuan, all the palace servants were extremely careful tonight, fearing that they might accidentally upset their mistress further.

Although they had only served Consort Ming for three days, they all genuinely liked their mistress.

She was generous with rewards, had a good temper, and even though the Crown Prince had gone to Consort Feng's place today and their mistress was unhappy, she hadn't lost her temper or made things difficult for them.

Looking at Ting Ruo, who had caused such a big disaster, their mistress had only punished her by making her kneel, and even took out the precious Yun Jin brocade to help her cover up...

Gu Gu Qin had warned them that as long as they followed the rules and were loyal, their mistress would truly protect them when needed.

Who wouldn't like a mistress who valued the lives of her servants as much as her own?

Ming Xi, seeing that everyone was being so cautious around her tonight, felt a bit helpless and simply let them all go to rest early, keeping only Ting Ruo and Ting Yu to attend to her.

It was late at night, and Ming Xi, after washing up, was about to go to sleep.

She had just approached the bed when a rustling sound came from the bed.

"Who is it!"

Ting Ruo and Ting Yu drew their soft swords from their waists and stood in front of Ming Xi.

"It's me."

The bedding was lifted, and the Crown Prince, who was supposed to be at Wen Zhu Yuan with Consort Feng, emerged from under Ming Xi's bed, looking fresh and lively.

Ting Ruo and Ting Yu were completely stunned.

Ming Xi's face also rarely showed a blank expression.

All three, master and servants, suspected they were dreaming.

Xie Pei emerged from the secret passage, coughed awkwardly with his fist against his nose, "Xi'er, did I scare you?"

Ming Xi blinked, then blinked again. Suddenly, she stepped forward and hugged the Crown Prince's slender waist, her voice soft and aggrieved, "Your Highness."

Ting Ruo and Ting Yu: "...Ah, they've eloped!"

Xie Pei's entire focus was on the person in his arms; he had no attention to spare for anyone else.

He gently embraced her, "I'm sorry, I made you sad."

Ming Xi shook her head, "No, it's fine now that you're here."

Xie Pei lowered his head to look into her eyes, gently cupping her small face, and said word by word, "Xi'er, I am useless. I can only allow those women to enter the Eastern Palace. What I can do is swear to you that, both in body and mind, I will only have you. It was true in the past, it is true now, and it will be true in the future."

Ming Xi's eyes widened slightly. It would be a lie to say she wasn't shocked.

She never expected the Crown Prince to make such a vow to her.

Did he understand what this represented?

Ming Xi gently rubbed her cheek against his palm, "I believe you, Your Highness."

Xie Pei, seeing her unconditional trust in him, had an expression so tender it could drip water.

He kissed her forehead almost reverently, "Xi'er, I will not let you down."

He would never let her be disappointed in him again.

The girl shyly lowered her eyes, affectionately nestling in his arms.

"Your Highness, I'll have someone prepare water for you to wash up."

"It's better if fewer people know I'm here."

Xie Pei whispered in her ear, "I'll use the water you've already used."

Ming Xi's face turned red, her eyes shimmering, "It's all cold now."

Xie Pei ruffled her hair, his voice hoarse with laughter, "It's fine."

After Xie Pei went to the washroom, the shy and tender look in Ming Xi's eyes faded as she silently looked at the messy bed.

She didn't delve too much into the underground passage. The Crown Prince was not a fool. For something as dangerous and confidential as a secret passage, he would control it perfectly.

Even if Ming Xi wanted to mind, she didn't have the ability to do so now.

What she was pondering was that the first step of her plan after entering the palace was indeed to make the Crown Prince care for and value her.

But she hadn't even put in much effort, and the Crown Prince had already eagerly taken the bait.

Wasn't this success a bit too easy?

The future was unpredictable, and vows and promises were empty words.

Regardless of whether it was because of the military power held by her father and brother that the Crown Prince spoke such sweet words to her, at least it could be confirmed that he genuinely valued her now.

This was her foundation for standing firm in the Eastern Palace.

So, forget about just hitting Consort Feng's maid; even if Ming Xi had beaten Consort Feng half to death, the Crown Prince would still help her settle the matter.

Ming Xi thought about this and felt a surge of satisfaction, her opinion of the Crown Prince improving once again.

As for the Crown Prince's hidden purposes and ambitions?

What was there for Ming Xi to fear?

As long as she ensured that the bargaining chips remained in her hands, wasn't that enough?

If one day the Crown Prince wanted to kill the donkey after it had served its purpose, Ming Xi would make sure he knew that neither she nor her brother were easy targets.

chapters.title: Showing Off Favor
chapters.content:
Ming Xi leaned against the edge of the bed and soon grew drowsy.

Before she knew it, her body tilted and she fell into a broad embrace. Ming Xi woke up, her sleepy eyes gazing at him as she softly called, "Your Highness."

Xie Pei had already remade the bed and was holding her as he lay down.

The girl suddenly stretched out her pair of snow-white, boneless arms and weakly wrapped them around his neck. "Why is Your Highness so good to me?"

Xie Pei's body instantly tensed like a drawn bow. His thin lips restrainedly pressed against her forehead once. "It's late. Xi'er should sleep."

Ming Xi pouted slightly, as if aggrieved. "I thought Your Highness wouldn't let me attend to you in bed and would instead favor Consort Feng again. Maybe you don't like me."

"Nonsense!" Xie Pei lightly pinched her small face. "Don't compare yourself to her."

Feng Yuerong was not even worthy!

Ming Xi huffed, pouting at him for the first time. "Am I not as good as her?"

Xie Pei showed no impatience, only helpless indulgence. "Xi'er knows I didn't mean that."

The girl seemed easily satisfied. She smiled brightly and snuggled into his arms. "Your Highness, I like you."

Xie Pei: "..."

The Crown Prince's heartbeat nearly exceeded its limit, his neck and ears flushing red.

His Adam's apple rolled with difficulty, his voice growing hoarser. "Xi'er... should sleep, okay?"

If this continued, Xie Pei wasn't sure if he could stop himself from turning into a beast.

Ming Xi restrained the mischief in her heart, her dark eyes clear and innocent as she looked at him.

Xie Pei couldn't help but feel a pang of guilt. His thoughts about her were too impure.

To prevent the Crown Prince from developing any issues, Ming Xi decided not to tease him further.

She covered her mouth and yawned. "Your Highness, I'm sleepy."

Xie Pei silently calmed himself, stroking her hair as he softly coaxed her. "Sleep. I'm here."

...

The next morning, when Ming Xi woke up, the Crown Prince had already left.

Ting Yu kept her head down, daring neither to mention nor ask anything.

On the other hand, Ting Ruo, who was slowly handing a skirt to her mistress, leisurely said, "This servant heard early in the morning that the Bamboo Courtyard called for water three times last night."

"Cough, cough…"

Ming Xi almost choked on her mouthwash.

Qin Gu Gu worriedly patted her mistress's back, scolding, "Ting Ruo, what nonsense are you spouting?"

Ting Ruo glanced at Qin Gu Gu, then lowered her head to focus on the exquisite embroidery on the mistress's skirt.

Qin Gu Gu: "..."

What did this foolish girl mean?

Ting Yu looked everywhere but at Qin Gu Gu.

Qin Gu Gu: "?"

Ming Xi's lips twitched slightly. "I'm hungry. Gu Gu, please arrange breakfast for me."

"Yes, Your Highness."

Before Ming Xi could finish her breakfast, Consort Feng arrived.

To ensure that yesterday's incident was completely forgotten by the Crown Prince and to demonstrate her virtue, even if it was just a pretense; Consort Feng had to come and apologize to Ming Xi.

"Sister Ming, why are you just eating breakfast now?"

In the Great Zhou's harem, concubines addressed each other as "sister" based on rank, with higher-ranking ones calling lower-ranking ones "younger sister." For those of the same rank, seniority was considered.

For those of the same rank and seniority, unless they were truly close, they usually addressed each other by their titles.

After all, no one wanted to be outranked, right?

By calling Ming Xi "younger sister," wasn't Consort Feng implying that Ming Xi was of lower status than her?

Ting Ruo rolled her eyes without any restraint. Anyway, everyone in the Eastern Palace now knew she was both fierce and reckless; any action she took wasn't surprising.

"Consort Feng, my mistress and you are both side consorts of the Eastern Palace, and you seem to be the same age, right?"

Who was she calling "younger sister"?

Did she really think she was the mistress of the Eastern Palace?

Did the Emperor and the Crown Prince agree to that?

Consort Feng's face stiffened.

"Ting Ruo, do not be rude." Ming Xi reprimanded Ting Ruo lightly, then smiled gently at Consort Feng. "My maid is straightforward and speaks her mind. She means no harm. Please do not take offense, Consort Feng."

This was still considered no harm?

If this were the Feng family, such a maid would have been dragged out and beaten to death long ago.

Consort Feng forced a smile, feeling very wronged, but she had to endure it.

Could she go over Ming Xi's head to punish Ting Ruo or complain to the Crown Prince?

Wouldn't that make all her efforts from last night until now go to waste?

Ming Xi raised her hand. "Consort Feng, please have a seat. Ting Yu, serve tea."

Consort Feng looked at the food on the table and once again felt disdain for Side Consort Ming's rudeness and lack of manners.

If it were her family's daughters-in-law still in bed at this time, they would have been disciplined by their grandmother with family rules.

A woman should be knowledgeable, virtuous, and dignified. How could she sleep in? And how could she receive guests like this?

Ah, well, Marquis Wu Ding and his son were military officers, rough and uneducated men. The mistress of the Marquis's residence was also an absurd person. Perhaps no one had taught Side Consort Ming proper etiquette since she was young.

Consort Feng couldn't help but glance at Ming Xi's overly enchanting appearance, feeling even more uncomfortable.

Her grandfather and grandmother had said that the most important thing for a woman was to be gentle and proper, suitable for family harmony, and not to be fox-like and seductive.

Side Consort Ming's appearance and figure looked like that of someone who couldn't stay content at home.

What if she seduced His Highness? That would be terrible.

Consort Feng, supported by her maid's hand, sat down with a posture that seemed measured by a ruler, as if to make Ming Xi feel ashamed of herself.

She picked up the tea, slightly lowered her head, and subtly revealed a hint of red marks under her collar.

Ming Xi: "..."

Ah, her curiosity was about to explode! What should she do?

What exactly happened last night?

It couldn't be what she was thinking, right?

If it was... tsk tsk, the Crown Prince was truly a marvel of the world!

After Consort Feng finished her "show-off," she put down the teacup without drinking and, in a tone as if it was for Ming Xi's own good, educated her:

"The early morning hours are precious. Side Consort Ming should really get up earlier in the future."

Upon hearing this, Ming Xi couldn't help but laugh.

She looked at Consort Feng with amusement. How could the Feng family have the heart to let her enter the palace?

"I have had a weak constitution since I was young. His Majesty, in his grace, ordered the Chief Physician of the Imperial Hospital, Physician Wen, to treat me. Physician Wen prescribed a medicinal diet for me and instructed me not to overexert myself. I must get enough sleep every day, otherwise it might affect my lifespan."

So, by asking her to wake up early, did Consort Feng want her to die sooner?

How malicious could that be?

Consort Feng's face stiffened again. She quickly said, "This consort did not mean that..."

"I naturally believe that Consort Feng did not intend to harm me. Alas, it's all my fault for having such a frail body. His Highness is kind and tolerant, not minding my lack of discipline and letting me prioritize my health. But my heart truly aches..."

Ming Xi's exquisite little face darkened, her eyes welling up with tears as she looked weak and helpless, as if she had been greatly wronged.

Consort Feng: "..."

Seeing that Ming Xi was about to faint from sadness, Consort Feng felt her scalp tingling.

If His Highness found out that she had upset Side Consort Ming to the point of illness again today, he would surely not trust her anymore.

Perhaps he would even, under Side Consort Ming's instigation, consider her a vicious woman.

Consort Feng couldn't sit still any longer. She quickly found an excuse to leave, no longer carrying the smug demeanor she had when she arrived.

Ming Xi dropped the handkerchief in her hand, her face showing no trace of the earlier sadness or weakness.

Ting Ruo couldn't help but roll her eyes again. "What kind of person is that?"

chapters.title: Why Must Your Highness Make Things Difficult for His Subordinates
chapters.content:
This time, even Qin Gu Gu didn't reprimand Ting Ruo for her lack of manners.

Even a fool could see that Consort Feng had come under the pretense of apologizing to their mistress, but in reality, she was here to flaunt the Crown Prince's favor from last night and to assert her dominance over their mistress.

But they were both side consorts. Consort Feng's turn to attend to the Crown Prince was still after Side Consort Ming's.

Where did she get the nerve to act like the mistress?

Qin Gu Gu murmured, "They say the Feng family women are refined and literate, with the grace of orchids and the heart of a scholar."

And this was the result?

After yesterday and this morning, Qin Gu Gu's rose-tinted glasses for the Feng family were completely shattered.

Ming Xi smiled. In the capital, which powerful and influential family didn't have a public persona?

Wasn't she the same?

The truth was known only to themselves.

Qin Gu Gu worried that her mistress might be upset. "Your Highness, your body is weak. His Highness pities you too much..."

As the chief maid of the Qiong Hua Courtyard, how could Qin Gu Gu not know that His Highness and her mistress had not truly consummated their marriage?

But last night, His Highness had "favored" Consort Feng three times.

If it were her, she would have wild thoughts too.

Ming Xi, who had "stolen" a night with the Crown Prince the previous evening, bit her lip to suppress her smile.

"Gu Gu, I really am fine and won't overthink it."

Seeing that her mistress genuinely didn't seem upset, Qin Gu Gu, though somewhat doubtful, was mostly relieved.

With her mistress's intelligence and schemes, her future was bound to be limitless.

As for someone like Consort Feng?

Ten of her wouldn't be enough for her mistress to play with.

...

The morning "uproar" at the Qiong Hua Courtyard soon reached the Crown Prince's ears.

Xie Pei let out a cold laugh. "Since she likes getting up early so much, tell Ying San that from now on, he is to go to the Bamboo Courtyard and rise at the Chou hour (1-3 AM)."

"Yes, Your Highness."

Eunuch Yu lowered his head, truly unable to understand why Consort Feng had so many tricks up her sleeve.

The mistress at Qiong Hua Courtyard was the apple of His Highness's eye. His Highness had gone to great lengths to protect her so thoroughly. How could Consort Feng dare to provoke her?

If it weren't for the fact that the Eastern Palace wasn't in a position to openly strike against the Feng family, Consort Feng would have been sent to hell long ago.

Xie Pei looked at the verbose memorial in his hands, submitted by an official from the Feng faction.

In his previous life, during the first selection of show girls after his ascension, Feng Yuerong had also been selected.

Out of respect for Grand Tutor Feng, he had directly granted her the position of consort, which was higher than the initial rank of Zhaoyi that Xi'er had held.

However, on the night before Feng Yuerong entered the palace, she was discovered to have eloped with Xie Yi.

Grand Tutor Feng had come to him in tears to plead for forgiveness. Although Xie Pei had been angry, he hadn't truly blamed anyone and had even bestowed marriage upon Xie Yi and Feng Yuerong.

But somehow, it had turned into a rumor that he was cruel and heartless, attempting to forcibly take his brother's wife.

And what about Grand Tutor Feng, whom he had respected the most?

During the palace coup, he had come forward to accuse Xie Pei of usurping the throne, claiming that the late emperor had passed the throne to Prince Qi, Xie Yi.

If Xie Pei hadn't been the one personally present when the late emperor closed his eyes, he might have doubted that he was indeed the usurper of the imperial decree.

Later, when he and Xi'er were imprisoned at the Nine Turns Pool, Feng Yuerong had even come to taunt them.

She had said that he had wronged her, destroyed her lifelong happiness, and made her life not worth living, so he deserved his current fate.

What Xie Pei hated the most was Feng Yuerong's humiliation of Ming Xi.

At that time, Xi'er had finally managed to exchange her last piece of jewelry for some food, only for Feng Yuerong to scatter it on the ground.

To this day, Xie Pei didn't dare to recall how helpless and heartbroken Xi'er had been.

But Feng Yuerong had gone even further, slapping Xi'er and cursing her as a fox spirit reincarnated.

The more Xie Pei recalled, the more sinister and terrifying the killing intent in his eyes became.

"Yu En, pass an order to Ying San. Tonight, he is to break both of Feng Yuerong's hands."

Eunuch Yu hastily complied.

He didn't dare to dwell on or question His Highness's seemingly mad actions.

Recalling when Ying San had first received this task, he had been scared out of his wits.

Ying San was skilled in disguise and often carried out missions that required impersonation.

When necessary, he had also frequented brothels many times.

He wasn't restrained when it came to matters of love between men and women.

But he was just a flirt, not someone with a death wish.

How dare he have designs on the women of the Crown Prince's harem?

The Crown Prince had only coldly stated, "This is an order. Also, they are not my women."

His wife was only Xi'er.

The others were merely pawns.

Who cared about the purity and feelings of a pawn?

If it was broken, it could be discarded and replaced with another.

The Crown Prince looked at Ying San, who was still in shocked doubt, with a smile that wasn't quite a smile. "Rest assured, you are much more important than those women. As long as you do not betray me, I have no need to harm you over such a small matter. I will allow you to live."

Ying San: "..."

That didn't reassure him... not at all!

Your Highness, was this really necessary?

Even if you only considered those women as pawns, couldn't you have done it yourself? You're a grown man; it's not like you'd lose out.

Why make things difficult for your subordinate?

The Crown Prince glanced at him. "Is my purity not also purity?"

Ying San: "..."

What about his purity then?

Oh, right, his purity had been lost eight hundred years ago.

Ying San trembled as he asked, "Should this subordinate take some sterilization medicine first?"

The Crown Prince: "I'm not that cruel to my own subordinates."

Ying San: "..."

No, Your Highness, please be cruel!

Ying San's mind was beyond the expression of "what the hell."

He truly didn't dare to imagine what His Highness intended to do.

Didn't His Highness fear that the royal ancestors would lift their coffin lids in the middle of the night?

The Crown Prince's dark eyes narrowed slightly. "If you can make Consort Feng pregnant, it would also count as a meritorious deed."

Ying San: "..."

He suddenly felt that life had no meaning. What should he do?

In the end, even if Ying San had to walk on eggshells and tightropes, he had to harden his head and go defile the imperial harem.

Yu En expressed deep sympathy for Ying San.

Moreover, not only did Ying San have to risk his life impersonating His Highness, but His Highness also had demands for that matter.

For example, last night he had to call for water three times, and tonight he had to break Consort Feng's hands.

Yu En had never been so grateful that he had been castrated early and was no longer a complete man.

Otherwise, if it were him, he might have immediately taken a knife to castrate himself to prove his loyalty.

Ying San: "..." Was it that he didn't want to?

But he was a special assassin trained by the Crown Prince. Obeying his master's orders without question was ingrained in his bones.

Not to mention just this "small matter," even if it were climbing a mountain of knives or jumping into a vat of oil, he would do so without hesitation.

...

Tonight, it was Consort Feng's turn to attend to the Crown Prince again.

In the middle of the night, the Bamboo Courtyard suddenly fell into chaos.

It turned out that Consort Feng, while attending to the Crown Prince, had been too imprudent and ended up breaking her own hands.

The "Crown Prince's" interest was interrupted, but instead of blaming Consort Feng, he made a big show of calling for the imperial physician.

The commotion kept the entire Eastern Palace awake.

The expressions of the four good ladies were quite colorful. Some were indifferent, while others were so jealous that they tore their handkerchiefs to shreds, tossing and turning in bed, unable to sleep.

The only calm place was the Qiong Hua Courtyard.

After the night watch palace servant gathered the news, they only secretly spat at the Bamboo Courtyard and did not disturb their mistress's sleep.

Ting Yu had already ordered them not to disturb Her Highness's rest at night unless it was extremely urgent, as her mistress had a weak body and needed her sleep.

chapters.title: Beneath the Favor
chapters.content:
Ming Xi only learned of this matter when she woke up early in the morning.

Her red lips twitched slightly, and she couldn't help but glance at the pillow.

Beneath it lay a jade pendant of a dragon coiling around a treasure.

Last night, His Highness the Crown Prince had emerged from under her bed right on time.

During the night, as he held her on his lap and talked, she had unconsciously played with the jade pendant at his waist.

She hadn’t expected him to leave it by her pillow before departing this morning.

Ming Xi lowered her gaze and smiled softly. Did he not fear being discovered by Aunt Qin and the others?

Well, this was the Eastern Palace, his territory.

Still, Ming Xi tucked the pendant under the pillow before Aunt Qin entered.

It wasn’t that she didn’t trust Aunt Qin.

But the idea of the Crown Prince secretly meeting his concubine every night was absurd no matter how you looked at it.

Moreover, there was another "Crown Prince" in Wen Zhu Yuan.

Some things were better kept known by as few people as possible.

After all, the Crown Prince had yet to ascend the throne; the Emperor still loomed above him.

" Aunt Qin, later you will go to the storeroom, select some tonics, and send them to Wen Zhu Yuan to visit Concubine Feng on my behalf."

"Yes."

Aunt Qin saw that the Crown Princess’s mood hadn’t been affected by the matters of Wen Zhu Yuan. She let out a sigh of relief, but couldn’t help feeling a pang of sympathy for her mistress.

Wasn’t it common for emperors to have three palaces and six courts? Which powerful family in the capital didn’t have men with multiple wives and concubines?

This was a hurdle the Crown Princess would have to overcome and get used to sooner or later.

Ting Yu glanced at Aunt Qin, feeling a bit numb.

Sometimes knowing too much wasn’t a good thing!

Ting Ruo, on the other hand, stood like a wooden post beside her mistress, doing whatever she was told.

Ignorance was bliss!

...

The commotion in the Eastern Palace in the middle of the night had spread through the palace by early morning. Everyone who needed to know was aware.

The Empress directly smashed her teacup. "I originally thought that the girl from the Wu Ding Marquis’s residence was too beautiful, destined to be a vixen seducing the master. But I never expected the real fox spirit to be someone else entirely."

"What a virtuous and gentle woman from the Feng family! What a scholarly and noble Feng family!"

Xiao Mingzhu, who had come to the palace to pay respects to the Empress and try to find opportunities to get close to the Crown Prince, didn’t look pleased either.

After a long and forceful argument with the system, it had reluctantly agreed that as long as she successfully conquered the main villain, the difficulty of conquering the male lead could be appropriately reduced.

That is, as long as the male lead’s favorability toward her was sufficient, she wouldn’t need to sleep with him.

Just thinking about the male lead and the old man... Xiao Mingzhu suffered from PTSD.

For now, Xiao Mingzhu had no feelings toward the male lead.

Xiao Mingzhu already considered the Crown Prince as her possession.

Hearing that he favored another woman, and making such a big scene about it, how could Xiao Mingzhu be in a good mood?

She gritted her teeth, clutching the handkerchief in her hand.

In the original book, wasn’t Xie Pei the one who liked Ming Xi the most?

How had it now become that brainless Feng Yuerong?

Well, the plot had long since gone off the rails because of her crossing into the book. It wasn’t strange that the main villain had changed his taste.

Originally, Xiao Mingzhu had planned to learn from Ming Xi, pretending to be a charming and domineering little woman to seduce Xie Pei.

But now he liked the gentle and virtuous type?

This was so annoying!

"System, you can even bring me into a book, why can’t you add two or three years to my age?"

That way, she could marry into the Eastern Palace.

How was a twelve-year-old girl, who hadn’t even fully developed, supposed to conquer the main villain?

【... The system isn’t an all-powerful wish-granting tortoise. Please overcome the difficulties and complete the task yourself, host.】

Xiao Mingzhu rolled her eyes.

But if she couldn’t marry the Crown Prince, couldn’t she at least deal with one of the women in the Eastern Palace?

Xiao Mingzhu immediately instigated the Empress to deal with that cheap woman, Feng Yuerong.

The Empress looked helplessly at her niece.

"The Crown Prince has only been married for a short time. It’s not like I can punish someone just because he slightly favors a woman. If word spreads to His Majesty, the Empress Dowager, and the officials, what will they think?"

Xiao Mingzhu pouted. Her aunt, the Empress, was being too cautious.

Did a mother-in-law need a reason to deal with her daughter-in-law?

In her family, didn’t her mother torment her daughters-in-law every day?

Did they dare say a word?

Empress: "..."

Could the little daughters-in-law of the Enguo Duke’s residence be compared to the Crown Prince’s concubine?

Feng Yuerong had the backing of Grand Tutor Feng.

A great Confucian scholar respected even by the Empress Dowager!

However, the Empress narrowed her eyes.

The Feng family had always prided itself on being a noble and honorable family, placing great importance on propriety and moral integrity. Now, they had raised a shameless daughter who seduced the heir to the throne.

What crime did that deserve?

"The censors dislike nothing more than women in the harem seducing the master. I will have someone push from behind, impeaching the Feng family and Concubine Feng to the death. By then, they will have enough to drink from the cup of suffering."

Xiao Mingzhu’s eyes lit up. "Aunt, you’re amazing."

The Empress poked her forehead. "You are just too reckless. The harem is not a place for direct confrontation. There will be plenty of opportunities for you to suffer in the future."

Xiao Mingzhu hugged the Empress’s arm, acting cute. "Aunt is now the Empress, and in the future, the Empress Dowager. As long as Pearl relies on Aunt and listens to Aunt, what is there to fear?"

The Empress was amused by Xiao Mingzhu’s coaxing.

"Sigh, if only you were a little older. Otherwise, what could those women in the Eastern Palace do?"

Xiao Mingzhu: "..."

Wasn’t that what she was thinking?

Ugh, so infuriating!

...

Actually, the Empress didn’t need to do anything. Memorials impeaching the Feng family and Concubine Feng had already piled up on the Emperor’s desk.

The Emperor had a bit of a headache.

He hadn’t expected his usually indifferent and saintly eldest son to cause such a commotion right after marrying.

But men, you know!

It wasn’t really a big deal, but it just happened to be a woman from the Feng family.

Grand Tutor Feng was highly respected and virtuous. How had he raised such an immodest granddaughter?

The Emperor’s admiration for the Feng family had also diminished somewhat.

Just as he was thinking about how to deal with Concubine Feng, the chief eunuch entered to report that Grand Tutor Feng had come to the palace to plead for forgiveness.

The Emperor was startled and quickly got up to greet him.

After all, he was his teacher, and the Emperor had to give him some face.

In the end, the Emperor only gave a light punishment: Confine Concubine Feng for a month and order her to copy the "Admonitions for Women" a hundred times.

As for how Concubine Feng, with both hands broken, would copy the books, that was not something the Emperor needed to consider.

In the Eastern Palace, Concubine Feng, upon learning that she had been impeached by the censors and punished by His Majesty with confinement and copying scriptures, felt her vision go black and cried in grievance.

She cared most about her reputation. After marrying into the Eastern Palace, she had vowed to be a virtuous wife and good mother.

Who would have thought she’d now be labeled as a woman who seduced the heir?

How could she accept this?

The "Crown Prince" gently comforted her, and that night, he continued to stay in Wen Zhu Yuan to keep her company.

Concubine Feng was so moved that she wished she could dig out her heart and give it to "His Highness the Crown Prince."

But those inside and outside the palace, upon hearing this, could only sneer.

What a Feng family that refused to conform to the world! What a Grand Tutor Feng with such thick virtue and flowing light!

Grand Tutor Feng was also so angry with his granddaughter, who had caused trouble instead of achieving anything, that he nearly had a stroke.

Had she forgotten all the teachings he had given her?

At this point, no matter what, she had to advise the Crown Prince to visit other concubines.

With both hands broken and punished, how dare she still host the Crown Prince?

His reputation, built up over many years, was about to be ruined by this granddaughter.

However, although the Feng family was being pointed at and criticized, it was not enough to cause them serious harm.

On the contrary, the more the Crown Prince favored Concubine Feng, the more popular the Feng family became.

Who knew, perhaps when the Crown Prince ascended the throne, the Feng family would produce an empress.

---

chapters.title: Competing for Favor
chapters.content:
Xie Pei casually flipped through the intelligence reports handed to him by Lu Ming, the corners of his thin lips curling up, though the smile did not reach his eyes.

"Even before I become emperor, they’ve already started taking sides and forming factions."

As soon as these words were spoken, Yu En immediately knelt down.

The Feng family was to be eliminated, but not now.

Before he ascended the throne and stabilized the court, the Feng family still had its uses.

However, the Feng family shouldn’t think they could stay in the background like saints, reaping the benefits as they did in the previous life.

Reputation was a double-edged sword, it could elevate the Feng family to the altar or drag them into hell.

Once the highly respected Grand Tutor Feng was no longer respected, the Feng family would be like a castle in the air. In the future, whenever Xie Pei wanted, he could make them collapse at any time.

Xie Pei leaned lazily against the rocking chair, his handsome face and painted-like brows and eyes making him look as beautiful as a god.

"Climbing high only makes the fall harder. Let the Feng family climb higher first."

When they thought wealth and honor were within their grasp, he would make them suffer an irreversible downfall. He believed Grand Tutor Feng’s expression would be quite spectacular.

Just like in the previous life, when he heard Grand Tutor Feng distorting the facts, accusing him of patricide and usurping the throne.

"Yu En."

"Your servant is here."

"Under the pretense of learning to manage palace affairs, find a few boxes of discarded account books and have Concubine Feng work on them carefully. If she can’t balance them correctly, she must keep trying until she does. Tell her that in a month, I will test her."

"...Yes, your servant will do it immediately."

With Concubine Feng’s hands broken, she had to copy books and now also learn accounting.

Moreover, according to the intelligence from the Feng family’s informants, Concubine Feng... was not good at math.

No one dared imagine how she would get through this month.

But who told her to say in front of that Crown Princess that "a day’s plan lies in the morning," acting so diligent and virtuous? She might as well not sleep at all.

"Where is Master Yu going?"

"Your servant is going to pay respects to Her Highness."

Yu had just walked out of Wen He Hall when he saw Ming Xi coming with her servants.

He quickly stepped forward to pay his respects.

Ming Xi smiled. "No need for such formalities, Master Yu. Is His Highness inside?"

"Yes, yes. This servant will lead you in."

"No need to announce?"

"No need. Please, Your Highness."

When Ming Xi entered, Xie Pei was impatiently tossing aside an overly verbose memorial.

Emperor Taizu of the Great Zhou had once reformed this issue, requiring officials to write memorials concisely.

However, as time passed and the dynasty developed, the bureaucratic system became increasingly cumbersome. Various factions fought chaotically, each person with countless schemes. Memorials had become increasingly verbose and complex, long-winded flattery mixed with subtle slander.

Genuine discussions of practical matters or suggestions beneficial to the country and people were either absent or reduced to a few brief lines.

The Emperor grew increasingly impatient with reading these and simply passed them to the Grand Secretariat.

This allowed the Grand Secretariat and the scholar-official faction to grow in power.

In his previous life, after ascending the throne, Xie Pei had taken steps to reform this, reclaiming power and weakening the Grand Secretariat. As a result, he had offended the entire scholar-official faction.

In the end, the mighty Son of Heaven was schemed against to such an extent.

Xie Pei found it all utterly ridiculous now.

The memorial flew to Ming Xi’s feet. She looked up at the Crown Prince sitting in the rocking chair.

It was a cold and sinister expression she had never seen before, like a fierce beast ready to pounce on someone at any moment.

Ming Xi felt a moment of disorientation.

Although she had never forgotten the Crown Prince’s status as a ruler, he had always treated her with extreme gentleness, completely without airs or temper, sometimes even shy and adorable like a young man experiencing first love.

Unknowingly, she seemed to have underestimated the danger posed by His Highness, the Crown Prince.

It was at this moment that Ming Xi suddenly realized:

Xie Pei had not been born the Crown Prince.

His position as heir was something he had fought and killed for.

At the age of fifteen, he had led eight hundred cavalrymen in a surprise attack on the Xirong capital, killing thousands of Xirong royals and forcing the Xirong king, who had stationed troops at the Great Zhou border, to hastily retreat to save his capital.

He then consecutively defeated the Xirong king’s frenzied attacks three times, annihilating one hundred thousand elite Xirong soldiers and beheading the Xirong king, whose head was sent directly to the capital.

He had crushed the Xirong’s ambitions of eastward expansion, ultimately forcing them to cede territory and pay reparations in humiliation.

After being established as Crown Prince, Xie Pei had never led troops into battle again. He had restrained his murderous aura, becoming the benevolent heir praised by the entire court.

To the point where now, many people had almost forgotten that this man was the Jade-Faced King of Hell feared by the Xirong barbarians, a Crown Prince who had risen from the battlefield, his hands stained with the blood of countless enemies.

Her elder brother had once said that as long as the Crown Prince lived, the Xirong would never dare invade the Great Zhou again.

Her elder brother had also said that in his later campaigns against Wu Ze, he had borrowed many of the Crown Prince’s military strategies and tactics.

But he regretted never having fought alongside the Crown Prince, and in his lifetime, he would probably never get to match skills with him.

However, among all the generals in the world, he alone feared the Crown Prince.

Ming Xi understood the implication in her elder brother’s words: as long as the Crown Prince was alive, no matter how much ambition he had, he would remain a general of the Great Zhou.

And it wasn’t just him, those fierce and battle-hardened generals on the border were the same.

On the battlefield, Crown Prince Xie Pei had been like the most dazzling meteor, brief but unforgettable, leaving behind an indelible legend.

Xie Pei looked up, his gaze falling on the girl’s figure. The cold and impatient expression on his face instantly froze.

He almost panicked as he stood up.

"Xixi, did it hit you?"

Xie Pei held her arm, not daring to use any force, looking at her with a mix of helplessness and concern.

The nearby Yu En had already knelt on the ground, feeling utterly miserable. If the Crown Princess misunderstood and thought His Highness had a bad temper, he might as well be dead.

Ming Xi snapped out of her daze and gave him a soft smile. "No, Your Highness, don’t worry."

Seeing that she wasn’t afraid of him, Xie Pei’s heart, which had been stuck in his throat, settled a little. He took her hand and led her to his main seat.

Ming Xi noticed the Crown Prince’s unease but didn’t say anything about etiquette or rules that might further unsettle his already fragile state of mind. She beckoned Ting Ruo to bring the food box.

She opened it and took out a white porcelain soup bowl. "The weather is especially cold today, so I thought I’d bring Your Highness a bowl of lamb soup to warm up."

Xie Pei took the soup bowl and placed it down, then enclosed her fair and soft little hand in his palm.

"You could have just sent a servant. Your body is weak; the cold wind isn’t good for you."

Ming Xi tilted her head and looked at him. "These days, everyone in the Eastern Palace says Your Highness favors Concubine Feng. I need to have some sense of crisis, so I thought I’d bring soup to compete for favor."

Xie Pei: ...

His Highness the Crown Prince suddenly felt like he was sitting on pins and needles. Even though he hadn’t actually done anything, he still felt guilty, sweat forming on his forehead.

"Xixi, I haven’t favored her. She is just..." a pawn to destroy the Feng family, that’s all.

chapters.title: Drinking Medicine
chapters.content:
Ming Xi burst into laughter, reaching out to wrap her arms around his waist and leaning into his embrace. She blinked playfully at him, "Your Highness didn't notice I was deliberately teasing you and getting jealous?"

Xie Pei: "..."

Looking at the girl in his arms, radiant with laughter, Xie Pei felt a warmth in his chest. He lowered his head and kissed her forehead, "Xier doesn’t need to be jealous."

Everything he had was hers.

"I know, Your Highness comes to see me every night. It's just that I like you, and when I hear them say you favor others, even if it's fake, I still get jealous."

Xie Pei's Adam's apple rolled, his soul completely captivated by her. Without any principles, he wanted to say, "Then I..." stop pretending, just kill her and be done with it.

In his heart, nothing was more important than her.

Ming Xi raised her hand to cover his mouth, her eyes sparkling like a serene lake, gentle and captivating, drawing one in effortlessly.

"Even though I have a bit of a temper, I'm also the most understanding. Your Highness can do whatever he wants; don't change your plans because of me."

Xie Pei took her hand, unable to resist pecking her red lips lightly. He didn’t deepen the kiss, afraid of startling the young girl.

The girl shyly lowered her gaze, her cheeks flushed, and gently pushed against his chest, "Your Highness, drink your soup before it gets cold."

The warm atmosphere in the palace was like spring, with subtle hints of affection lingering in the air. Eunuch Yu and Ting Yu had already withdrawn.

Only a fool would stay and ruin the mood.

Xie Pei cleared his throat and agreed.

Even though they had been intimate as husband and wife in the past, doing everything together, now that they were starting over, every time he got close to her, his ears would still burn, and his blood would boil.

"Your Highness, is it good?" Ming Xi tilted her head, watching him drink the soup.

Xie Pei scooped a spoonful and offered it to her. Ming Xi parted her lips to drink it, then seemingly accidentally brushed her lips against the spoon, successfully hearing his instantly heavy breathing.

She met his fiery gaze with a smile, "It's good."

Xie Pei: "..."

His Adam's apple slid up and down. He felt he couldn't drink this lamb soup anymore; he might get a nosebleed.

Xie Pei gently wiped the milky soup from the corner of her lips with his fingertip, his voice hoarse, "Xier, my life is truly in your hands."

Ming Xi pretended not to understand, pouting at him, "What nonsense is Your Highness talking about?"

Xie Pei, almost in a fluster, grabbed the cold tea on the table and drank it all in one go.

"This tea is already cold, why is Your Highness still drinking it?"

"..."

Cold was good. In fact, the Crown Prince would prefer something even colder.

Outside, the cold wind howled, but Xie Pei felt as if he were engulfed in flames.

But his beloved was still young; what could he do?

Endure!

Later, he would have the imperial physician prepare some cooling herbal medicine for himself.

Xie Pei struggled to find a topic to dispel the intimate atmosphere, "Xier, did you make this soup?"

"No, with my cooking skills, I wouldn’t want to commit regicide."

"..."

Xie Pei looked at her helplessly.

But he had grown accustomed to her directness.

In his past life, whether it was vying for favor or other matters, she had always been straightforward with him, saying whatever was on her mind.

At first, it always left Xie Pei at a loss, yet he couldn’t help but find it fresh and interesting. Unconsciously, he indulged her, and before he knew it, he had completely fallen for her.

Back then, Xie Pei, who had always been strict with rules and etiquette, had for the first time broken his principles for her. When favoring other concubines, he used a secret potion to make them hallucinate.

He was unwilling, even repulsed, to touch any woman other than her.

At that time, he thought he must have been bewitched.

If he was like this in his past life, then in this life, he would never even glance at another woman.

Ming Xi blinked at him innocently, "Your Highness, it's not that I don’t want to cook for you. The things I cook are bad in color, aroma, and taste, and on top of that, they’re poisonous."

Xie Pei couldn’t help but laugh. He gently rubbed her slender, fair fingers, not daring to recall how they had once been covered in scars and frostbite.

Suppressing the pain in his heart, he said softly, "Xier doesn’t need to go into the kitchen. Even I cannot let you work so hard."

This time, surrounded by gold and jade, luxury and splendor, he wanted her to always stay this bright and noble.

...

Under Ming Xi’s insistence, Xie Pei did not change his plans.

No one in the entire Eastern Palace knew that Ming Ce Fei had gone to the Crown Prince to vie for favor.

Just as Ming Xi had thought, the matters of the Eastern Palace were only known if the Crown Prince wanted them to be.

If he didn’t want it known, no matter how much he favored someone, it wouldn’t spread.

However, when it came to Ming Xi, Xie Pei was always meticulously cautious.

As long as he could protect her, Xie Pei would use any means necessary.

After staying in Wen Zhu Yuan for three consecutive nights, the "rule-abiding" Crown Prince went to the courtyards of the other noble consorts.

Shi Yuan didn’t expect that after the two Ce Fei, the "Crown Prince" would come to her courtyard first.

Separated by two lifetimes, Shi Yuan’s feelings for this future emperor were extremely complicated.

Resentment, unwillingness!

Clearly, she was the woman in the entire harem who loved him the most, yet he never gave her an extra glance.

Even after Ming Gui Fei had slapped her without reason, he had only casually said, "Nonsense," neither punishing her nor comforting Shi Yuan.

Obviously, Shi Yuan subconsciously ignored that it was she who had first been jealous of Ming Gui Fei for being the first to conceive a royal son. After her own miscarriage, she had pretended to offer comfort while actually saying things that stabbed at others' pain.

"Your servant greets Your Highness." Shi Yuan bowed her head, not daring to show any unusual expression.

"Rise." The "Crown Prince" walked past her directly into the bedroom.

Shi Yuan quickly stood up and followed to attend to him.

In her past life, she had also served the emperor, but for some reason, her memories were always vague.

At this moment, Shi Yuan couldn’t help but feel nervous and shy.

Sigh, why couldn’t she stop herself from falling in love with him?

But looking at the unparalleled handsome and noble Crown Prince before her, her heart couldn’t help but thump wildly.

The bed curtains swayed, and after the "Crown Prince" had finished, he got up and called for water.

Shi Yuan endured her discomfort, "Your Highness, let your servant attend to you."

"No need, you rest." The "Crown Prince" waved his hand and went to the washroom himself.

Shi Yuan saw that he didn’t even glance at her, and bit her lip.

What made Shi Yuan even more desperate was that the "Crown Prince" had someone bring a bowl of black medicine and ordered her to drink it.

She looked at him in disbelief, tears falling. "Your Highness, has your servant done something wrong?"

The "Crown Prince" looked at her expressionlessly, "No, it’s just that before the Ce Fei conceives, none of you can get pregnant."

Ce Fei was not the Crown Princess; what right did she have?

Shi Yuan almost couldn’t help but shriek in protest.

But facing the "Crown Prince’s" cold gaze, she swallowed her words and drank the medicine.

"Alright, you rest. I have other matters to attend to." Shi Yuan watched the "Crown Prince" leave indifferently, and couldn’t help but collapse onto the bed, crying her heart out.

How could he treat her like this?

How could he?

Ce Fei?

Was it Ming Xi or Feng Yuerong?

Shi Yuan recalled how the "Crown Prince" had recently shown favor and protection to Feng Yuerong.

Ah, in the last life, the winner of the initial selection was Feng Yuerong, who was directly promoted to concubine by the emperor.

It was just unexpected that on the night before entering the palace, Feng Yuerong would elope with Prince Qi.

There had been rumors that the emperor, knowing of Prince Qi and Feng Yuerong’s deep love, had tried to take her by force, but eventually had to let go because of their profound bond.

No wonder the "Crown Prince" had made such a big scene when favoring Feng Yuerong!

So, he truly loved Feng Yuerong!

Therefore, was he now planning to let Feng Yuerong give birth to the first royal grandson, so he could petition to make her the Crown Princess?

Preposterous!

Shi Yuan’s face twisted in hatred.

In the past life, Ming Xi couldn’t even become empress; how could Feng Yuerong in this life...

---

chapters.title: Pouring Oil on the Flames
chapters.content:
After the "Crown Prince" had stayed with Shi Yuan for three nights, he went to Dong Liang Yuan, then Qu Liang Yuan, and finally Zhao Liang Yuan.

The "Crown Prince" distributed his favors evenly, adhering strictly to the old ancestral rules and etiquette.

Even though he showed extraordinary favor to Concubine Feng, he had not lost his senses.

Both the palace and the court were quite satisfied with this.

A traditional, by-the-book future monarch was easier to control. If he were too unconventional, the officials would also be driven to despair.

Moreover, the Crown Prince was not an ordinary man; the imperial lineage was tied to the foundation of the nation, and he could not afford to be willful.

Thus, the public’s criticism was still directed at the Feng family.

Who had told them to produce a Concubine Feng who seduced the Crown Prince?

Especially the families of the four noble consorts, who wished they could brand Concubine Feng with the title of "a seductive concubine who brings disaster to the nation."

Lately, the Feng family had been in the limelight.

First, Concubine Feng was favored, and then there was Grand Tutor Feng’s 70th birthday.

The Crown Prince had specially sought the emperor’s permission to lift Concubine Feng’s confinement, personally taking her out of the palace to celebrate Grand Tutor Feng’s birthday.

The Crown Prince, busy with state affairs, left quickly, but allowed Concubine Feng to stay at home until the palace gates closed for the night.

On that day, the Feng family’s gate was bustling with carriages and horses, with nearly half of the capital’s nobles attending the birthday banquet, showcasing their immense prestige.

For a time, everyone privately discussed that once the Crown Prince ascended the throne, the Feng family would likely become the most prominent family in the capital.

The more glorious the Feng family became, the more people disapproved.

They were almost daily impeached by censors.

Even the emperor, who had great respect for Grand Tutor Feng, mentioned to the empress dowager with deep meaning, "Teacher and the Feng family have endured for many years; it seems they are finally going to soar to great heights because of Concubine Feng."

After all, having been part of the clean stream for so many years, many believed Grand Tutor Feng was a wise man who did not seek power. And now...

The Feng family’s painstakingly built reputation over the years was ruined in a day.

...

No matter how lively it was outside, it didn’t affect Ming Xi’s winter hibernation.

As the weather grew colder, she didn’t like going out unless necessary.

The room was heated with underfloor heating, and Ming Xi lazily nestled on the luohan bed covered with brocade cushions, tallying the Crown Prince’s... assets.

In the seventh month, the Crown Prince had gone south to relieve a famine. To cover up the mistakes of her pitiful brother, he had nearly emptied more than half of his wealth.

Fortunately, years ago, he had raided the Xirong royal city, emptying the treasuries of the Xirong royal family and many officials.

Over the years, the various industries under the Eastern Palace had also been well-managed, bringing in considerable income.

Otherwise, for the Jiangnan famine relief, the Crown Prince truly wouldn’t have been able to provide so much money.

Of course, whatever the Crown Prince had taken out before, he had later recovered manifold from his good second brother.

Then, the Eastern Palace became even wealthier.

Not long after she married in, the Crown Prince had presented her with the keys to his private vault, the Eastern Palace’s treasury, and all the account books.

At that time, Ming Xi had been a bit stunned.

Not to mention ancient nobles, even in modern times, in slightly wealthy families, men would never hand over all their assets to their wives.

But Xie Pei seemed to wish he could sign a contract selling himself to her.

Ming Xi didn’t understand.

But men in this world were untrustworthy, yet tangible gold and silver were another matter.

Ming Xi now somewhat believed that the Crown Prince genuinely liked her.

She didn’t know how long this liking and care would last.

Rather than dwelling on this question, it was better to take advantage of the time while he cherished her, to accumulate her own capital.

One day, when the passion faded, or even when they grew tired of each other, she would still be able to maintain her high position, with the ability and qualifications to stand on equal footing with him.

Don’t look at how the Crown Prince currently hadn’t let any concubine manage the inner court; in reality, the Eastern Palace’s roster had long been delivered to Ming Xi.

She could mobilize anyone in the Eastern Palace at any time and could start cultivating her own influence.

"I wonder if this makes me a behind-the-scenes Crown Princess?" Ming Xi had once teasingly remarked to the Crown Prince, actually probing his reaction.

Who would have thought that this sentence would completely move the Crown Prince, causing him to hold her tightly, full of guilt and apologies.

He said he was truly useless, unable to let her be the Crown Princess as she wished.

He even had to pretend to favor those messy women; his Xier was truly too wronged, too wronged.

Ming Xi: "..."

Actually, it wasn’t that wronged.

Moreover, she really didn’t care about the title of Crown Princess, nor did she particularly want to be it.

After all, there were still the emperor and empress above.

The political situation at court was unclear, and the factional struggles were intense. Ming Xi truly didn’t want to be a living target.

Just look at Concubine Feng; even a bit of false favor had turned the Feng family into a target of public criticism.

Ming Xi gave the Crown Prince a peck on the face, "It’s fine, it’s fine. Before we’re strong enough, let’s develop quietly. We’ll make a grand appearance later."

The Crown Prince, kissed into a rapid heartbeat, could only stupidly say, "Xier is right!"

...

"Your Highness, Concubine Feng pushed Shi Yuan into the lake."

Ting Yu entered to report.

"Hmm?" Ming Xi closed the account book, showing a hint of surprise, though she wasn’t particularly shocked.

The Eastern Palace’s inner court currently appeared calm.

However, invisible swordplay clashed every moment.

Concubine Feng was "favored," so Wen Zhu Yuan naturally held prestige.

They didn’t dare to provoke Qing Hua Yuan, as they knew Ting Yu would truly beat someone to death.

Ming Ce Fei had a high status and was protective; if she was provoked, and she wanted to severely punish someone, even Concubine Feng couldn’t stop her.

But the other four noble consorts, who hadn’t been bullied, who hadn’t been wronged?

In terms of clothing, food, housing, and transportation, wasn’t Wen Zhu Yuan always competing for the best?

Among them, the one with the most strained relationship with Concubine Feng was Shi Yuan.

Originally, when Shi Yuan had attended the Crown Prince, the fact that the "Crown Prince" hadn’t stayed overnight had made her the laughingstock of the entire Eastern Palace.

Concubine Feng had even visited her, acting with the demeanor of a mistress, setting various rules for her own good, which were actually all veiled insults.

This had directly made Shi Yuan cry.

When the matter reached the Crown Prince’s ears, not only did he not punish Concubine Feng for overstepping, but he also told Shi Yuan to stop bothering Concubine Feng.

This made Concubine Feng even more arrogant.

Shi Yuan could only endure her anger in silence.

However, Concubine Feng, no matter how arrogant, wouldn’t have the audacity to kill a noble consort of the Eastern Palace.

In these palace intrigue scenarios, if it wasn’t entirely self-directed, at least eight out of ten times it was self-staged.

Ming Xi didn’t expose this. She only asked, "Is Shi Yuan alright? Does the Crown Prince know about this?"

"Shi Yuan was rescued in time, and the imperial physician has already been called. No one would dare hide such a matter from His Highness the Crown Prince. I imagine he has already gone to Shi Yuan’s place by now."

Ming Xi nodded, taking Ting Yu’s hand to stand up and put on her fox fur coat, holding a hand warmer, before heading to Shi Yuan’s residence.

chapters.title: No Way to Defend Oneself
chapters.content:
The Longxia Courtyard was in chaos at the moment.

In the main hall, the Crown Prince, dressed in a dark robe, sat at the head of the table. Concubine Feng knelt before him, weeping bitterly as she protested her innocence in pushing Consort Shi Liang into the water.

Xie Pei immediately noticed Ming Xi’s arrival. He pressed his lips together, struggling to maintain the facade of anger on his face.

Ming Xi secretly winked at him, as if to say: *Your Highness, stay calm, don’t give us away!*

Xie Pei’s heart melted at her wink, and he suppressed the flutter in his chest.

No one noticed the silent exchange between the two.

Ming Xi took graceful steps forward and greeted the Crown Prince, “This concubine pays her respects to Your Highness.”

“Mm, take a seat.”

Xie Pei straightened his posture slightly, resisting the urge to personally help her up.

As Ming Xi approached the armchair beside him, Listen, her maid, seemingly out of nowhere, produced a soft cushion and placed it on the chair.

The palace servants from Wen Zhu Yuan and Long Xia Yuan stared in surprise.

Concubine Ming was truly particular, even His Highness the Crown Prince didn’t have a cushion, yet she dared to sit so boldly.

Did she not fear the Crown Prince’s displeasure?

Well, Concubine Ming was the eldest legitimate daughter of the Wu Ding Marquis, and her father and brothers were all accomplished. With such a background, she had no need to fear losing favor in the Eastern Palace.

Moreover, Concubine Ming was breathtakingly beautiful, with a graceful figure, no less than a celestial being descended to earth.

Even if such a beauty acted improperly, she remained endearing. Who could bear to blame her?

When Ming Xi appeared, Concubine Feng bit her lip tightly.

No matter how much she denied it, she couldn’t stop the fact that the moment Ming Xi entered, the room was filled with radiance, reducing everyone else to mere foils, dim and overshadowed.

Ming Xi ignored Concubine Feng’s jealous glare.

There were plenty in the capital who envied her, one more like Feng made no difference.

Ming Xi turned to the Crown Prince. “Your Highness, this concubine heard that Consort Shi fell into the water. How is she now?”

“She was shocked into fainting. The imperial physicians are currently treating her with acupuncture.”

Xie Pei’s tone was indifferent, giving no hint of whether he cared about the matter.

Concubine Feng bit her lip until it bled, her pleading eyes fixed on the Crown Prince. “Your Highness, this concubine truly did not push Consort Shi!”

“Does Your Highness not know what kind of person this concubine is? How could I be so vicious as to harm someone?”

“Moreover, as a concubine, why would I trouble myself to harm a mere consort? There is no enmity between Consort Shi and me!”

Before Concubine Feng could finish, Consort Shi’s personal maid crawled forward on her knees, her face streaked with tears as she sobbed, “Your Highness, please seek justice for my mistress, Consort Shi!”

“Concubine Feng claims to have no feud with my mistress, so why has she allowed the servants of Wen Zhu Yuan to bully my mistress all this time?”

“First, she hinted to the kitchen to serve my mistress cold and spoiled food. Then, she ordered people to tear up my mistress’s clothes… Not a single servant from Long Xia Yuan has escaped the insults and beatings from the people of Wen Zhu Yuan!”

As she spoke, the maid rolled up her sleeve, revealing arms covered in bruises.

Concubine Feng snapped, “How dare you! A mere servant accuses this concubine so recklessly!”

“Your Highness, I did not! I truly did not!”

Xie Pei’s expression remained blank, but his eyes were cold, as if deeply disappointed in Concubine Feng.

The Crown Prince “valued rules above all else” and could not tolerate servants overstepping their masters. Previously, he had nearly lost favor with Concubine Feng because her maid had offended Concubine Ming.

“What did you promise me before?” he asked coldly.

Concubine Feng’s face paled. “Your Highness, these matters truly have nothing to do with this concubine. Please, believe me…”

Ming Xi, who was watching the drama unfold with great interest, covered her mouth and chimed in, “They say the Feng family’s daughters are virtuous and kind. How is it that Concubine Feng repeatedly allows her people to commit such outrageous acts?”

“If Your Highness were to entrust Concubine Feng with managing the Eastern Palace, the other concubines and consorts would have no chance of survival. The Eastern Palace would become a laughingstock to the world.”

Xie Pei barely resisted the urge to say, *“Xi’er is right.”*

But before he could speak, Concubine Feng glared at Ming Xi with hatred. “Concubine Ming, why must you kick me while I’m down and slander me so?”

Ming Xi feigned innocence. “These days, every single thing done by Wen Zhu Yuan has caused unrest in the Eastern Palace. Do I need to slander her for that?”

“You…”

Unable to retort, Concubine Feng could only turn to the Crown Prince, her eyes filled with love and suffering. “Your Highness, this concubine has no way to defend herself!”

Ming Xi almost laughed out loud.

This Concubine Feng was truly a *remarkable* person!

Xie Pei was thoroughly disgusted by Concubine Feng’s act. He pretended to consider for a moment before asking Ming Xi, “Beloved, should this matter be left to…”

“Your Highness has seen for yourself how much Concubine Feng resents this concubine. If I were to investigate, she would surely refuse to accept it. She might even frame me for harming her. This concubine cannot bear such a responsibility.”

Ming Xi adopted the spoiled demeanor of a petty woman, completely unafraid of losing favor by contradicting the Crown Prince.

After all, her family background was unassailable!

Xie Pei rubbed his temples in feigned exasperation. “Forget it. Yu En, you will investigate. The matter of Consort Shi falling into the water, as well as Wen Zhu Yuan’s bullying of the other consorts, look into it all and get to the bottom of it.”

“As for Feng, before the truth is uncovered, you are to stay in Wen Zhu Yuan and not step outside.”

Concubine Feng’s tears welled up, her expression filled with grievance, as if to say, *I love the Crown Prince so much, how can Your Highness not believe me?*

Even Ming Xi was left speechless.

This Concubine Feng’s condition seemed even more severe than her mother, Lady Wen’s!

After being given medicine, Consort Shi woke up.

Upon seeing the Crown Prince, she did not lodge a complaint but only wept bitterly.

Unfortunately, the Crown Prince’s heart was as hard as iron, he showed not the slightest pity. He merely rewarded her with some trivial gifts, indifferently ordered someone to attend to her, and then waved his hand to dismiss her.

Consort Shi bit her lip, tears falling like rain. She was truly miserable now.

She didn’t understand, where had she fallen short? Why was the Crown Prince so heartless toward her time and time again?

Ming Xi also wanted to leave, but out of courtesy, she had to at least pretend to offer some comfort.

“Consort Shi, take care of your health and don’t think too much. If you need anything, send someone to inform His Highness. He won’t let you suffer.”

Consort Shi was taken aback by Ming Xi’s words.

Normally, shouldn’t she have said, *“If you need anything, come to me”*?

She had been hoping for that.

But Ming Xi would never take on such trouble for herself.

Consort Shi and Concubine Feng were locked in a bitter struggle, why should Ming Xi spend her money and effort on her?

Was she a fool?

As for forming alliances, Ming Xi didn’t need that for the time being.

Moreover, this Consort Shi didn’t seem like an easy person to deal with. She was ungrateful, and who knew, she might even turn around and bite the hand that fed her.

Seeing that Ming Xi was about to leave, Consort Shi couldn’t help but call out, “Concubine!”

Ming Xi turned slightly to look at her. “Does Consort Shi have something else to say?”

---

chapters.title: Xi’er Loves Me
chapters.content:
“Are you willing to accept this, Your Highness?”

“Hm?”

“If not for Concubine Feng, you would be the most honored in the Eastern Palace, and the Crown Prince’s most favored. Now, all the attention is on Concubine Feng… Don’t you feel wronged?”

Consort Shi fixed her gaze on Ming Xi, her words deliberate, as if casting a spell.

She refused to believe that Ming Gui Fei, who had dominated the emperor’s affections in her past life, would now willingly submit to someone as foolish as Concubine Feng.

If Ming Xi made a move, how could Feng Yuerong possibly survive?

Then, with a little push from her, the Crown Prince would see Ming Xi’s true, vicious nature…

Once Feng Yuerong was dead and Ming Xi lost favor, she didn’t believe the Crown Prince would still overlook her.

Ming Xi smiled, her beauty dazzling, but it made Consort Shi’s heart clench.

In her past life, whenever Ming Gui Fei smiled like that, someone was bound to suffer greatly.

Slapping concubines, throwing people into the imperial prison to face torture, what hadn’t she done? What didn’t she dare to do?

Even when Emperor Jian Wu was later overthrown, with Ming Jing and hundreds of thousands of Tian Ding Army soldiers as her backing, Prince Qi didn’t dare to do anything to her beyond confining her and the emperor.

She was the kind of person who inspired jealousy to the bone.

Suddenly, Ming Xi reached out and pinched Consort Shi’s chin. “Consort Shi, are you trying to use me as a pawn?”

“I; I…”

“Was jumping into the icy lake fun? Should I have someone throw you back in to clear your mind, hmm?”

Consort Shi’s face paled. “This concubine… this concubine doesn’t understand what Your Highness is saying!”

“How you scheme against Concubine Feng, how you fight with her; I don’t care. But if you dare to extend your claws toward me, don’t blame me for chopping them off!”

Ming Xi let go of Consort Shi, took the handkerchief handed to her by Ting Yu, wiped her hands, and casually tossed it onto Consort Shi’s face before gracefully leaving with Ting Ruo’s support.

Consort Shi trembled all over, consumed by fear and humiliation.

*Shameless! Every single one of them is shameless!*

She would make sure they all died without a proper burial!

…

As night fell, the Crown Prince, as expected, emerged from the secret passage to meet his beloved concubine in private.

Lately, he had been arriving earlier each day, even bringing official documents and state affairs with him.

The desk by the window in the bedchamber was for his use.

It was a dowry desk Ming Xi had brought from home, and it had nearly delighted His Highness to the point of losing his senses.

If Xi’er was willing to let him use her dowry, she must love him deeply and truly consider him her husband.

After winter set in, the Empress Dowager’s health had been declining.

The Emperor was so worried that he couldn’t eat or sleep. Apart from attending court, he spent all his free time at the Empress Dowager’s bedside.

As a result, most of the court affairs had fallen onto the Crown Prince’s shoulders.

These days, he often worked late into the night, reviewing memorials.

Being an emperor was no easy task, and being a worthy ruler was even harder.
